properties.name: Pfister Brewery Inn GmbH
properties.description:
## Bio and Beer

### Obernsees Spa, Feuerstein Flight School, Franconian Switzerland, Young Theater Forchheim, Bamberg, Forchheim, Levi Strauss Museum Buttenheim, Liasgube Environmental Station.

The beers that come from the Pfister brewery are made exclusively from organically grown brewing ingredients, which is underscored by the Bioland seal. That does nothing to diminish the taste, quite the opposite: both the organic country beer and the organic black cellar beer are extremely easy to drink. At Christmas, Stefan Pfister also treats beer lovers to a fine Bioland bock beer as the “organic Christ Child.” The tavern history in Weigelshofen began in 1612. Stefan Pfister’s ancestor Johann then got his start in the brewery in 1848 and founded the family tradition. While revolutionary turmoil raged elsewhere in the country, people in Weigelshofen focused on the essentials: good beer. And good food, for example blue carp and trout in the months with an “r” in their name. Roast fans get their money’s worth every Sunday at lunchtime. On special occasions, beer sommelier Stefan Pfister also invites guests to his “Brau. Gasthof. Land. Quartier.” for delicious beer-based culinary creations featuring many beer specialties from around the world.

properties.name: Neunkirchen am Brand
properties.description: Our staff will be happy to help you with any questions about your holiday, finding accommodation, or planning leisure activities.

properties.name: Pumptrack Anlage Gunzenhausen
properties.description:
In mid-November 2019, the Gunzenhausen pump track facility opened. With this facility, a real highlight has been created in Gunzenhausen for all bikers, BMX riders, and skateboarders.

When the facility was being built, care was taken to ensure that both beginners and professionals could ride their laps.

Designed as a continuous loop, with a specially created asphalt track, the aim is to actively ride a pump track with its waves, curves, and jumps through dynamic up-and-down movements (“pumping”) and generate speed without pedaling or pushing off. Across generations, cyclists, skateboarders, scooter riders, inline skaters, and even wheelchair users can give free rein to their urge to move on the landscaped terrain, regardless of skill, riding style, or age.

properties.name: Hebendanz Brewery
properties.description:
## Wer probt, der lobt

### Forchheim ist wegen seiner großen Zahl von historischen Gebäuden, Plätzen, Denkmälern und anderen Sehenswürdigkeiten ein beliebtes Ziel für Besucher aus nah und fern. Außerdem ist Forchheim ein hervorragender Ausgangspunkt für Ausflüge in die nahe gelegene "Fränkische Schweiz" oder in andere Gebiete des reizvollen Umlandes der Stadt.

So klingt der in heutiger Zeit etwas holprige Wahlspruch der zweitältesten Brauerei Forchheims, die aber gerade wegen ihrer Ecken und Kanten eine der liebenswertesten ist. Mit Martina Hebendanz steht bereits die Tochter von Fritz Hebendanz mit am Sudkessel und sorgt dafür, dass die bald 500-jährige Familientradition fortgesetzt wird. Logisch, dass das Bier auch auf dem Annafest, Forchheims fünfter Jahreszeit Ende Juli, ausgeschenkt wird. Mit der Brauerei-Gaststätte Hebendanz mitten in Forchheim hat sich im Gegensatz zum Kellerwald-Trubel eine wahre Oase der Ruhe etabliert. Hier kommen die Forchheimer gerne auf ein oder zwei gemütliche Bierchen, den kleinen Plausch am Rande oder die Schafkopfrunde zusammen. Eine deftige gute Küche versteht sich fast von selbst. Wer aber doch auf den bekannten Forchheimer Kellerberg pilgern will (was wir sehr gut verstehen können), kann entweder zum besagten Annafest oder den ganzen Sommer über auf den Schlößla- oder den Hebendanz-Keller kommen und muss auch hier nicht auf das urige Forchheimer Bier verzichten.

properties.name: Fürth Market
properties.description:
## The place to stroll and snack

The Fürth Market in the heart of the city attracts locals and visitors from across the region with its modern stalls and stands. The selection offers a colorful variety of regional produce, fresh specialties, and handmade treats. Around the food stalls, tables and chairs invite you to enjoy the special atmosphere. Plenty of space for eating, drinking, lingering, and socializing. From shashlik, falafel, and Asian food to cold drinks, freshly roasted coffee, creative cakes, vegan snacks, and tasty beer, the selection is wide and delicious.

properties.name: Crime Museum
properties.description:
## Polizeiarbeit und Kriminalfälle - damals und heute

In dem kleinen privat geführten Museum in den Kellerräumen des Rathauses werden die Geschichte der Fürther Polizei und Gerichtsbarkeit seit 1806 sowie spektakuläre Kriminalfälle aus den letzten 200 Jahren präsentiert.  

Besucher:innen erhalten Einblicke in aktuelle Themen der Polizeiarbeit, wie Drogenkriminalität, Geldfälschung oder Waffendelikte. Ein nachgestellter Tatort veranschaulicht exemplarisch die Ermittlungsarbeit der Kriminalpolizei in den Bereichen Spurensuche und Kriminaltechnik. Auch das Thema Rechtsmedizin wird anschaulich präsentiert.  

Das Museum beleuchtet das Thema Kriminalität in Vergangenheit und Gegenwart und zeigt mit einem Augenzwinkern, dass Verbrechen sich nicht lohnen – weder für Opfer noch für Täter.  

Gelegentlich finden im Museum auch Lesungen statt.

properties.name: Kaiser Brewery
properties.description:
## Das Bier der Brückenheiligen

### 7 Brückenheilige von Grasmannsdorf.

Insgesamt sieben Heilige wachen über Grasmannsdorf und seine alte Ebrachbrücke: Nikolaus, Nepomuk, Kilian, Vitus, Wolfgang, Heinrich und Otto. Seit 1783 steht ihnen mit der ehemaligen Schlossbrauerei auch noch guter Gerstensaft zur Seite, heute heißt sie Brauerei Kaiser. Der Klassiker im Hause ist das Pils, ergänzt durch ein spritziges Weizen im Sommer, sowie ein malzbetontes Festbier und einen hellen Bock zur Weihnachtszeit. Letzterer hat mit 17,5 Prozent Stammwürze und 7,5 Prozent Alkoholgehalt nach seiner achtwöchigen Lagerung Einiges zu bieten. Die ca. 250 Einwohner versammeln sich mehr oder weniger vollständig nach der Kirche bei Georg Kaiser und seiner Familie im Brauerei-Gasthof – so wie sie es gefühlt schon immer getan haben. Der Renner ist dabei die halbe Ente (warme Gerichte müssen vorbestellt werden). Im Sommer lädt zudem auch der Biergarten zum regelmäßigen Besuch – das Essen darf gerne mitgebracht werden. Allerdings gibt es sehr gute Brotzeiten aus eigener Herstellung, ab und an sogar Schlachtschüssel. Außerdem sollten Sie sich den vorletzten Sonntag im August vormerken: da ist Kerwa angesagt …

properties.name: Kulturforum Fürth
properties.description:
## From Historic Slaughterhouse to Modern Cultural Hotspot

Idyllically located on the banks of the Rednitz River not far from Fürth's old town, the **Kulturforum Fürth** is one of the region's most distinctive and versatile cultural centers. On the grounds of the former, listed slaughterhouse from the Gründerzeit period (built 1878–81), a lively production and event venue was created in 2004. Here, historic sandstone architecture meets state-of-the-art technology, giving the place its unique atmosphere.

Under the direction of Melina Hüttner, the house, supported by the Cultural Office of the City of Fürth, offers a wide-ranging program that spans tradition to experimentation and regional highlights to international guest performances.

## Program Variety, Festivals & Collaborations

The Kulturforum is known for its cross-disciplinary art projects and high-profile focuses. The current [**program**](https://www.kulturforum.fuerth.de/desktopdefault.aspx/tabid-1094/) can be viewed here.

- **Concerts & Theater:** High-quality live music ranging from jazz and classical to pop is on the agenda here, as are innovative in-house productions and guest performances of children's theater.

- **Festivals:** The venue hosts the city's major festivals, including [**Jewish Music Today Fürth**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/veranstaltungen/festivals/jewish-music-today/) (Europe's largest Klezmer festival), the [**international figuren.theater.festival**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/veranstaltungen/kunst-kultur/internationales-figurentheaterfestival/) and Fürth's literature festival [**Lesen!**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/veranstaltungen/kunst-kultur/lesen/).

- **Stadttheater Fürth:** Since its opening, the Kulturforum has served as the permanent venue of the [**Stadttheater Fürth**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/poi/stadttheater-100036896/) for modern and unusual formats in the fields of drama and dance theater. The KULT ensemble for children's and youth theater, the youth clubs, and community theater projects (such as "Brückenbau") also regularly use the halls as a stage.

**Tickets & Advance Sales:** Admission tickets for all Kulturforum events are available directly through the [**Reservix online ticket system**](https://kulturforum-fuerth.reservix.de/events) as well as at the usual advance ticket outlets.  

**Tip:** Anyone wanting a look behind the scenes can take part in the exciting guided tour *"*[**From Slaughterhouse to Temple of Culture**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/stadtspaziergaenge/verfuehrt-hinter-die-kulissen/vom-schlachthof-zum-kulturtempel/)*"*.

## Cinema & Dining Under One Roof

- **[Uferpalast Art House Cinema](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/poi/kino-uferpalast/):** Film enthusiasts will find an ambitious, independent cinema program here under the roof of the Kulturforum. Screenings include documentaries, gems of independent cinema from around the world (mostly in the original version with subtitles), as well as film classics. Blockbusters are nowhere to be found here.

- **Restaurant [La Scala](https://www.lascala-fuerth.de/):** A visit to the cultural venue can also be rounded off culinarily on site. The in-house restaurant serves Mediterranean delicacies and invites guests to linger on the terrace directly on the Rednitz River in summer.

## Rentals

The Kulturforum also offers an [**exceptional setting for your own events**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/planen-buchen/tagen-feiern/kulturforum/). All rooms as well as the foyer and inner courtyard can be rented. The venue's scheduling service is available for coordination and support with planning.

properties.name: Kulturzentrum Ostpreußen im Schloss Ellingen
properties.description:
In addition to the permanent exhibition and museum education programs in Ellingen, the cultural center’s repertoire also includes bilingual permanent exhibitions and special exhibitions in the Lithuanian and Polish parts of East Prussia today. For example, the exhibition “The Lords and Counts von der Groeben – an East Prussian noble family” can currently be seen in Rastenburg/*Kętrzyn*. Permanent exhibitions on the history of the town can also be visited in various Polish museums (including Lyck/Elk, Rastenburg/*Kętrzyn*, Lötzen/Giżycko, Allenstein/Olsztyn).

The cultural center is also an exciting destination for families. Regular ArtClubs (once a month) invite children aged 6 and up, under the guidance of the museum educator, to explore various topics in and around East Prussia. At the most recent ArtClub in February – passend to the special exhibition – the topic of “Flight and Expulsion” was explored using an original escape suitcase together with documents from 1945. The children considered what they would pack today in the event of a hurried escape and told each other stories of classmates’ escapes – and after two hours this resulted in a very impressive installation of various suitcases and their contents. All artworks created as part of the ArtClub can be viewed in the rooms of the cultural center.

In autumn 2026, the Kulturzentrum Ostpreußen in Ellingen will present two new special exhibitions.

From 5 September 2026 until November 2026, the poster exhibition **“Poland Laughs at This. A Country Study in Cartoons and Texts”** invites visitors to take a humorous look at Poland. The pointed cartoons by the well-known Polish artist **Andrzej Mleczko** are complemented by texts by Poland expert and publicist **Matthias Kneip**. Together, they offer surprising insights into the history, society, and mentality of the neighboring country.

From **10 October 2026**, **“Woodcuts. Memories of East Prussia. Eduard Bischoff”** will focus on an important East Prussian artist. The exhibition shows a comprehensive selection from Bischoff’s woodcut series “East Prussia,” created between 1952 and 1960. His expressive and increasingly abstract works reflect the artist’s deep connection to his lost homeland. The exhibition can be visited until 09 January 2027.

Both exhibitions open up different perspectives on culture and history and invite visitors to discover familiar themes in new and special ways.

School holidays are not neglected either – whether Easter, Pentecost, summer, or autumn holidays. The cultural center has suitable programs for every holiday period. Children become little jewelry designers or discover fossil insects.

In addition to the children’s programs, once a month (on the last Wednesday of each month) a group of steadfast hobby knitters meets in the conference room of the cultural center to indulge in their shared hobby – East Prussian double knitting. From 1 p.m. to 5 p.m., they knit new creations here, alongside coffee and cake. What is special about double knitting: by working two strands at the same time, a dense, double-layered fabric with mirrored patterns on both sides is created. The technique was used especially for particularly warm and durable gloves and socks and is now considered a valuable textile cultural heritage that is increasingly being rediscovered. New interested participants are always warmly welcome. All they need is the right equipment: circular knitting needles size 2.5 (40 cm), 2 balls of wool in different colors, and a knitting thimble. Admission is free; donations are very welcome.

The cultural center also hosts a crafts and arts market twice a year. The Easter market offers both artists and culinary exhibitors the opportunity to present themselves and generally takes place on a Sunday around Easter. The autumn market regularly takes place over 2 days in November. This year, the autumn market will take place from 21–22 November 2026. Further information can be found on the website [www.kulturzentrum-ostpreussen.de](http://www.kulturzentrum-ostpreussen.de).

All further information on the holiday programs, workshops, and events can be found on the cultural center’s homepage ([www.kulturzentrum-ostpreussen.de](http://www.kulturzentrum-ostpreussen.de)) and on social media (Instagram, Facebook, Franken Radar, Altmühlfranken entdecken, Ellingen APP), as well as in your daily and weekly newspaper.

The Kulturzentrum Ostpreußen is open daily from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. and from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. The museum is closed on Mondays.

properties.name: Mager Brewery Inn
properties.description:
## With the horse-drawn cart in the logo

### Pottenstein Adventure Mile, Wild Romantic Castles, Caves, Rock Pool, Toboggan Run, Juramar Baths, Golf, Guided Tours, Mini Golf, Boating.

Back when natural ice was still used in the brewery, the beer had to be transported after the brewing process to the rock cellar about 800 meters away. This was done by a horse-drawn team with a barrel cart, which then brought the finished beer back for bottling a few weeks later. This scene delighted father Georg Mager and son Andreas so much that they included it in the official brewery logo. Today, the brewery produces four easy-drinking beers and, seasonally, various festival and strong beers, but the horse-drawn team is long gone. Not so the roulade. The supposedly dead live longer, as the supposed farewell to roulade as a Franconian roast roll had already begun twenty years ago, yet the beef roll has since worked its way back into gourmet kitchens. Here in Pottenstein, you can get the original Franconian roulade, for which guests travel from far and wide, and of course enjoy the brewery's good beer with it. We especially like the hop-bitter "Schl5cggla" and, of course, the "Pottensteiner Red Beer."

properties.name: Brauerei Gasthof Schwan
properties.description:
## Bamberg Old-Timer

The history of the Schwan brewery inn dates back to 1394, perhaps even earlier. This makes the house one of the oldest in the Bamberg district. The history comes alive every October during the church fair, when the Lechner family serves the traditional “Kerwasbier.” In summer, you should not shy away from the walk to Burgebrach Kellerberg, where the brewery’s beer cellar, the Schwanenkeller, is located. Fish is one of the specialties at the “Schwanawirt”; a particularly popular dish is carp in beer batter (in the months with an “r” in their name), but the sausages are also always worth a visit — both at the inn and at the Schwanenkeller. Legendary in November is the St. Martin’s goose dinner, when the roasted bird is carved at the table before the guests’ eyes. However, due to the weather, this takes place only at the inn. Note: by the way, it is always closed when the cellar is open.

properties.name: Stern-Bräu, Scheubel
properties.description:
## Moved to the Open-Air Museum

### Pommersfelden Palace, Schlüsselfeld Old Town, Freizeitland Geiselwind.

Beer has been brewed by the Scheubel family since 1828. For this purpose, the communal brewhouse built in 1737 was used. Today, this building, with its historic brew kettle from 1850, stands in the Bad Windsheim Open-Air Museum and is thus available to the public. At Brauhaus Scheubel, the old traditions are still preserved and combined with modern brewing technology of today. Günter Scheubel will be happy to introduce you to the history of the house on one of the brewery tours. By prior arrangement, groups can learn everything worth knowing about beer. In the associated inn, you can enjoy the full breadth of Franconian culinary art. In summer, the Scheubel Cellar also beckons, a true idyll on the edge of town. You sit under old trees with a cool beer and a good snack. The little ones have fun romping around on the playground.

properties.name: Kehl Fruit Teaching Garden - Variety with every tree
properties.description:
Apfel = Apfel Dass diese Gleichung nicht so leicht aufgeht, ist vielen Menschen bekannt. Doch wie groß die Sorten- und damit die Geschmacksvielfalt im Streuobst ist, wissen nur die wenigsten: Mehrere tausend Apfel-, Birnen-, Pflaumen- und Kirschsorten sind bekannt. Der Obstlehrgarten Kehl zeigt diese Vielfalt im kleinen Maßstab, insgesamt haben über 65 Sorten hier ihre Heimat gefunden. Neben Klassikern wie dem Rheinischen Bohnapfel finden sich auch Besonderheiten wie der Weiße Winterglockenapfel. Bei einem Spaziergang durch die herrliche Streuobstwiese kann man wunderbar die Seele baumeln, und die Vielfalt und Schönheit der Natur auf sich wirken lassen. Zwei Stationen geben Auskunft zu Obstbau, Biodiversität und Sortenreichtum.

Der Natur zuliebe - auch im Obstlehrgarten:

- Keine Blumen oder Sträucher ausreißen.
- Abfall bitte wieder mitnehmen und ordnungsgemäß entsorgen.
- Hunde an die Leine nehmen.

properties.name: Weißenburg Pump Track Facility
properties.description:
The wave track was built by the specialist company Radquartier and was subsidized, among other things, with LEADER funding. The location of the pump track was deliberately chosen next to Aumühlweiher and is also intended to serve as a starting point for tours in the surrounding area.

A pump track is a closed circuit with waves, banked turns, and jumps. The term pump track comes from English and uses the word "pump" to describe the loading and unloading of the sports equipment while riding over the waves, and the word "track" to describe the course on which one rides.

By deliberately loading and unloading — the so-called "pumping" — enough speed is generated to ride around the track without additional pedaling or pushing. This activity is a lot of fun, but it also requires physical effort and endurance, making it a perfect sports and fitness program. And that is exactly the goal: to create a leisure activity for children, young people, and adults alike, and thus rekindle enthusiasm for fun, sport, and exercise in the fresh air.

**Pump tracks are for everyone!**

Suitable for ages 2 to 85. From mountain bikes, BMX bikes, skateboards, inline skates, scooters, and longboards to balance bikes — even wheelchairs can use this pump track. Designed for beginners and advanced riders, all the way up to Olympic athletes.

properties.name: Zirndorf Brewery
properties.description:
## Authentic and easy-drinking

The Zirndorf Brewery now stands for more than 335 years of brewing tradition. Back then, Margrave Johann Friedrich of Ansbach was delighted with the products of his "brewmasters," whose strict requirements ensured that the beer, thanks to its high quality, quickly became known and popular throughout the surrounding area. The good Zirndorfer today comes in three varieties: Landbier, amber-colored and finely hopped; Kellerbier, unfiltered and full-bodied; and Landweizen, refreshing and flavorful. Selected raw ingredients are used, from hops from the Hallertau and Spalt to barley from controlled cultivation.

properties.name: Naturerlebnisraum Bibertinsel in Zirndorf

properties.name: Islandpferdehof Hesthólar
properties.description:
If you want to experience the beautiful area around Weißenburg from a different perspective and are enthusiastic about Icelandic horses, you've come to the right place!
The Hesthólar Icelandic Horse Farm is located in a secluded setting on the outskirts of Weißenburg below Wülzburg, with a wonderful view into the valley. With 2.5 hectares of meadows, a riding arena, a small indoor riding hall, and wonderful riding terrain, the farm offers ideal conditions for keeping and training horses as well as for running single-day and multi-day programs. The farm is home to eleven of its own Icelandic horses, kept in a loose housing stable with a spacious sand paddock and directly adjoining pastures.

We run our horse farm with a holistic educational approach (experiential education, environmental education, and riding education). Our special focus is on natural interaction with the horse as a living being, and on working with or riding the horse in a trusting, safe, and relaxed way. The people who come to us should get to know and appreciate the horse as a friend and partner, not see it as a piece of sports equipment.

We offer educational programs with horses for children, young people, adults, and people with disabilities:

- Therapeutic riding
- Early childhood riding education
- Educational riding lessons
- Guided walking rides
- Half-day and full-day programs as well as multi-day holiday camps on various themes (e.g. Native Americans, Romans, Celts, nature experiences, etc.)
- Horse trekking
- Children's birthday parties

Have we sparked your interest? Then we look forward to welcoming you to our farm!

properties.name: Kraus Brewery Inn GmbH & Co. KG
properties.description:
## Big-screen entertainment in Hirschaid


### Bamberg, Franconian Switzerland.


By 1845, Hirschaid had managed to secure access to the most important transport routes by water and land with a landing place and a modest railway station. At that time, the town had around 700 inhabitants and no fewer than eight inns—the highest number in a rural municipality in the Bamberg hinterland. One of them was the “Kramer´sche Wirtschaftsguth,” taken over that year by Johannes Kraus, the miller’s son from Eggolsheim—among other things with a brewery. Since then, the brewery inn has been continuously owned by the Kraus family and is in many respects one of the industry’s flagship establishments. Today, Stefanie Missner and Hilde Kraus are ever-present managers and respected members of the community. They organize charity events and are always available to the people of Hirschaid. Since 2006, the beer has even been available in swing-top bottles, the Krausenbügel. Recommended are the “Hirschentrunk” and, for those eager to experiment, the “Lapland Saunabier.”

properties.name: Kayak Tours at Leinen Los
properties.description:
**Mit dem Kajak durch die Fränkische Schweiz (Von Behringersmühle nach Streitberg) :**

Die Strecke vom Bahnhof Behringersmühle bis nach Streitberg ist auf ihren 12,9 km wunderbar abwechslungsreich. Ruhige, gemütliche Flussabschnitte wechseln sich hier mit faszinierenden Uferblicken und spritzigen Stromschnellen ab. Die Klassiker Tour verspricht Paddelspaß pur und bietet genügend Zeit, Einkehrmöglichkeiten in Muggendorf zu nutzen.

Das Mindestalter bei Kindern beträgt 8 Jahre.  
Voraussetzung für das Kajakfahren mit Kindern ist, dass eine Erwachsene Begleitperson mit teilnimmt und die Kinder Schwimmen können.


Und wer nach einer Kajaktour noch Lust auf mehr Action hat, kann den Tag perfekt erweitern: Probiert euch beim [Discgolf](https://leinen-los.de/discgolf/) aus oder zeigt beim [Bogenschießen](https://sehnensucht.de/) euer Können! 

So wird aus einer Kajaktour ein abwechslungsreicher Tag voller Bewegung, Natur und Spaß, ideal für Familien, Freunde, Gruppen und alle, die gerne draußen aktiv sind.

properties.name: Sauer Brewery
properties.description:
## More than 200 years of tradition and experience

### Bamberg, Franconian Switzerland, Hauptsmoor Forest.

That is the motto of Christian Sauer, who today runs the brewery founded in 1784 eight kilometers south of Bamberg. It has now been six generations who have stood and still stand here behind the brew kettle and lauter tun. The high quality of the beer and food is confirmed by Feinschmecker magazine’s award as a “particularly recommended tip for connoisseurs.”

In summer, it is also worth making the trip to the rustic outpost, the brewery’s former rock cellar.

With its tunnels hewn far into the mountain, where until not too long ago beer was still stored in old oak barrels, it is a very special place, especially since the old trees also create a very special atmosphere.

Guests there are especially pleased with the house-brewed beer.

For those of you who are hungry, the pork chops and the Friday fish variations are particularly worth mentioning.

If you like hearty fare, the brewer’s tarte flambée, for example, is an excellent choice.

Add a “Roßdorfer Brown Beer” with its light caramel malt note and you will be in seventh beer heaven.

Guaranteed!

properties.description: Located directly on the Zenn, a leisure zone stretches out that has something for every taste. The elements of exercise and relaxation are cleverly combined. Over approx. 200 meters, various areas line up one after another: from the exercise course to a relaxation zone and the beer garden, there is something for everyone. An e-bike charging station can also be found in the beer garden. The adventure playground and the toddler playground, a labyrinth, a water playground, as well as the new bouldering rock, invite children to play and let off steam.

properties.name: Braumanufaktur Hertl
properties.description:
## A Family in Beer Fever

David Hertl knew what he wanted at 15: to become a brewer!

After a year of practical training in seven (!) breweries, he went on to train with Düll in Krautheim, then earned his master brewer’s qualification and also became a beer and wine sommelier.

Then, in 2012, the time had come: Hertl founded his brewery manufactory, largely planned and built by himself and firmly in family hands, which is why every family member got their own beer.

With almost 40 (!) beer creations per year, there are still plenty of new beer names left for friends and employees.

For smaller groups, the family ensemble also offers brewing seminars.

David’s latest coup: the takeover of Eichhorn Brewery in Forchheim and the brewing facility of Friedel Brewery in Schnaid.

Eichhorn’s former head brewer Kunner Greif supported David with advice and practical help and introduced him to the secret recipes of his family.

Under David’s aegis, the brewery’s own cooling ship is also being returned to its true purpose.

The cooling ship in Schnaid, however, he had already brought back to life.

Since then, many of his special brews have seen the light of day here.

properties.name: Griess Brewery Inn
properties.description:
## As nature created it

That’s the beer of Peter Griess, who in 1983, as the then youngest brewmaster in Germany, took over the brewery from his father Andreas. With his beer, he relies entirely on tradition: it is neither flash-pasteurized nor sterile-filtered, and certainly not preserved. Yet its drinkability means the best-before date is never reached anyway. Tip: the light cellar beer, so even drivers can enjoy it without regret. In winter, the popular pale bock has noticeably more alcohol. Bread-time snack with chatter: this is the kind of evening program guests of the brewery inn treat themselves to. The snack here consists mainly of Ziebeleskäs, garlic cheese and Zwetschgenbames, which are available both in the inn and at the lovely beer cellar next door. The chatter usually concerns the latest news from Geisfeld society and, of course, the political farces from nearby Bamberg. Also recommended is the Griess Cellar a little outside the village. At the entrance to Geisfeld (about 100 m from the inn), camper van enthusiasts can park their vehicle in the natural parking area.

properties.name: Sailing on Lake Großer Brombach - Pleinfeld Recreational Facility
properties.description: In the heart of Franconia, water sports enthusiasts can expect ideal conditions for their leisure activities: set against an idyllic backdrop on the southern shore of Lake Großer Brombach, the Pleinfeld recreational facility has a total of 70 shore berths.

properties.name: Kneipp facility at the bathing lake
properties.description: Direkt am Badesee in Heiligenstadt gelegen, bietet die Kneippanlage eine ideale Möglichkeit zur Erfrischung und Gesundheitsförderung nach Sebastian Kneipp. Umgeben von der natürlichen Landschaft der Fränkischen Schweiz können Besucher hier beim Wassertreten die Durchblutung anregen und aktiv zur Entspannung beitragen.

properties.name: Schorschbräu GmbH
properties.description:
## Ahead of the Pack

Diplom-Braumeister Georg Tscheuschner has now made a name for himself worldwide with the mission of brewing the strongest beer in the world. In the competition with his main rival Brewdog from Scotland, he has the edge: the Schorschbock 57 reaches an astonishing 57.7% alcohol content. All this is brewed using classic brewing methods and in accordance with the purity law - though, of course, only to be enjoyed in small sips! Anyone not put off by the concentrated power of this barley juice can stock up on the beers from local and online retailers. The beers from Schorschbräu are certainly a small highlight as an aperitif or digestif for very special moments.

[Parking available](/verkehr/parkplatz-seezentrum_wald-42387)

From the landing stage of the MS Altmühlsee, the lake can be enjoyed from the water. In season, the boat tours the individual lake centers up to five times a day. During the season, numerous special events take place on the MS Altmühlsee.

The sailing harbor with 96 water berths and 120 land berths offers a slipway and an electric hook-up point. Sailing berth rental is handled by the Altmühlsee Special-Purpose Association.

properties.name: Lindenbräu e. K.
properties.description:
## A true family business

### Lillach Spring with sinter steps, 5- Seidl'a- Steig (hike to 5 breweries).

The inn has been family-owned since 1900; a malting house and brewery were added in 1932. Today, Irene Brehmer-Stockum and Ralf Stockum continue to run the brewery as a family business in the third generation. Beer is the passion at Lindenbräu, and love for the product comes first. Raw materials and consumables come from the local area: barley from local farmers, the finest aromatic hops from Gräfenberg, Spalt, and the Hallertau. Brewing is done in the traditional artisanal way according to the brewery's own recipe: through a multi-hour brewing process and traditional cold open-vat fermentation, Lindenbräu beer is given its flavor maturation in peace and quiet. Incidentally, some of the malt is produced on the threshing floor in the brewery's own malting house! Of course, good beer also calls for good food. And that is excellently provided at the brewery inn, and in summer also in the lovely beer garden under the linden tree in front of the house.

properties.name: Wallfahrtskirche St. Johannes der Täufer in Mettendorf
properties.description:
Mettendorf Church is a pilgrimage church dedicated to St. Anne. The pilgrimage to the two late Gothic miraculous images - a Madonna with the infant Jesus and a Holy Kin group - dates back to 1727. Many votive tablets on display still bear witness today to numerous answered prayers of pilgrims seeking help.

The present Church of St. John was built during the reign of Prince-Bishop Johann Anton II von Freyberg of Eichstätt in the years 1778 to 1738 by the court architect Gabriel de Gabrieli.

The ceiling paintings depict the Baptism of Christ in the choir as well as St. Anne and her death.

Scenes from the life of Mary can be seen on both galleries. The high altar was created around 1720; however, the altarpiece dates from the early 17th century and shows the church patron John the Baptist in the solitude of the desert. In the glass cases of the side altars are the two miraculous images: on the right, the seated St. Anne holding the infant Mary and the infant Jesus in her arms; on the left, the figure of Mary with the infant Jesus.

properties.name: Alte Veste
properties.description:
## Von Ruinenresten umgebener Aussichtsturm

Die Alte Veste im [**Fürther Stadtwald**](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/poi/stadtwald-fuerth-100121789/) wurde zwischen 1228 und 1235 als Turmhügelburg auf dem Rosenberg nahe Zirndorf errichtet. Zu jener Zeit war der Rosenberg noch weniger bewaldet als heute, wodurch die „Burg Berch" – benannt nach der Familie Berg, die sie erbauen ließ – stolz auf dem Hügel thronte.

Der heutige Aussichtsturm, der zwei Vorgänger hatte, die im Dreißigjährigen Krieg und im Zweiten Weltkrieg zerstört wurden, wurde am 17. September 1980 feierlich eröffnet. Seitdem ist die Alte Veste samt dem Gasthaus am Fuße des Turms ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel im Fürther Raum. Besucher können kostenlos die 162 Stufen zur Aussichtsplattform hinaufsteigen, die sich 28 Meter über dem Boden befindet. Von dort genießt man einen wunderbaren Blick über Fürth, Nürnberg, Zirndorf und den Landkreis Fürth, bei guter Sicht sogar bis in die Fränkische Schweiz.

## Historie trifft Genuss

Direkt am Fuße des Turms lädt der traditionsreiche [**Gasthof Alte Veste**](https://www.alteveste-zirndorf.de/) zur Einkehr ein. Von herzhaften Brotzeiten bis hin zu festlichen Banketten zelebriert die Küche die regionale Lebensart mit Hingabe. Ob nach dem Turmaufstieg oder als Stärkung zwischendurch, genießen Sie fränkische Gastlichkeit an einem Ort voller Geschichte und gutem Geschmack.

### Unser Tipp: Erlebnisweg Wallensteins Lager

Auf den Spuren des Dreißigjährigen Krieges führt der rund 17 km lange [**Erlebnisweg Wallensteins Lager**](https://www.zirndorf-tourismus.de/den-erlebnisweg-wallensteins-lager-erkunden) entlang der ehemaligen Lagergrenzen von 1632. An 28 interaktiven Stelen, Bodenmarkierungen und Originalschauplätzen wird Geschichte real und digital via App erlebbar gemacht.

Für Kinder ist ein breites Angebot an Spielgeräten und Spieltürmen vorhanden.

Für alle anderen Altersgruppen besteht die Möglichkeit durch die vorhandenen Geräte verschiedenste Muskelpartien zu trainieren und die Beweglichkeit, die Flexibilität des Körpers und die Motorik aktiv zu halten.

Das Schönste ist jedoch der Spaß, den Groß und Klein hier haben!

properties.name: Hauptbahnhof
properties.description:
The city's central railway hub

Fürth Central Station has borne its current title since 1922 and refers to the "railway building" built in 1863 on the Nuremberg–Würzburg line. The architect Eduard Rüber was commissioned to build it. On 19 June 1865, the first train left the station. In 1876, the Nuremberg–Bamberg line was also routed via Fürth, which made it necessary to add two wings in 1904. A station restaurant opened in the east wing on 14 August 1904. In 1914, a forecourt structure was added for the ticket halls.

In autumn 2013, it became known that Deutsche Bahn was planning to demolish the entrance hall in order to expand the underground shopping arcade from the station to the subway. The railway company stated that it had to tear down the forecourt structure for structural reasons and then replace it with a glass-and-steel building. The State Office for Monument Protection opposed these plans in a statement dated 28 October 2013. In January 2014, the issue was discussed in the city council, where the wish was expressed to preserve the entrance hall while taking monument protection into account.

In 1909, a freight station was also built. Over time, the Central Station replaced the older Ludwigsbahnhof on today's Freiheit, which had previously only been connected to the Ludwig Railway to Nuremberg.

properties.name: Hausen
properties.description:
Hausen offers, in addition to pure nature in and around the village, local recreation opportunities right on your doorstep. Take a quick bike ride or a short walk with the family into the nearby fields or to the water wheel on the Regnitz. Hausen is also connected to the running trail network “Lauferlebnis Fränkische Schweiz”; four marked running routes start in Hausen and two in Wimmelbach.

Via the hiking trails of the project “Kulturerlebnis Fränkische Schweiz,” Hausen and Wimmelbach are also connected to this hiking network with its cultural focus. On the hiking trail “Karpfen und andere große Fische” (24.6 km) from Forchheim to Hallerndorf, you will also learn a great deal about Hausen and Wimmelbach at five information boards along the way.

Or you can visit the village center, to the village museum in the Greifenhof. If interested, the local heritage officer offers a personal guided tour. Schloss Thurn amusement park is right in the neighboring village and offers variety for the whole family.

Hausen is attractively located on the Regnitz axis in the Nuremberg metropolitan region. The district town of Forchheim is within sight of Hausen. In just a few minutes you can reach all cultural opportunities from Nuremberg to Bamberg: opera, theaters, museums, and cinemas.

The Franconian Switzerland and the Karpfenland with its many attractive leisure activities are right on Hausen’s doorstep. An attractive public transport system will take you quickly everywhere.

**Family life means more than just living together under one roof in a place with sufficient educational opportunities. Families want to feel comfortable and at home in their place of residence. What does the municipality specifically do to meet the needs of families?**

Families and children are very important to us. In Hausen and Wimmelbach, three daycare centers and a forest kindergarten provide high-quality care for our youngest residents. From 2021, we have 5 kindergarten groups, 3 nursery groups, one mixed-age group in the regular kindergarten, and one group in the forest. The slightly older children have the primary school right in the village. Secondary schools can later be found in Heroldsbach and Forchheim. As a municipality, we fund an open all-day school with strongly rising numbers of children. The contact person for children and young people in Hausen is the municipal youth welfare service, which organizes an attractive holiday program and full-day holiday care program every year, also in cooperation with the clubs, so that the children are well cared for during much of the holidays.

Several playgrounds offer play opportunities close to homes in both parts of the village.

**The extremely long list of clubs shows the commitment of Hausen’s citizens. Which festivals and events are organized by the members and sweeten residents’ free time?**

The clubs in Hausen and Wimmelbach are committed and offer a wide range of activities in the community. Take advantage of this offer. As a long-time club chairman and youth leader, I can only recommend it. By actively participating in the clubs, you get to know people and can make friends. Everyone is warmly welcome here..

Fire brigade, sports, singing, theater, traditional costume, Kerwasburschen, and much more. Join in our diverse club landscape. In the cold season, our Theadärä are active. Within the clubs themselves, many Christmas parties and annual general meetings take place. In late spring, the many public club festivals begin, and in early autumn they come to an end with the still original Hausen Kerwa, shaped by tradition. The fire brigades, the sports clubs, and the larger associations such as the fruit and gardening association, the singing association, and the St. Wolfgang men’s association offer lovely festivals, sometimes lasting several days. Enjoy yourself and get to know Hausen and Wimmelbach at these festivals from their most beautiful side. Sit down at one of the tables and strike up a conversation; you will be welcome.

Since 2015, the municipality of Hausen, in cooperation with the “Fränkischer Theatersommer,” has also been offering open-air theater performances on the Greifenhof grounds. Top-class theater in the village in such a beautiful setting — you’d otherwise only find that in the city!

**Hausen is beautifully situated and has retained its village charm. But what else does the municipality have to offer?**

Two local supply centers make it possible to buy all the important things quickly within a few minutes. Doctors, dentists, alternative practitioners, and pharmacies are in the village.

Our farmers offer a wide range of regional products all year round in their farm shops or direct sales. From spring onward, Hausen shines as an asparagus village with an absolutely fresh selection of asparagus and many vegetable and fruit products. From the field and garden straight to your kitchen — that is the motto of our farmers.

You are warmly welcome here and invited to be surprised by the diversity and appeal of our municipality.

Yours  
Bernd Ruppert  
Mayor

properties.name: Brauerei Zehendner
properties.description:
## A tasty drink, even for the Swiss

The Zehendner brewery in Mönchsambach has been in existence since 1808 and has been family-owned since 1939. It brews Export, unfiltered lager beer, Hefeweizen, May bock, wheat bock and Christmas bock. About three or four times a week, Stefan Zehendner fires up the brewhouse, and you can smell all over the village that fine barley juice is being made again, known in Franconia only as “the good Mönchsambach beer” and greatly appreciated. By the way, it has already made it onto the Swiss national holiday to be drunk by the Swiss. Today I bake, tomorrow I brew – at “Zehendner” this old brewer’s wisdom is still alive; beer and home-baked bread share the good reputation there. And rightly so. Best of all, according to connoisseurs and regulars, the two taste best together. For example, with the famous house-made bratwurst and mustard, or for vegetarians with Ziebeleskäs from the organic farmer. Children can let off steam on the small playground.

properties.name: Roppelt Brewery Inn
properties.description:
## At the Foot of Kreuzberg

### Kreuzberg

Here is the beer cellar of the Roppelt brewery, founded in 1870, which contributes a great deal to Kreuzberg’s reputation as a mecca for beer-cellar visitors. There you can enjoy the tasty cellar beer, homemade snacks, home-baked cakes, and hot dishes such as Schäuferla, pork knuckle, and Knöchla. Every two weeks, the Roppelts celebrate tapping their house-brewed beer, essentially a mini Oktoberfest-style tapping every 14 days. By the way, the brewery’s beer is available only in the inn and at the Roppelt Keller 200 meters away (a real classic and one of THE tips for families!), but always fresh from the barrel. Carp and game: these are the inn’s specialties, apart from the beer. With the Aischgrund carp (from their own ponds), the Roppelts serve homemade potato salad, which itself would be worthy of its own small fan base. Otherwise, game lovers also get their money’s worth: roe deer, hare, wild boar, and wild duck from their own hunting grounds are regularly on the menu here and are sure to delight connoisseurs of local specialties.

properties.name: Reichold Brewery Guesthouse
properties.description:
## Not so sweet, lightly hopped, and very easy to drink

### Brewery Trail Aufsess, centrally located between Bamberg, Bayreuth, and Forchheim.

This is how the not exactly few die-hard Franconian beer fans describe the lager from Reichold, another of Aufsess’s world-record breweries. Our favorite, however, is the Zwick‘l, an amber-colored, unfiltered cellar beer that is especially refreshing after a long hike. The family business, now over 100 years old, is currently run by Jörg Reichold, who brews his total of four different beers in the brewhouse built by his grandfather Felix in 1960. The fermentation, storage, and filtration cellars were completely rebuilt in 2002, and the bottling line has long since been brought up to date as well. Thanks to its good reputation, Jörg Reichold now ships his crates of beer all over the world. From there, a colorful mix of guests also comes here to the tranquil Aufsess district of Hochstahl, where they either stay in the guesthouse or at the lovely caravan site. His guests often walk the famous Brewery Trail and end their beer-filled day at Reichold’s, close to bed. Sounds like a very good idea for a nice outing, doesn’t it?

properties.name: KOHLENMÜHLE Inn-Brewery e. K.
properties.description:
## Return after a short break

The Kohlenmühle in Neustadt an der Aisch is a place where history does not just hang on the walls, but comes freshly tapped into the glass. An old grain mill, once in a dilapidated state, has been transformed into a lively brewery inn that, since its revival, once again does exactly what Franconia does especially well: provide good beer, good food, and good reasons to linger a little longer. At the center is Lothar Hufnagel’s small in-house brewery. The beer is brewed by hand according to the Bavarian Purity Law—for guests, friends of the house, and anyone who likes to drink their Seidla with character. The Moggerla, a pale, unfiltered full-bodied beer, is something like the friendly host in a glass: easy-drinking, down-to-earth, and pleasantly uncomplicated. There is also the dark, malty Rabenschwarz and the fresh Eiszeitweizen with its soft, fruity note. If you are lucky with the season, you may also encounter the Koksbock—the name alone sounds as if it would warm your shoulders a little in winter. The surroundings fit as well: the mill courtyard, beer garden on the Aisch island, historic walls, and an event barn with old copper brewing kettles create an atmosphere that is rustic without seeming old-fashioned. The kitchen serves Franconian, seasonal fare—with Schäufele, carp, bratwurst, and everything a hungry beer calls for in a worthy companion.

properties.name: Jüdisches Museum Franken
properties.description:
## Jüdische Geschichte und Kultur: Mittelalter bis Gegenwart

Das Jüdische Museum Franken vermittelt die faszinierende Vielfalt fränkisch-jüdischen Lebens von seinen Anfängen im Mittelalter bis in die Gegenwart. Es umfasst drei Standorte in Fürth, Schnaittach und Schwabach, deren Museumsgebäude allesamt beeindruckende historische Baudenkmäler sind. Träger des 1990 gegründeten Museums ist ein gemeinnütziger Verein.

Die Häuser vereinen besondere Architektur, begehbare historische Räume und faszinierende Sammlungen zu einem lebendigen, authentischen Gesamterlebnis.

## Der Hauptsitz Fürth: Historisch und geheimnisvoll

Seit über zwei Jahrzehnten erzählt der Hauptsitz des Museums in Fürth anhand wertvoller Judaika, historischer Dokumente und persönlicher Alltagsgegenstände die Geschichte einer Region, die einst als bedeutendstes religiöses Zentrum des Judentums in Süddeutschland galt.

Das Museum selbst befindet sich in einem ehemaligen jüdischen Wohn- und Geschäftshaus aus dem frühen 18. Jahrhundert, das der jüdische Kaufmann Hirsch Fromm 1702 errichtete. Das Gebäude spiegelt auf einzigartige Weise den gelebten Alltag jüdischer Familien wider.

**Einzigartige Spuren der Vergangenheit entdecken:**

- **Das historische Ritualbad (Mikwe):** Ein Weg im Keller führt hinab zu einem originalen Tauchbad von 1702, wo Besucher die feucht-erdige Atmosphäre des historischen Gewölbes hautnah spüren.

- **Historische Laubhütten:** Im hinteren Anbau zeugen eine originale Kassettendecke und ein flexibles Dach aus dem 18. und 19. Jahrhundert von den traditionellen Laubhüttenfesten der Familien Ansbacher und Arnstein.

## Die Dauerausstellung: Geschichte, Riten & Überraschungen

Die Dauerausstellung bietet spannende und oft überraschende Einblicke in jüdische Riten, Festtage und Lebensweisen:

- Erfahren Sie, wie jüdische Gemeinden bereits im Mittelalter virtuelle Gedächtnisräume schufen.

- Entdecken Sie bewegende Familiengeschichten – etwa warum ein ausgestelltes Porzellanservice gleich vier Mal den Atlantik überqueren musste.

- Gehen Sie auf Spurensuche zu ganz praktischen Fragen des jüdischen Alltags: Wie klingt ein Schofar? Warum gelten Heuschrecken als koscher? Und was macht eigentlich ein Tyrannosaurus Rex im Museum?

## Raum für Begegnung, Kultur & Genuss

Ein 2018 eröffneter, moderner Anbau erweitert das Museum in Fürth um Räumlichkeiten für wechselnde Sonderausstellungen, Kulturveranstaltungen, eine Fachbibliothek sowie einen Museumsshop mit integrierter Buchhandlung.

**Das Mary S. Rosenberg Café im Museumsgarten**

Ein besonderer Ort zum Verweilen ist das museumseigene Café im idyllischen Garten. Hier werden traditionelle jüdische Gebäckspezialitäten serviert, darunter die berühmte *Fürther Zitronentorte*, die nach dem Originalrezept einer jüdischen Familie gebacken wird.

## Wichtige Links für Ihren Besuch

- **[Hier finden Sie alle wichtigen Besucherinfos](https://www.juedisches-museum.org/besuch/)**

- **[Hier finden Sie eine Übersicht weiterer Museen in Fürth.](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/entdecken-staunen/kunst-kultur/museen/)**

## Unser Tipp: Stadtführungen zur Jüdischen Geschichte in Fürth

Einst als „Fränkisches Jerusalem“ bekannt, war Fürth über Jahrhunderte ein bedeutendes Zentrum jüdischen Lebens in Süddeutschland. Ergänzend zum Museumsbesuch bietet die Tourist-Information Fürth spannende thematische Stadtführungen an. Das Führungsangebot der Tourist-Information umfasst unter anderem:

- **[Wovon die Steine zeugen](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/stadtspaziergaenge/juedisches-fuerth/wovon-die-steine-zeugen/)**

- **[Jüdisches Leben – damals und heute](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/stadtspaziergaenge/juedisches-fuerth/juedisches-leben-damals-und-heute/)**

- **[Ein guter Ort – der Neue Jüdische Friedhof](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/stadtspaziergaenge/juedisches-fuerth/neuer-juedischer-friedhof/)**

- **[Fürth – Zentrum jüdischen Lebens](https://www.tourismus-fuerth.de/erleben-geniessen/stadtspaziergaenge/juedisches-fuerth/fuerth-zentrum-juedischen-lebens/)**

properties.name: The Castle Road
properties.description: Idyllische Landschaften, malerische Orte, mehr als 60 eindrucksvolle historische Gemäuer und unzählige weitere Sehenswürdigkeiten: An der Burgenstraße finden Sie alles, was eine gelungener Urlaub braucht. Zwischen Mannheim und Bayreuth erwarten Sie entlang der 780 Kilometer langen Route über 40 sehenswerte Orte - vom charmanten Geheimtipp über UNESCO-Welterbestätten bis zum weltbekannten Reiseziel á la Heidelberg, Rothenburg ob der Tauber oder Nürnberg. "Werte Schätzen - Schätze entdecken" lautet das Motto der traditionsreichen Touristikroute - eine Einladung zum Reisen mit Muße: Erkunden Sie entlang der Burgenstraße die vielfältigen Kultur- und Genussregionen zwischen Neckar und Fichtelgebirge - als individuelle und entspannte Bummeltour durch die Vergangenheit auf den Spuren von Rittern und Edeldamen, Kurfürsten und Markgrafen, Königen und Kaisern. Nicht der schnellste, sondern der schönste Weg von Ort zu Ort verbindet die mehr als 45 Stationen der Burgenstraße. In beiden Richtungen durchgehend beschildert, lässt sich die beliebte Ferienstraße in beliebig langen oder kurzen Etappen erkunden. Unterwegs warten prachtvolle Schlösser, trutzige Burgen, romantische Ruinen und verträumte Altstädte darauf, entdeckt zu werden. Vielfältige Erlebnisangebote laden Sie zum Kennenlernen und Mitmachen ein, darunter Führungen im historischen Gewand oder mittelalterliche Märkte. Für einen genussvollen Roadtrip sorgen auch die Spezialitäten einer jeden Region: Kosten Sie feinen Schwetzinger Spargel, zünftige schwäbische Spätzle und Maultaschen, deftige fränkische Bratwürste, Württemberger Weinbautradition, oberfränkische Bierbraukunst und kleine süße Verführungen vom Heidelberger Studentenkuss bis zum Coburger Schmätzchen. Wandern und radeln, schwimmen und saunieren, klettern und Kanu fahren, Höhlentouren und Dampfbahnstrecken, Museen und Parks, Golf und Greifvögel: Reichern Sie Ihre Burgenstraßen-Tour nach Lust und Laune mit weiteren Aktivitäten an. Ein reichhaltiges Angebot erwartet Sie! Die Burgenstraße lässt sich nicht nur mit dem Auto bereisen. Sie ist auch ein ideales Revier für Wohnmobilisten, Oldtimerfahrer und Motorradliebhabern. Der in etwa parallel verlaufende Radweg "Burgenstraße" lädt auf 860 Kilometern dazu ein, sich mit dem Drahtross ins Reich der Ritter aufzumachen. Wer nachhaltig unterwegs sein möchte, kann die Burgenstraße auch mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln entdecken. Die 14 Premium Partner Hotels der Burgenstraße reichern Ihre Reise in die Vergangenheit mit zeitgemäßem Komfort und persönlicher gelebter Gastlichkeit an. Ausführliche, zielgruppengerecht aufbereitete Informationen finden Sie auf unserer Homepage www.burgenstrasse.de. Dort können Sie auch umfangreiches Prospektmaterial downloaden oder kostenfrei bestellen. Die Stationen der Burgenstraße von West nach Ost: Mannheim - Schwetzingen - Heidelberg - Neckargemünd - Neckarsteinach - Hirschhorn - Eberbach - Mosbach - Hotel-Restaurant Burg Hornberg - Gundelsheim / Schlosshotel Horneck - Burg Guttenberg - Neckarbischofsheim - Sinsheim - Bad Wimpfen - Heilbronn - Weinsberg - Öhringen - Waldenburg - Schwäbisch Hall - Kirchberg an der Jagst / Biohotel Schloss Kirchberg - Rothenburg ob der Tauber - Colmberg / Hotel Burg Colmberg - Ansbach - Lichtenau - Wolframs-Eschenbach - Abenberg - Roth - Stein b. properties.name: Sophienhöhle bei Burg Rabenstein
properties.description:
Über Jahrtausende sind in der Höhle Tropfsteingebilde entstanden: Stalagmiten, wie der riesige "Millionär", oder bis zu drei Meter lange Sinterfahnen. Im Vorhöhlenraum wird eines der vollständigsten Höhlenbärenskelette weltweit gezeigt.

Von April bis Oktober bieten Höhlenkonzerte ein einzigartiges Musikerlebnis. Bei "Sophie at night" - samstagabends von 18 bis 21 Uhr - ist die Höhle erfüllt von wunderbarer Musik und eine faszinierende Lichtinzenierung lenkt den Blick auf die Glanzpunkte der Höhle.

Geschichtliches:

Die Sophienhöhle bei Rabenstein im Ahorntal gilt als die älteste urkundlich erwähnte Höhle der Frankenalb. Schon 1490 wird von einem Versuch zur Gewinnung von Salpeter im Vorraum der Höhle berichtet. Dieser Vorraum wurde bereits von prähistorischen Menschen aufgesucht, wir die zahlreichen Funde vorgeschichtlicher Keramik beweisen.

Die Entdeckung weiterer tropfsteingeschmückter Räume im Jahre 1833 bescherte der Sophienhöhle schlagartige Berühmtheit. Da die neuen Räume sofort nach ihrer Entdeckung verschlossen wurden und der nachfolgende Ausbau zur Schauhöhle sehr behutsam erfolgte, hat die Sophienhöhle bis in die heutige Zeit ihren ursprünglichen Reiz bewahrt. Die 1. und 2. Abteilung sind mit Tropfsteinformationen großer Formen- und Farbenvielfalt ausgeschmückt. Die 3. Abteilung zählt mit seinen 42x25x11 Metern zu den größten fränkischen Höhlenräumen. Die Sophienhöhle gilt als eine der schönsten Höhlen Deutschlands. Sie ist benannt nach der Schwiegertochter des damaligen Besitzers. Einzigartige Bewohner der Höhle sind Strudelwürmer, konnte Dr. Schabdach feststellen.

properties.name: Tiergarten Nürnberg
properties.description:
Der Tiergarten Nürnberg ist ein ganz besonderes Ausflugsziel. Unzählige große und kleine Tiere und eine von Felsen und Wald geprägte Landschaft machen einen Besuch zu einem interessanten, erholsamen und spannenden Erlebnis. Mehr als eine Million Besuche verbucht der Tiergarten Nürnberg pro Jahr.

Der einzigartige Landschaftszoo mit ruhigen Wegen zwischen alten Bäumen und großen Freiflächen, Weihern und Wasserwelten bietet etwa 300 Tierarten ein Zuhause. Im Tiergarten Nürnberg gibt es mit der Delphinlagune die einzige Freianlage für diese Meeressäugetiere in Deutschland.

properties.name: Schloss Weissenstein in Pommersfelden
properties.description: Mit seinen Gemäldegalerien, seiner kompletten Inneneinrichtung und seiner beeindruckenden Architektur ist Schloss Weissenstein in Pommersfelden ein repräsentatives Glanzstück des fränkischen Barock. Es wurde 1711 bis 1718 von Johann Dientzenhofer erbaut. Der Bauherr Fürstbischof Lothar Franz v. Schönborn war ein leidenschaftlicher Kunstsammler. Neben hervorragenden italienischen und deutschen Werken enthält die Galerie mit ihren etwa 500 Gemälden auch eine stattliche Anzahl niederländischer und flämischer Arbeiten des 16. bis 18. Jh. Zu sehen sind u. a. Werke von Brueghel, van Dyck, Rubens und Tizian.

properties.name: Ansbach Golf Club - Colmberg Castle
properties.description:
At the foot of Colmberg Castle, the beautiful and traditional 18-hole golf course of Golf Club Ansbach lies.  

For relaxed golf on gently rolling terrain, the nine holes of the **"Altmühlrunde"** provide the perfect setting. Some sections of the course are reminiscent of a links course and reward steady play with a good score.  
The combination of different landscapes, flexible tee times, and a friendly atmosphere shape the character of the golf course.  

Old fruit trees, fairways running directly alongside the castle’s wildlife enclosures, and the hilly terrain define the landscape character of the somewhat more challenging 9 holes, the so-called **"Burgrunde"**.  
From here, you can enjoy magnificent views of the upper Altmühl Valley.  

To round off a day of golf, the **terrace with a wonderful view of Colmberg Castle** is an inviting place to relax in good company. If necessary, even without a round of golf. Cyclists passing by here on the Altmühl Cycle Path also like to stop here.  

Click here for the [short film about Golf Club Ansbach](https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=1&v=aS1Kenur_Bo) in Colmberg.  

Offer:  
Golf school, courses, large driving range, practice area, restaurant, tournaments. Green fee agreements with hotels in the region, motorhomes for golfers allowed in the parking lot.  

[Green fee information](https://www.golf-ansbach.de/gaeste/greenfee/)

properties.name: Museum Berching
properties.description: The life and work of the town's most important son, the opera composer and reformer Christoph Willibald Gluck (1714-1787), are a focus of the Berching Museum of Local History. In a multimedia presentation, Gluck's life, which took him through half of Europe, is illustrated and traced with numerous musical examples. In addition, the museum shows an extensive collection of peasant furniture, mainly from the western Upper Palatinate, from the period 1700 to 1880 and numerous utensils from peasant and rural bourgeois everyday life.

properties.name: Bubenreutheum (Instrument Manufacture Museum Bubenreuth)
properties.description: Eine kleine fränkische Gemeinde schrieb Musikgeschichte. Weltberühmte Musiker wie Elvis, die Beatles, die Rolling Stones oder Yehudi Menuhin, sie alle spielten im Laufe ihrer Karriere auf Instrumenten aus Bubenreuth. Das bäuerliche Dorf war in der Nachkriegszeit zur europäischen Metropole des Saiteninstrumentenbaus aufgestiegen. Zu verdanken war dies der Bereitschaft der 500 Einheimischen, 2000 Instrumentenbauern aus dem Sudetenland eine neue Heimat zu geben.Entstanden ist hier ein Musikmuseum der besonderen Art, das kontinuierlich weiter ausgebaut wird: das Bubenreutheum. Musikinstrumente, Texte, Bilder und v. a. Musikbeispiele ermöglichen eine Reise durch die Entwicklung der verschiedenen Musikstile des 20. Jh. und erzählen zudem die Geschichte von Flucht, Vertreibung und einer erfolgreichen Integration in der Nachkriegszeit.

properties.name: Botanischer Garten der Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (Botanical Garden of the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg)
properties.description: Klein, aber fein: An die 5000 verschiedene Pflanzenarten aus aller Welt können im Botanischen Garten im nördlichen Schlossgarten bestaunt werden. 1828 gegründet, dient er sowohl der akademischen Lehre als auch der Erbauung und zeigt seinen Besuchern das ganze Jahr über pflanzliche Artenvielfalt und naturkundliche Zusammenhänge. Einzigartig ist die sogenannte Neischlhöhle, eine künstliche Tropfsteinhöhle, die 1907 errichtet wurde und durch ihre außergewöhnliche Naturtreue auch heute noch fasziniert. Die normalen Öffnungszeiten beziehen sich auf die Gewächshäuser und die saisonalen Öffnungszeiten auf das Freigelände.

properties.name: Kunstpalais Erlangen (Erlangen Art Palace)
properties.description: Old meets new: Palais Stutterheim, built in 1730, houses the Kunstpalais on two floors, which specialises in contemporary art and art education. Relevant positions of the international art scene and their conceptual references to literature, philosophy and film are the focus here.The Kunstpalais also includes the Erlangen Municipal Collection (Erlangen Art Palace). It comprises well over 4,500 important graphics, multiples, artists' books and portfolios and reflects important trends in international art after 1945.

properties.name: Siemens MedMuseum (Siemens Medical Technology Museum)
properties.description: Medical technology from Erlangen has been going around the world since the discovery of X-rays in 1895. The Siemens MedMuseum is now located in the machine hall of Siemens Healthcare's predecessor company Reiniger, Gebbert & Schall, which was built in 1893. It tells stories of people with a pioneering spirit and displays selected exhibits on medical technology from its beginnings to the present day. Equipped with digital magnifying glasses, visitors can immerse themselves in the fascinating world of medical technology over an area of 400 m².

properties.name: Heinrich Kirchner Sculpture Garden
properties.description: 17 bronze **large-scale sculptures** by the Erlangen artist are on display there: in the upper, park-like area, the older, less monumental figures are exhibited; the steeper lower area is characterized by ten monumental sculptures from the artist's final years. Kirchner's works deal directly or indirectly with the relationship between **human beings and nature**.

properties.name: Loewenich Palace/Art Museum
properties.description:
In the mid-18th century, this building was constructed by Joachim Christoph Herr in the **Baroque style**. From 1817 onward, it served the **Loewenich family** as a residence and for tobacco manufacturing. It remained in family ownership until 1941. Today it houses the **Art Museum**.

The exhibition program of the Art Museum of the city of Erlangen includes **regional art after 1945**. The focus is primarily on the work of artists from Erlangen and the Nuremberg metropolitan region. Solo, group, thematic, and memorial exhibitions are shown, as well as photography and art from regional collectors.

The **exhibitions** at the Erlangen Art Museum change regularly, so there is something new to discover with every visit.

properties.name: Pottenstein Adventure Rock
properties.description:
The Pottenstein Adventure Rock is a unique excursion destination in Bavaria that has something to offer for everyone. From adventure and fun to relaxation and nature experiences, the Pottenstein Adventure Rock offers a wide variety of attractions that will delight visitors of all ages.

- 2 summer toboggan runs
- Witch's Broom
- Skywalk
- excursion dining
- and much more

properties.name: Heimatmuseum Merkendorf (Museum of local history Merkendorf)
properties.description: The Heimatmuseum Merkendorf (Museum of local history Merkendorf) provides a varied insight into the former life, living and work in a small agrarian town. In the tithe barn dating from 1726, handicraft tools and products, evidence of popular piety, textiles, household goods and agricultural implements document the town's history, such as Merkendorf's former position as a cabbage metropolis or its importance as a weaving town.

properties.name: Kräutlein Mill
properties.description:
Die Barockmühle in Wiesethbruck ist die einzige noch mahlende Mühle an der Wieseth und seit 1880 in unserem Familienbesitz .

Zur Zeit arbeiten wir mit zwei Generationen in der Mühle, die mit Hilfe der Wasserkraft ca. 800 Tonnen Getreide pro Jahr vermahlt. Ist die Mühle nicht in Betrieb, wird der Strom zur Warmwasserbereitung der Wohngebäude genutzt.

properties.name: Industriemuseum Lauf (Industrial Museum Lauf)
properties.description: In 14 denkmalgeschützten Gebäuden taucht der Besucher im Industriemuseum Lauf in eine vergangene Arbeitswelt ein. Von der „Frühindustrie“ bis zur „Hochindustrie“ macht das Ensemble Aspekte der regionalen Industriegeschichte erlebbar. Direkt an der Pegnitz gelegen, kann das Museum sogar mit funktionsfähigen wasserradgetriebenen Originalgewerken aufwarten: ein Eisenhammerwerk, eine Getreidemühle und ein Elektrizitätswerk. Das 20. Jh. wird repräsentiert durch die ehemalige Ventilfabrik Dietz. Werkstätten typisch städtischer Gewerbe und Wohnungseinrichtungen vervollständigen das Bild vom Alltag städtischer Arbeiter und Handwerker von etwa 1890 bis 1970.

properties.name: Antikensammlung der Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (Collection of Antiquities of Friedrich-Alexander-University Erlangen-Nuremberg)
properties.description: Friends of ancient Greek vases will find what they are looking for at the university's Collection of (Classical) Antiquities. In addition, numerous other ancient pottery objects and small-scale works of art and craft are on display. With a total of around 700 original ancient objects, the museum offers an overview of the development of cultures in the Mediterranean region from Troy to the Roman imperial period. The focus is on Greek pottery from the 6th and 5th centuries BC, especially the richly decorated vases from Athens. The plaster cast gallery, the original core of the collection founded in 1857, shows around 150 larger sculptures and statues.

properties.name: Altmühltaler Schnuckenhof
properties.description:
In der Schäferei Glossner werden rund sieben verschiedene Schafrassen gehalten. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf Herdbuchzucht und Erhaltung alter und gefährdeter Nutztierrassen. Dazu gehören unter anderem Alpines Steinschaf, Rhönschaf, Skudde, sowie graue und weiße gehörnte Heidschnucken und weiße hornlose Heidschnucken. Mit dieser Vielfalt leistet die Schäferei einen wichtigen Beitrag zum Erhalt genetischer Ressourcen und zur traditionellen Schafhaltung.

properties.name: Brauhaus Höchstadt/Aisch e. G.
properties.description:
## Bier kann auch zuhause reifen

In den 1920er Jahren spitzte sich die Lage am Höchstadter Biermarkt drastisch zu. Einerseits schlossen immer mehr Privatbrauer ihre Pforten, andererseits war das Kommunbrauhaus nicht in der Lage, die schnell ansteigende Nachfrage zu befriedigen. So schlossen sich am 8. Dezember 1926 sieben Höchstadter Gastwirte zusammen und gründeten eine Brauereigenossenschaft, das Brauhaus Höchstadt. Heute ist es Michael Ackermann, der etwa 6.000 hl Bier im Jahr herstellt. In der alten Tradition findet an jedem Mittwoch das Hausbrauer-Fassen statt, wenn sich die Beteiligten das Bier in ihre Fässer füllen lassen, in denen es dann zuhause fertig reifen kann.

properties.name: Franken-Therme Bad Windsheim
properties.description:
Immerse yourself in the soothing and healing Bad Windsheim natural brine and do something good for your body and soul.

Six thermal saltwater pools with salt concentrations between 1.5% and 12% invite you to enjoy healthy bathing in the indoor and outdoor areas of the 17,500 m2 thermal spa complex.  
Various water attractions, steam baths, Kneipp pools, as well as activity and relaxation offerings, provide variety.  

The highlight of the spa is the partially covered salt lake with a semi-transparent dome. Fed with fully saturated brine (26.9% salt content), you can bathe and float here just like in the Dead Sea.

In the sauna area, visitors can expect eight saunas, the icy cold snow sauna, a relaxation pool, the spacious sauna garden, as well as several rest rooms and a daily changing infusion program.  
The day can be rounded off with a wellness treatment in the generously designed spa area.

properties.name: Margravial Museum with Kaspar Hauser section
properties.description:
This required a costly third firing. The models for the patterns and colors were Chinese porcelains from the so-called Kangxi period, from the late 17th and early 18th centuries. Attempts were made in many places in Europe to imitate this, but only in Ansbach was it possible between 1724 and 1749 to reproduce the quality of the colors. After that, knowledge of the special color recipe was probably lost. This means that the beginnings of the Green Family date back to the years of rule of Margravine Christiane Charlotte.

Prepared according to modern museum-education principles, and in part also staged, the history of the city and the Principality of Ansbach becomes an informative experience at the Margravial Museum. The collections are housed in an attractive building complex dating from the 14th to the 18th century, which also includes a section of walkable city wall. On the ground floor of the main building, the Kaspar Hauser section can be explored; on the upper floors are the collections from the margravial period. Both are accessible without barriers. The annex houses exhibits from prehistory and early history.

No guided tours on Mondays.

Admission prices:
Adults: €3.50
Reduced admission (young people aged 13 to 17, students, trainees, unemployed persons, holders of the volunteer service card, severely disabled persons, participants in the Federal Volunteer Service): €2.00

Family ticket (max. two adults plus accompanying children and young people up to 17 years): €7.50
Children up to 12 years, visitors with the Discoverer Pass, school classes, groups from kindergartens, members of the Historical Association for Middle Franconia, members of the Art Association, visitors as part of city tours, press: free

The exhibits of the

**[Jägerndorf Homeland Rooms](https://www.jaegerndorf-sudetenland.de/Termine.html)**

can be viewed on approx. 60 m² in the Margravial Museum Ansbach (Kaspar-Hauser-Platz 1) during the museum's current opening hours.

properties.name: Heilsbronn
properties.description:
Die Fränkische **Münsterstadt** Heilsbronn mit seinen 9.500 Einwohnern liegt in einem waldreichen Tal des Romantischen Frankens zwischen Nürnberg und Ansbach und ist im wahrsten Sinne des Wortes das Zentrum Mittelfrankens, da sich am nördlichen Rand der Stadt der **geografische Mittelpunkt** des Regierungsbezirks befindet.

Als attraktives und lohnenswertes Ausflugsziel zeichnet sich Heilsbronn durch sein breites **Freizeit- und Kulturangebot** sowie durch seine lebendige Gemeinschaft mit regem Sozial- und Vereinsleben aus. So locken Konzerte im Münster sowie traditionelle Kirchweihen, Feste und Märkte immer wieder aufs Neue zahlreiche Besucher an und auch die

*__Kultur im Kreuzgang__* ist seit 2001 fester Bestandteil des Veranstaltungskalenders. Aber auch erst kürzlich im Programm aufgenommene Veranstaltungen wie *Klassik im Garten* oder die Hervorhebung der Region als **Karpfengebiet** zeigen die kulturelle Vielfalt, die Heilsbronn zu bieten hat.

Sei es mittels des *__Fränkischen Karpfen-Radwegs__*  oder des *__Radwegs für Genießer__*, die herrliche Natur rund um Heilsbronn lässt sich mit einer Vielzahl an gut markierten Rad- und Wanderwegen vorbei an idyllischen Gasthöfen und Biergärten entdecken. Dabei ist Heilsbronn auch Teil des ehrwürdigen **Jakobswegs**, der als bekanntester Pilgerpfad zum Grab des Apostels Jakobus mit Station in Heilsbronn an nicht weniger bedeutenden Gräbern vorbei führt. So befindet sich im über 880-jährigen Münster die wohl in Süddeutschland größte **Hohenzollerngrablege** (1297 – 1625).

Das Münster gilt als die älteste Klosterkirche der **Zisterzienser** im deutschen Kulturraum und wurde 1132 vom Bischof Otto von Bamberg gestiftet. Einst durch den Mönchsorden zu kultureller und wirtschaftlicher Blüte gelangt, eröffnet sich in dem über 875-jährigen Münster eine Welt wertvoller Kunstschätze des Nürnberger Kunstkreises um Michael Wolgemut, Albrecht Dürer und Adam Kraft.  
**Touchscreen-Informationsterminals am **Konventhaus und am Bahnhof informieren dauerhaft und außerhalb der Rathaus-Öffnungszeiten.

properties.description:
At the Tourist Information office of the tourism association, you will receive detailed information about the entire Romantic Franconia region. City maps, cycling and hiking maps, sights and much more. The Tourist Information office is located in the Frankenhöhe community center in Colmberg, right next to the church.
Cyclists can charge their e-bikes here, and in front of the building a large bench under a tree invites you to rest.

properties.name: Franconian Open-Air Museum Bad Windsheim
properties.description:
They have all been moved to the museum from different parts of Franconia and are authentically furnished, very different depending on their region of origin.

In the summer months, the Franconian Open-Air Museum in Bad Windsheim offers themed weeks in the afternoons. Following the **"Cicerone principle"**, **big and small museum visitors** can learn about various topics  
. Museum guides and scientific staff at the relevant houses or objects provide museum visitors with exciting background information.  
A permanent exhibition on mill construction can be seen in the Schlauerbach Mill.

The open-air museum has a large program of events throughout the year, which are always very popular with visitors because the museum comes alive with exhibitions, courses, craft demonstrations, open-air theater, readings, evening concerts and open-air cinema.
