properties.name: Late Gothic Town Hall
properties.description:
The Town Hall was built around 1530 by the Augsburg master builder Sebolt Schönmacher. It is documented to have belonged to Count Verri de la Boshia and was granted by him to the municipality as a fief on 20 July 1802. The Town Hall only later, at an unknown date, passed into the ownership of the municipality.

Around 1813, the Town Hall contained — as was also customary in other municipalities at the time — among other things a grain market, a slaughterhouse, a large hall, a "Town Hall room" and a prison.

A defining feature is the five-storey pillar tower with a hood-like onion-shaped tower roof, in whose open lantern a bell is housed. The bell bears the inscription: "Ave Maria, gratie plena, Dominus tecum". On the onion dome there is a weather vane with the heraldic animal of Rennertshofen, a rising fox.

The Town Hall was renovated in 2005/2006 for approx. 1 million.

properties.name: Kolbermoor Spinning Mill
properties.description:
### History

The economically attractive connection between rail access and hydropower led in 1861 to the construction of the cotton spinning mill and six workers' houses. Further apartments and storage and factory buildings followed, and they have been preserved to this day.

To build the originally six-story cotton spinning mill, the Mangfall had to be straightened between Bad Aibling and Kolbermoor and a factory canal built. In 1863 yarn production began with 11,000 spindles, and by 1864 already with 41,000 spindles. After a fire, two three-story spinning mill buildings were rebuilt in 1899 and 1908 to the right and left of the factory canal, where yarn production continued until 1993.

After several years of renovation, the spinning mill site with former storage and factory buildings was professionally restored and has offered around 12,000 square meters of residential and office space, including restaurants and shopping areas, since 2011.

In the Spinnereipark to the west, residential buildings and an exciting [playground](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/alle-sehenswuerdigkeiten/spielplatz-spinnereipark-14bb4e2d52) were created.

### Industrial monument

The new spinning mill building in exposed brick was rebuilt as a three-story structure in 1899 after a fire. Preserved to this day are the clock tower, tower projections with pilaster strip articulation, cornice bands and segmental-arched windows in classicizing forms. Today, the new building is a residential building in the southern part and a commercial building in the northern part.

The former gatehouse is a two-story exposed brick building with a hipped roof, dormers, facade articulation and ashlar-framed aedicule detailing, and today houses, among other things, a bakery.

The former yarn warehouse is a single-story hall building over a raised basement of partly plastered brick masonry with pilaster strip articulation and segmental-arched windows in classicizing forms. This site was connected to the spinning mill grounds north of the canal by tracks. These tracks can still be seen today above the small bridge.

### Spinning mill grounds

From 1862 onward, various storage and workshop halls were built on the site north of the factory canal. Some of these are still completely preserved and have been carefully renovated inside and out. Throughout the site, partly plastered brick facades can be seen, along with segmental-arched, round-arched, segmental-arched and tall slit windows, pilaster strip articulation and projections.

The following are still preserved today:

- the bale warehouse
- batteur building
- dye works
- boiler house as a single-story hall building with a free-standing round chimney
- turbine house

These buildings are now listed monuments and house cafés, practices and shops. Many information boards explain the original function of each building.

The [boiler house can now be booked as an event venue](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/chiemsee/congress/house/Kolbermoor-Eventlocation-An-der-Alten-Spinnerei-DEU00000060702005577).

### Workers' housing

As part of industrialization and the construction of the cotton spinning mill, six workers' houses with 36 family apartments were initially built in 1862. Due to increasing production and the growing number of workers, additional residential buildings with a factory kindergarten were built from 1907 onward between the Mangfall and the Mangfall Canal. From 1920, two residential buildings were erected along Carl-Jordan-Straße.

The initially uniformly designed two-and-a-half-story gabled-roof houses with small outbuildings and gardens were replaced by a more differentiated style, mostly single-story, relatively spacious residential buildings in groups of two and three, with high roofs, transverse gables and bay windows. The aim was to create a more attractive living environment.

On Carl-Jordan-Straße, single- and two-story residential buildings were erected based on the model of Baroque palace architecture. Many bay-window extensions and decorative gables in baroque forms interrupt the long row development.

This workers' settlement has been preserved to this day and is owned by the city. "Nowhere else in Bavaria is there a comparable ensemble of a workers' settlement in a rural area." (State Office for Monument Preservation)

[You can read an exciting story about Kolbermoor's past here by our author Andrea Strauß >>](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/kunst-kultur-brauchtum/spinnerei-in-kolbermoor)

### Filming location discovery

The Old Spinning Mill served as a filming location for The Rosenheim Cops in 2002 (season 1, episode 9).

properties.name: Seating area on the Landshut High Trail
properties.description: Auf Keramik in die Ferne blicken.

properties.name: View of the Alps near Irnsing
properties.description: On a clear day, you can see all the way to the Alps from the Irnsing viewpoint.

properties.name: Pauls Ruh
properties.description:
Der Aussichtspunkt Pauls Ruh lässt sich bei der großen Wanderung ["Rund um die Herreinsel"](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/tourenportal/rund-um-die-herreninsel-ueber-ottos-und-pauls-ruh-f9007d7c36) mitnehmen. Der ruhige Ort, fernab des Trubels von [Schloss Herrenchiemsee](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/alle-sehenswuerdigkeiten/schloss-herrenchiemsee-55689a39bd), lädt zum Verweilen ein. Von dort eröffnen sich Ausblicke auf den [Chiemsee](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/chiemsee) und die nahe gelegenen Voralpen, wie beispielsweis die [Kampenwand](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/alle-sehenswuerdigkeiten/kampenwand-79a7a9ddcd).  

Bei der Wanderung wird auch der zweite Aussichtspunkt der Inse, Ottos Ruh passiert.

properties.name: Herrnberg Viewing Plateau
properties.description:
In the slightly elevated district of Herrnberg, the small viewpoint offers a wonderful view over the rooftops of Prien and the mountain panorama.

The viewpoint can be easily combined, for example, with [Hiking Trail No. 3 “Mountains, Moor and Lake“](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/tourenportal/wander-und-spazierweg-nr.-3-berg-moor-und-see-93dd975b04).

properties.name: Grieser Angel
properties.description:
Before 1600, the Gries consisted of just three houses. In the 17th and 18th centuries, a large number of craftsmen settled in the Gries area, as the water of the Prien was necessary for their trades.

Among those who settled there were dyers, rope makers, saddlers, wheelwrights, coppersmiths, soap boilers, gunsmiths, glaziers, artists, tailors, stocking knitters, rag collectors,

coopers, shoemakers; but court officials also lived in the Gries.

Particularly famous is the curious story of the Victory Genius sculpture (Grieser Angel) next to the linden tree in the Gries.

properties.name: Dorfmuseum Kienberg (Village Museum Kienberg)
properties.description: Evidence of local history, such as flags, richly embroidered chasubles and needlework sample ribbons, can be seen in the basement of the Kienberg schoolhouse.

properties.name: Parish Church of St. John the Baptist's Beheading in Neuhofen
properties.description: Ein spätgotischer Bau, der um 1500 errichtet wurde. Das Langhaus und der Turm sind älter. Das Langhaus wurde 1906 nach Westen verlängert. Die Einrichtung stammt hauptsächlich aus dem 18. Jhd.

properties.name: MobiFit course
properties.description: Der MobiFit-Parcours ist für jeden Mensch geeignet, aber im speziellen auf die Bedürfnisse der Generation 60+ ausgelegt. Verschiedene Geräte und Untergründe bieten die Möglichkeit den Bewegungsapparat zu stärken und für Alltagssituationen fit zu machen. Der Parcours befindet sich zwischen Simssee Klinik, Ambulantem Rehazentrum, Chiemgau Thermen und dem Kultursaal am Park. Er kann steht allen erwachsenen Benutzern zur Benutzung zur Verfügung.

properties.name: Pfarrkirche St. Peter und Paul Ellerbach
properties.description: The Catholic parish church of St. Peter and Paul in Ellerbach, a district of the municipality of Holzheim in the district of Dillingen an der Donau, was built in the mid-19th century on the site of a Gothic predecessor church. The tower dates back to the 14th/15th century. Especially worth seeing inside the church are the colorful leaded glass windows. These were created in 1911 based on designs by Joseph Peter Bockhorni in the workshop of Hans Bockhorni in Munich and depict the scenes of the Stations of the Cross.

properties.name: Old Port of Kelheim
properties.description:
### Ludwig-Donau-Main-Kanal – Geschichte einer Wasserstraße

Der [Ludwig-Donau-Main-Kanal](https://www.ludwig-donau-main-kanal.de/) verband einst die Donau bei [Kelheim](https://www.herzstueck.bayern/de/urlaubsregion/stadtgeschichten/stadtgeschichten-kelheim) mit dem Main bei Bamberg und war eine der bedeutendsten Ingenieursleistungen des frühen 19. Jahrhunderts. In den 1990er Jahren übernahm der moderne Main-Donau-Kanal seine Funktion als Schifffahrtsstraße. Der historische Kanal ist heute zwar nicht mehr befahren, aber entlang der gesamten Strecke von Kelheim nach Bamberg gibt es zahlreiche Zeugnisse dieser Epoche zu entdecken.

### Ein Denkmal der Ingenieurbaukunst

Der Alte Hafen Kelheim umfasst ein 600 Meter langes Ensemble aus Hafenbecken mit original erhaltenen Lastenkränen, dem Kanaltrog mit Schleuse 1, dem historischen Lagerhaus sowie dem Schleusenwärterhaus. Da alle diese Bauten noch vollständig funktionsfähig sind, wurde das Gesamtensemble als Denkmal der Ingenieurbaukunst unter Schutz gestellt. An einem Info-Punkt erfahren Besucher Wissenswertes über die Kanalgeschichte und den Alltag der Menschen an seinen Ufern.

### Aktiv entlang des Kanals

Wer den Kanal auf eigene Faust erkunden möchte, findet entlang des Main-Donau-Kanals und der historischen Überbleibsel des Ludwig-Donau-Main-Kanals attraktive Radwege: Der [Fünf-Flüsse-Radweg](https://fuenf-fluesse-radweg.info/de/) und der [Regnitz-Radweg](https://www.regnitzradweg.de/) führen durch die Kanallandschaft, die [„Erlebnis-Kanal-Tour“](https://www.ludwig-donau-main-kanal.de/wege/radtour_kanalerlebnis-3959/) verbindet gezielt die wichtigsten historischen Stationen.

### Stadthafenfest mit Fischerstechen

Jeden August verwandelt sich der Alte Hafen in einen lebendigen Veranstaltungsort: Beim traditionellen Hafenfest findet das Fischerstechen statt, ein altes Wettkampfspektakel auf der Donau. Zwei Mannschaften treten jeweils in einer Zille – einem traditionellen Fischerboot Bayerns und Österreichs – gegeneinander an. Während die Ruderer das Boot in Position bringen, versucht der Mann am Bug, den Gegner mit einer Stange ins Wasser zu stoßen. Livemusik und regionale Kulinarik runden das Fest ab.

properties.name: Sisi-Schloss Aichach-Unterwittelsbach
properties.description:
The moated castle in the Aichach district of Unterwittelsbach was acquired by Duke Max in Bavaria as a hunting lodge. The daughter of “Zither-Maxl” – Elisabeth – became Empress of Austria in 1854. Exhibitions are held annually in the moated castle. The new permanent exhibition on the first floor offers multifaceted insights into Elisabeth’s life from childhood to death and explores the question of how the myth of “Sisi” came into being. In a multimedia presentation, visitors learn a great deal about Elisabeth’s problems with the strict Viennese court ceremonial. They gain an impression of her cult of beauty and her escape into extensive travels. Reproductions of the Empress’s dresses are skillfully staged. The “Sisi Castle” is a stop on the European “Sisi Route”. The castle park can be visited year-round.

The castle chapel of St. Ulrich, Afra and the Virgin Mary, with its neo-Gothic, Oriental-style mix, is unique far and wide. Two heraldic stones bearing the lozenges and the lion of the Palatinate on the Rhine adorn the façade.

The castle itself is open only in connection with events and during the Sisi exhibition.

properties.name: Branch Church "St. Nicholas" Argelsried
properties.description: Built as a replacement for the dilapidated, smaller Baroque predecessor, the church in Argelsried in the municipality of Gilching, consecrated in 1931 and very plain on the outside, impresses inside with a magnificent wooden barrel vault and its rich Late Renaissance and Baroque furnishings.

properties.name: Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary
properties.description:
The Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary, built in 1431, with its monumental triple onion dome tower, is clearly visible from afar and an impressive church building.

The high-quality Baroque altar furnishings as well as the beautiful frescoes from 1774, "The Coronation of Mary," and a rare allegory of the "Adoration of the Lamb of God" are noteworthy.

For centuries, many pilgrims visited the church especially because of the Salzburg carved figure of the Mother of God in the southern tower chapel, dating from around 1460.

The church was last renovated in 1986.

**Guided tours can be booked with:**  
Group tours are conducted by  
Richard Hellmeier  
Church guide  
Phone 08074/1293  
or through the parish office

properties.name: Bronzezeit-Bayern Museum Kranzberg (Bronze Age Bavaria Museum Kranzberg)
properties.description: Ein freundlich lächelndes Gesicht auf einem Bernstein repräsentiert im Museum in Kranzberg das „erste goldene Zeitalter der Menschheit“ – die Bronzezeit. Funde aus dem Ortsteil Bernstorf, wo die mit ca. 13 ha größte bronzezeitliche Befestigungsanlage nördlich der Alpen entdeckt wurde, zeichnen ein beeindruckendes Bild des 14. vorchristlichen Jahrhunderts. Die dort aufgefundenen Gold- und Bernsteinobjekte aus dem östlichen Mittelmeerraum revolutionieren unsere Vorstellungen von dieser Zeit. Erlebbar wird dies v. a. medial: Virtuelle Idealrekonstruktionen lassen die Welt von vor 3500 Jahren wieder auferstehen.

properties.name: Wurmannsquick Observatory – Experience Astronomy
properties.description: Just outside the gates of the market town of Wurmannsquick in the Lower Bavarian district of Rottal-Inn, the **Sternenfreunde Wurmannsquick e.V.** operate a modernly equipped observatory at an altitude of around 500 meters.

properties.name: Fuggerschloss Glött
properties.description: Anton Fugger had the castle built in the second half of the 16th century as a moated castle (construction began in 1550). Glött Castle remained in the Fugger family's possession until 1869 and then passed by purchase to the Regens Wagner Foundation, which established a medical and care facility there. Today, the Regens Wagner Glött disability facility has 118 residential places. The castle is closed to the public and can therefore only be viewed from the outside.

properties.name: Gern Castle Estate
properties.description: Die **Hofmark Gern** war seit jeher ein **wichtiges Handels und Wirtschaftszentrum für die Region**. Eine Tradition, die auch in Zukunft fortgesetzt werden soll.

properties.name: Parish Church of St. Nicholas, Oberthürheim
properties.description: The magnificent village church in Oberthürheim was built in 1683. On a visit, one should take note of the Baroque interior and the late Gothic figures, especially the Madonna with Child (1470). The Stations of the Cross paintings from 1720 come from the demolished Fultenbach Monastery. About 500 meters away is the Linden Chapel (1756).

properties.name: Church of the Assumption of Mary in Antwort
properties.description:
From a church account from 1538, we know that the church in “Antvurti” has existed since 924. The Church of Antwort has long been visited as a place of grace for the “Pilgrimage of Our Lady in the Valley.” The present Baroque building was consecrated in 1679 by Prince-Bishop Sigismund Carl Count von Castelbarco. During the renovation in 1948, the interior coloring of the 18th century (Rococo, Lorenz Sciasca) was restored and the ceiling paintings by Joseph Adam Mölck from 1747 were uncovered. The tower and façade were also renovated.

Church weddings are possible here.

properties.name: Altes Schloss Schleißheim - "Das Gottesjahr und seine Feste" - Ökumenische Sammlung Gertrud Weinhold (Old Schleißheim Castle - "The Year of God and its Festivals" - Ecumenical Collection Gertrud Weinhold)
properties.description: In the original presentation of the collection of Prof. E. h. Gertrud Weinhold (1899-1992), which has remained unchanged until now, a "universal atlas" of religious festivals and everyday cultures around the globe is opened up. More than 6000 objects, collected on countless journeys, document the calendar festivals of the religious year as well as their traditions and customary objects in a worldwide comparison. Gertrud Weinhold's achievement is the first supranational documentation of religious folk cultures. The result is an ecumenical presentation of the religious festivals developed on the basis of the Holy Scriptures, with a comparative view of the ceremonies and means of devotion of the neighbouring religions of Judaism, Islam and Buddhism.

properties.name: Die Barockkrippe von Frauenwörth
properties.description:
The "Great Baroque Nativity Scene" of [Frauenwörth Monastery on Fraueninsel](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/alle-sehenswuerdigkeiten/kloster-frauenwoerth-auf-der-fraueninsel-d53e104ab1) is considered one of the oldest nativity scenes in southern Germany. As can be seen from the diary of Abbess Magdalena Haidenbucher (1606–1650), she had the figures, which were already present in the convent nativity scene at the time, set up for the first time at Christmas 1627 in the Apostles' Chapel (today Irmengard Chapel) in the minster.

As a result of secularization, whose reach the figures fortunately escaped, no archival records of the oldest nativity scenes in southern Germany have survived that would indicate the origin of the wood carvings.

The figures are up to 80 centimeters tall. The splendid and valuable fabrics and garments were undoubtedly made in the monastery itself. Among the figures still preserved today, the Christ Child, Mary and Joseph, three shepherds, four prophets, and three angels belong to the oldest stock.

The figure of the "dancing little Jesus of Frauenwörth" is a special feature. It dances toward the Three Wise Men in the scene of adoration, with its hand raised as a sign of peace, on a wave of Lake Chiemsee.

The nativity scene is usually set up in the period between Christmas and Candlemas (February 2). [Current dates and guided tours >>](https://www.frauenwoerth.de/blog/categories/termine)

properties.name: Glockenschmiede - Hammerschmiede-Museum (Bell Smithy - Hammersmith Museum)
properties.description: Ein Wasserrad mit 3,80 m Durchmesser betreibt das alte Hammerwerk mit seinen drei schweren Schwanzhämmern. Kuhglocken waren das Hauptprodukt der Glockenschmiede, aber auch Werkzeuge wurden hier gefertigt und geschliffen. Wie, das kann man heute noch sehen in einer der letzten Hammerschmieden Bayerns. Mitte des 17. Jh. erstmals erwähnt, steht sie bereits seit 1936 unter Denkmalschutz und war bis 1958 in Betrieb. Zum 100. Geburtstag des letzten Meisters entstand eine Dauerausstellung über Geschichte, Technik und Produkte der Schmiede. Ein Originalfilm von 1955 über den letzten Kuhglockenauftrag zeigt die Arbeitswelt der damaligen Zeit. Schon in den 1950er Jahren kamen Touristen in die Glockenschmiede. Für sie wurden damals Reiseandenken geschmiedet, wie man sie auch heute noch hier erwerben kann.

properties.name: Stein Rock Castle with Brewery
properties.description:
The wild robber knight Heinz von Stein, who once inhabited the castle, was feared far beyond the borders of Stein for his misdeeds.

On a guided tour, visitors learn all about the tragic end of the young Waldtraud and the secret of the deep well.

An exhibition also offers insight into the world of the noble family "Leuchtenberg," which resided here for some time.

The castle can only be visited as part of a guided tour.

Those who wish can then take part in a beer tasting at Stein Brewery, right next door.

Guided tours

Guided tours run from early April to the end of October and last about 1.5 hours. The rock castle is not accessible for people with disabilities. Further information [here](https://www.steiner-bier.de/fuehrungen/#/).

properties.name: Heimatkundliche Sammlung im Heimathaus
properties.description: Visitors to the Heimathaus can see tools used in agriculture and for processing wood and flax, Pfronten's most important sources of income in the past. Housing and household objects are also on display, as well as products from the precision engineering industry, which was very important for the region.

properties.name: Pfarrkirche St. Michael in Großhöhenrain
properties.description:
Die St. Michaelskirche in Großhöhenrain wurde im spätgotischem Stil erbaut. Im Jahre 1682 brannte die Kirche jedoch ab und ein Neubau war notwendig. Durch diesen Neubau wurde das Innere im Barock Stil gehalten, welcher aber nach einer Restaurierung wieder dem spätgotischen Stil gewichen ist. Eine besonders wertvolle Arbeit in der Kirche ist der Epitah des Hans Heinrich von Taufkirchen mit seiner Familie, welche im Stil der Renaissance angefertigt wurde.

Quelle:   

Helmut Giese: Bruckmühl und Umgebung - Ein Heimatbuch. Bruckmühl, 2006

properties.name: Vorgeschichtliches Erlebnisdorf ALCMONA (Prehistoric adventure village ALCMONA)
properties.description: The ALCMONA adventure village is a station of the Altmühltal Archaeological Park (APA), which stretches from Kelheim to Dietfurt over a length of almost 40 km. Archaeological excavations have proven that the area around Dietfurt has been continuously inhabited since the Stone Age. The Alcmona Association has so far reconstructed a Bronze Age longhouse according to local findings on a site next to the old Ludwig-Danube-Main Canal.

properties.name: Kunstmuseum Walter
properties.description: The Kunstmuseum Walter im Glaspalast (Walter Art Museum in the Glass Palace) is a privately run museum dedicated to modern and contemporary art. With no public funding, its collection of over 1,600 works invites visitors on a fascinating journey through the art history of the 20th and 21st centuries. Works from Germany, Europe and America are presented with a special focus on the art of the world-famous Leipzig School. In addition to this unique collection, the museum also exhibits important works of classical modernism from the first half of the 20th century. The Walter Collection brings the juxtaposition of Eastern and Western art to life in the extraordinary architecture of the historic glass palace with its high, light-flooded rooms. Here, the works of art are shown to their best advantage in an impressive way and invite visitors to enjoy an exciting tour.

properties.name: Georg Brenninger - Open-Air Museum
properties.description:
In Brasilien und in Brüssel, in berühmten Sammlungen und Museen, auf den öffentlichen Plätzen der großen Städte stehen die Skulpturen des Bildhauers Georg Brenninger. Die meisten und wohl auch eindrucksvollsten seiner Werke befinden sich in Velden an der Vils. Man kann schon von einem Brenninger-Freilicht-Museum sprechen.

In Velden ist Georg Brenninger 1909 geboren und aufgewachsen, dort liegen seine Wurzeln, aus denen er zeitlebens Kraft und Energie schöpfte. Er war eng verwachsen mit der Landschaft seiner Heimat, den fruchtbaren Äckern und Wiesen, den Wegen und Straßen mit alten Bäumen, den Wäldern, Tälern und sanften Hügeln.

Im Rathaus und dem Heimatmuseum erhalten Sie eine Begleitbroschüre, mit deren Hilfe Sie die Kunstwerke identifizieren und erkunden können.

properties.name: Museum Maxhütten Bergen (Maxhütten Museum)
properties.description: The Maxhütte Bergen, formerly the largest and most important ironworks in Bavaria, was founded as early as 1561. Many businesses (hammer smiths, wire makers, nail smiths) were established in its vicinity and provided a livelihood for around 1000 people. The museum presents the history of the ironworks in a vivid way. It explains how iron was extracted and processed and shows how people lived and worked here.

properties.name: Schöllkopf Lido Prien
properties.description:
Insiders claim that the Schöllkopf lido between Prien and Bernau is the most beautiful place to swim in Prien and the surrounding area.

Quiet, peaceful, and equipped with large, shady sunbathing lawns, the natural Chiemsee bathing area at Schöllkopf presents itself in summer. The kiosk team serves guests refreshing drinks, ice cream, light snacks, coffee, and homemade cake on the terrace.

- Changing rooms and toilets
- Parking spaces
- Dogs (on a leash) allowed

### Water temperature and water quality

[Results of the tests according to the Bavarian Bathing Water Ordinance >>](https://www.landkreis-rosenheim.de/Default.asp?rq_AppGuid=D53E3617FFC7C16729E9ABD3CE049BFAE5B2C888&rq_TargetPageGuid=EF40C39012B45281205707FA16808A31105D1936&rq_RecId=31323432&rq_MenuGuid=D0173D02C59B463759AD075F28C3C4704624C523&rq_TemplateKey=73746167655F6170706D61696E#%7B1%7D)

properties.name: Roman villa
properties.description:
Im Jahr 1934 wurden am Fuße des Tegelbergs die ersten Überreste einer römischen Villa rustica entdeckt – eines ausgedehnten Gutshofes, der um die Mitte des 2. Jahrhunderts n. Chr. gegründet wurde.

Weitere bedeutende Funde kamen 1966 beim Bau der Talstation der Tegelbergbahn sowie 1996 während der Arbeiten an der Sommerrodelbahn ans Licht.

Die Anlage zählt zu den eindrucksvollsten Zeugnissen römischer Besiedlung im Alpenvorland.

Ein besonderes Merkmal der Villa rustica war das Privatbad, wie es in ländlichen römischen Gutshöfen durchaus üblich war. Herausragend ist das hypocaustum, das römische Fußbodenheizsystem: Heißluft wurde in einem Hohlraum unter dem Fußboden erzeugt und zirkulierte durch röhrenförmige Ziegel in den Wänden nach oben. Dieses ausgeklügelte Heizsystem sorgte für ein angenehmes Raumklima und zeugt vom hohen technischen Niveau römischer Baukunst.

Besondere Aufmerksamkeit erregten die bei den Ausgrabungen geborgenen Fragmente von farbigem Wandverputz. Trotz des Einsturzes des Gebäudes blieben viele dieser Fresken außergewöhnlich gut erhalten und konnten erfolgreich restauriert werden. Sie geben einen faszinierenden Einblick in die Gestaltung römischer Innenräume und haben der Römervilla weit über Bayern hinaus Bekanntheit verschafft.

properties.name: The New Historical Ground
properties.description: Der Neue Geschichtsboden ist ein Raum für Heimat, Identität, Geschichte und Baukultur.

properties.name: Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary, Bad Aibling
properties.description:
Die Pfarrkirche Mariä Himmelfahrt ist auf einem Hügel erbaut und steht damit hoch übern den Dächern Bad Aiblings. Mittels Stufen von der Innenstadt kommend, einer Brücke oder über den Hofberg gelangt man zur Kirche. Ein Großteil der Kirche stammt aus dem frühen 15. Jahrhundert. Bis zum Ende des 15. Jahrhunderts war der Pfarrsitz noch in Ellmosen, einem Ortsteil von Bad Aibling. Doch seit über 500 Jahren ist dieser direkt neben der Kirche auf dem Hofberg angesiedelt. Die erste Renovierung wurde im Jahre 1663 durchgeführt, die letzte sowie umfassende Renovierung fand 2018 statt.

Vor dem 18. Jahrhundert waren Kreuzwege nur in den Kirchen der Franziskaner gestattet. Doch als Papst Innozenz XII. die Ausstattung der Kirchen mit Kreuzwegen gestattete, beauftragte im Jahre 1734 der damalige Pfarrer Dinzenhofer den Maler Hans Höttinger den noch heute in der Kirche befindlichen Kreuzweg anzufertigen. Da die Bevölkerungszahl von Bad Aibling immer mehr anstieg, wurde die Kirche auf Rat des berühmten Münchener Stadtbaumeisters Johann Michael Fischer gen Westen verlängern. In den Jahren 1754 und 1755 wurde dies durch den Maurermeister Abraham Miller von Hausstatt verwirklicht. Die gotischen Gewölberippen wichen dem Gewand des Rokoko.

Messezeiten:

Dienstag: 9:00 Uhr Heilige Messe  
Freitag: 9:00 Uhr Heilige Messe  
Samstag: 18:15 Uhr Rosenkranz / Anbetung / Beichtgelegenheit  
Samstag: 19:00 Uhr Vorabendgottesdienst  
Sonntag: 10:00 Uhr Eucharistiefeier

[Weitere Infos und Termine hier >>](https://www.erzbistum-muenchen.de/Stadtkirche-Bad-Aibling/Page061641.aspx)

**Öffnungszeiten:**

täglich von 08:00 - 18:00 Uhr

properties.name: Archaeological Museum in the Local History Museum Essenbach
properties.description:
Im Heimathaus in Essenbach wird den Besuchern ein Querschnitt durch die fast 7.500 Jahre alte Besiedlungsgeschichte des mittleren Isartales geboten.  

Über 300 archäologische Fundstücke aus dem Gemeindegebiet werden dort bewahrt.

properties.name: Stadtpfarrkirche St. Nikolaus und St. Stephan in Eggenfelden
properties.description:
"Cathedral of the Rottal" is the name given to the magnificent and imposing church from the late Gothic period.

The tower of this important sacred building rises far above the houses of the charming town square.

properties.name: Franz-Jürgen Habben Studio House
properties.description:
Habben's **themes** are becoming and passing away, life, love, but also downfall and death. A hymn, a thanksgiving for the miracle of life.

Franz Habben wants to interpret all facets of life, of ideas, and of the soul with his means of form and color, sometimes also with words, while remaining open to every possible interpretation.

Some images create the impression of apocalyptic visions, such as a major work from the "Trojan Cycle" of 1985 with the symbolic title "Troy Is Still Burning." The symbolism of such images is more relevant today than ever, for they conceal the fears of our time that affect us all.

Harald Wiese puts it succinctly when he says: "These are sacred images, altarpieces, for which there are not yet any churches."

With their powerfully colorful visual language, they lead the viewer into a fantastic, unreal world that can only be grasped through reason and feeling. The most varied pictorial means of expression complement one another through the movement, change, and dynamism captured on the painting surface.

properties.name: Kreisheimatstube (Kreisheimatstube)
properties.description: Faithfully renovated and furnished buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries invite visitors to explore the former way of life of farming families in central Swabia. During the tour, old furniture, equipment and objects are explained in their original context and in some cases their function is demonstrated.

properties.name: Hörpfad im Lohwald Neusäss
properties.description: The town of Neusäß, in cooperation with the Augsburg Office for Food, Agriculture and Forestry, has created an audio trail through the Lohwald. At a total of ten stations, children and adults can learn interesting and curious facts about the theme of the forest.

properties.name: Augsburger Dom
properties.description:
Wo heute der romanisch-gotische Dom Mariä Heimsuchung  
aufragt, standen noch im 5. Jahrhundert n. Chr. Wohnhäuser des römischen Augsburg. Eine erste Kirche wurde dort zwischen dem 5. und dem 8. Jahrhundert errichtet.

Bischof Simpert ließ einen im Jahr 807 geweihten karolingischen Neubau errichten. Die romanische Simpertkrypta ist eine der Hauptsehenswürdigkeiten des Doms.

Weil die Bischofskirche um das Jahr 994 eingestürzt war, wurde der romanische, damals noch nach Westen ausgerichtete Dom neu errichtet und 1065 geweiht.

Fünf Prophetenfenster aus dieser Zeit sind Relikte des ältesten bekannte figürlichen Glasmalereizyklus der Welt.

Erst im 14. Jahrhundert wurde der Dom nach Osten hin ausgerichtet: In mehr als hundertjähriger Bauzeit entstand der 1431 geweihte Ostchor.

Um 1350 erhielt dieser Neubau zwei Figurenportale.

Das südseitige Marienportal ist das figurenreichste Portal des 14. Jahrhunderts.

Am (weitgehend rekonstruierten) Nordportal findet man auch eine Darstellung Bischof Ulrichs sowie der Kaiserin Adelheid.

Ein Höhepunkt der barocken Ausstattung im Dom ist die Figur des Geißelheilands: ein Werk des Bildhauers Georg Petel, des „deutschen Michelangelo“.

Nirgendwo in Deutschland sieht man derart viele hochrangige Grabdenkmäler wie im Kreuzgang am Mariendom – 401 Epitaphe und Grabplatten aus der Zeit um 1350 bis 1800.

properties.name: Staatsgalerie in der Burg Burghausen
properties.description: The Bavarian State Painting Collections have set up a branch gallery on the 2nd and 3rd floors of the Palas of the main castle. The selection of 56 paintings deliberately refers to their location: on display are 15th- and 16th-century pictorial works from southern Germany or Bavaria and neighbouring Austria, as well as several large-format paintings on the history of the Bavarian dukes from the cycle of pictures painted by the Munich master Hans Werl († 1608) for the Old Hercules Hall of the Residenz in Munich. Sculptural works from the holdings of the Bayerisches National Museum (Bavarian National Museum) complement the exhibition.

properties.name: St. Vigilius Church in Kirchdorf a.H.
properties.description:
The 750th anniversary of St. Vigilius Parish Church was celebrated in autumn 2008. Accordingly, the church was founded in the mid-13th century, more precisely as the first wooden building around 1250 and as a consecrated church in 1258. At that time, Kirchdorf near Bruckmühl was appointed parish of Rott am Inn Monastery. Since a devastating fire raged in the 15th century, only the church tower has survived from the founding period. In 1470, the church was rebuilt in the Gothic style on the instructions of the nobleman Hanns von Holnstain. His tomb can still be found there today, a life-size likeness of the nobleman carved into a marble slab in the church. Although St. Vigilius Church, like many churches, was also baroquized, the wooden figures from the 15th century on the altars were preserved. At the end of the 19th century, the church underwent another stylistic transformation, back to Gothic, and received the tall, pointed church tower.

The old village cemetery is located right next to the church. The "new" cemetery, however, which was already laid out before the First World War, is a short distance away from the church.

properties.name: Mesner Gartl Hirnsberg
properties.description:
The “Mesner Gartl” is a real insider tip in idyllic Hirnsberg, the Golden Village of 2016. The place is beautifully situated at an elevated location on the eastern edge of Lake Simssee. The local parish church of the Assumption of Mary was built from the Marian chapel of the former Castle Hirnsberg, which existed until the 14th century. The village of Hirnsberg emerged from the Meuerhof near Castle Hirnsberg.

The garden is located not far from the parish church. In order to honor the plants mentioned in the Old and New Testaments, some of the plant species were planted in the Mesner Gartl in cooperation with botanists: a colorful variety and, in the warm months, a beautiful abundance of blossoms. The biblical plants of the Holy Land were very important to people in everyday life back then—and often still are today.

The year-round and winter-hardy flora includes grapevines, walnut and apple trees, barley, flax, field flowers, common poppy, corn chamomile, milk thistle, rue, coriander, black mustard, mandrake, broom, roses, leeks, onions, garlic, and horse mint. The non-winter-hardy botanicals include the date palm, olive tree, pomegranate, aloe vera, carob tree, fig, myrrh, frankincense bush, and many others.

properties.name: Wallfahrtskirche St. Erasmus in Heiligenberg
properties.description: In the middle of a small hamlet stands the remarkable church complex dating from around 1500.

properties.name: Pertenstein Castle
properties.description:
#### History

Water castles like that of the Hofmark Pertenstein Castle, idyllically located on the Traun between Matzing and Traunwalchen, were once typical of the Chiemgau region. Pertenstein Castle has a long history dating back to the 13th century, when Perchta von Toerring zu Stein brought the building site into her marriage with Engelbrecht von Taching. Since then, the castle has seen turbulent times, was expanded into a stately country castle, and later fell almost into ruin.

It was not until 1969 that the "Heimatbund Schloss Pertenstein e.V." saved the castle from complete decay. Today it is maintained by the association in cooperation with the Bavarian State Office for Monument Preservation. The current owner, H.S.H. Count Ignaz zu Toerring-Jettenbach, has granted it to the association under hereditary lease. Under the motto "New life in old walls," the castle now serves as a cultural and event venue. The ensemble, consisting of the castle, stables building, tithe barn, and round hall, is a sought-after location for weddings, corporate events, concerts, and more.

The castle cannot be visited, but it can be rented for celebrations or events. In addition, events such as the arts and crafts market, concerts, or song recitals take place there.

properties.name: Radiomuseum (Radio Museum)
properties.description: Wehrmacht equipment, radio receivers, but above all radios from the 1920s to the 1960s, microphones, record players and tape recorders are on display at the private Radiomuseum (Radio Museum) in Rottenburg.

properties.name: Autobahnsee Augsburg
properties.description: Auch wenn der Name und die Nähe zur A8 viele Besucher abschreckt: Am Autobahnsee im Augsburger Osten ist Erholung angesagt. Großflächige Liegewiesen, schattenspendende Bäume und mehrere Grillplätze machen die Hektik des Alltags schnell vergessen. Auch für Schwimmer ist der Autobahnsee ein beliebtes Ziel – der Wasserwacht-Station und der ausgezeichneten Wasserqualität des EU-Badegewässers sei Dank

properties.name: St. John’s Branch Church, Vorderried
properties.description: Das kleine Kirchlein im Ortsteil Vorderried wurde 1680 erbaut und besticht mit einer hervorragenden Figurenausstattung: bedeutende Tonmadonna im Stil der Schönen Madonna, wohl eine Augsburger Arbeit (1410/20), und weitere spätgotische und barocke Figuren.

properties.name: Kunsthalle Augsburg im Glaspalast
properties.description: The Kunsthalle Augsburg (formerly H2 – The Center for Contemporary Art) on the ground floor of the Glaspalast is Augsburg's municipal museum for modern and contemporary art. Changing special exhibitions and collection presentations on 20th century art as well as contemporary art from a regional, national and international context are shown in two halls (H1 and H2) on an area totaling 2,700 square meters. Regular public guided tours and exhibition-accompanying events such as concerts, readings, artist talks or panel discussions complement the program. The museum is directed by Jan T. Wilms.

properties.name: Museum Salz und Moor im Klaushäusl (Salt & Moor Museum)
properties.description: Das in Salzbergwerken gewonnene salzhaltige Wasser, die Sole, wurde seit dem 17. Jh. in Rohrleitungen zur Weiterverarbeitung in Salinen geleitet. Das „Klaushäusl“ von 1810 liegt in der Nähe des Chiemsees und ist die einzige vollständig erhaltene Pumpstation an der 107 km langen Soleleitung von Berchtesgaden nach Rosenheim. Im Mittelpunkt steht die originale Reichenbach’sche Wassersäulenmaschine, die 150 Jahre lang in Betrieb war. Im Brunnwartshaus informiert eine Dauerausstellung über die Natur- und Kulturgeschichte des nahe gelegenen Hochmoores „Kendlmühlfilzen“.

properties.name: Parish Church of the Holy Blood, Landshut
properties.description: Die Kirche geht zurück bis in die Zeit der Christianisierung im 8. Jahrhundert. Die spätgotische Kirche ist durch ihre in Altbayern einzigartigen Rundtürme bekannt. Von den barocken, klassizistischen und neugotischen Umgestaltungen blieben verschiedene wertvolle Einzelstücke in der Ausstattung erhalten.

properties.name: Lenbach-Museum
properties.description: It was an unprecedented career. Who would have guessed in 1836 that little Franz, the 13th child of a master bricklayer from Schrobenhausen, would one day rise to become a famous "painter prince"? Franz v. Lenbach (1836-1904) was one of the most important German portrait painters of the late 19th century. He painted emperors and popes, many princes and important entrepreneurs of the Gründerzeit - and not least countless female beauties. With around 500 paintings, sketches and drawings, the museum in his birthplace houses the largest collection on Franz v. Lenbach. It ranges from his artistic beginnings in 1851 to his later creative period in Munich and thus provides an excellent overview of the artist's development. Two rooms on the ground floor of the Lenbach-Museum are dedicated to Lenbach's friend and early teacher, the painter Johann Baptist Hofner (1832-1913), who became famous for his animal paintings.

properties.name: Branch Church "St. James the Elder and St. Stephen" in Ottershausen
properties.description: Right on the wild, romantic banks of the Amper, the small village church rises from the floodplain landscape and overlooks the village square and maypole of the still agriculturally shaped village of Ottershausen in the southeastern Dachau district.

properties.name: WasserWertSchätzen Knowledge Center
properties.description:
The WasserWertSchätzen Knowledge Center in Rottenburg an der Laaber offers a wealth of water knowledge for young and old alike.

From well drilling to the water footprint – everything here revolves around our drinking water and how to protect it.

properties.name: St. Peter's branch church
properties.description: A late Gothic building with wall and ceiling paintings from the 15th century and carved figures from the 15th and 16th centuries. One of the handsome churches of the Wasserburg region.

properties.name: Parish Church "Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary" Unterhausen
properties.description: Die Kirche in Unterhausen birgt Bilder des Glaubens, die einen Besuch wert sind. Der Hochaltar ist geprägt von einer Madonna, die Hans Degler 1621 geschaffen hat. Das Patrozinium erinnert an die Begegnung von Maria und Elisabeth, im Deckengemälde von Johann Baptist Baader (1773) dargestellt.

properties.name: Borstei-Museum (Borstei Museum)
properties.description: "The home consolidates peace in the family, which is the foundation for peace in the state," was the credo of the founder of the Borstei housing estate, Senator Bernhard Borst, who completed it in 1929. The small museum documents his life's work and the history of Borstei. The large parks of the listed settlement have over 60 works of art that can also be visited.

properties.name: Wallfahrtsmuseum Wieskirche (Wieskirche pilgrimage museum)
properties.description: "Here dwells happiness, here the heart finds peace", said the church's builder, Abbot Marianus II Mayer. However, it was certainly rarely really quiet here, after all, an immense stream of pilgrims to the "Scourged Saviour on the Wies" was the reason for building the church. And even today, the Wieskirche, a rococo jewel and World Heritage Site, built between 1746 and 1754 according to plans by Dominikus Zimmermann, is a popular destination for pilgrims and tourists. Things are a little more tranquil in the pilgrimage museum in the adjoining prelate's house. Here, confirmations of indulgences or requests to "touch" the miraculous image, miracle books, devotional objects, devotional and votive pictures as well as objects from the Brotherhood of the Scourged Saviour document the origins and development of the pilgrimage.

properties.name: Diabetesmuseum München (Diabetes Museum Munich)
properties.description: Auf 23 qm präsentiert Familie Neumann ihre umfangreiche Sammlung zum Thema Diabetes mellitus und ermöglicht so eine Zeitreise durch die Geschichte der Zuckerkrankheit.

properties.name: Feichteck
properties.description:
Various routes lead to the scenic summit, and they are among the easier mountain hikes. Its location offers views of neighboring peaks such as Spitzstein and [Hochries](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/alle-sehenswuerdigkeiten/hochries-29637ec6dd), to the south of the Kaiser Mountains, and on the ascent also repeatedly of Lake Chiemsee and Rosenheim.

**Our tip:** An after-work tour to Feichteck! The summit of Feichteck is a place where the sun sets, and at dusk you can see the sea of lights all the way to Munich.

[Webcam from Hochries toward Feichteck >>](https://www.foto-webcam.eu/webcam/hochries-sued/)

### Alpine huts:

[Feichteck Alm >>](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/essen-trinken/gastronomie/feichteck-alm-715ebc1977)

[Wagneralm >>](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/essen-trinken/gastronomie/wagneralm-083b4c18e9)

[Snowshoe tour to Feichteck >>](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/tourenportal/schneeschuhfeichteck-im-chiemgau-e955ced76d)

[Mountain tour to Pölcherschneid >>](https://www.chiemsee-alpenland.de/entdecken/tourenportal/samerberg-zur-poelcherschneid-rundweg-nr.-34-6270351225)
