Das hier gemeinschaftlich gebackene Brot konnte, zu einem günstigen Preis, an die Not leidende Bevölkerung verteilt werden.

Sehr schnell griffen die Idee des „Backhaus samt Backhausverein“ benachbarte Orte im ganzen Westerwald, im Lahn-Dill-Bergland und dem Burgwald bis zur Schwalm auf.

So finden sich heute viele Backhäuser, deren Grundsteinlegung in derselben Epoche erfolgte.

Die Kunst des guten Brotbackens im Backhaus erforderte schon immer ein hohes Maß an Erfahrung und war gemeinschaftsprägend.

Es begann schon bei der Auswahl und des Schlagens des geeigneten Holzes, dem nächtlichen Anheizen des Ofens und der Festlegung der Backreihenfolge.

Diese wurde von der Backhausgemeinschaft im Vorfeld festgelegt, oft entschied das Los.

Der Brotteig selbst wurde in der Regel nach hauseigenem Rezept individuell im Vorfeld hergestellt und zum Backhaus getragen.

Entscheidend für das gute Gelingen war nicht nur die Auswahl des Mehles, sondern insbesondere auch die Temperatur, bei der die Brotlaibe mit dem Schieber in den Ofen geschoben wurden.

Die Zeit, in der das Brot im Ofen verweilte, wurde zum kommunikativen Austausch der „Backesbäcker/innen“ untereinander genutzt und war daher für den dörflichen Zusammenhalt von wichtiger Bedeutung.

Dieses traditionelle, dörfliche Backhauswesen war fast von der Mitte des 19. bis in jene des 20. Jahrhunderts fester Bestandteil der örtlichen Versorgung.

Durch die technische Entwicklung besaßen seit Mitte der 1950iger Jahre viele Haushalte einen eigenen elektrischen Backofen, sodass das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Backhäusern mehr und mehr an Bedeutung verlor.

Insbesondere in den 60iger Jahren wurden viel Backhäuser abgerissen.

Bis heute jedoch bestehen noch immer zahlreiche Backhäuser und Backhausvereine mit einer oftmals langen, ungebrochenen Tradition bis in die Gegenwart hinein, die in altbewährter Weise backen und die Dorfgemeinschaft pflegen.

Gegenwärtig erlebt das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Hessen eine Wiedergeburt.

properties.name: Alter Bahnhof Ulm
properties.description:
The Ulmtalbahn ran along the route of today's Ulmtal Cycle Path in the last century. Between 1921 and 1976, it operated as the legendary Balkan Express from Stockhausen (Lahn) to Beilstein (Dillkreis) and back. Steam locomotives and rail buses transported passengers and local raw materials over a considerable height difference of 245 m.

The rugged landscape of the Westerwald, into which the workers skillfully fitted the tracks, perhaps reminded one of the character of the Balkans in Southern Europe (Karl May: “Through Wild Kurdistan”). Thus the Ulmtalbahn received its name "Balkan Express."

The route of the Ulmtalbahn is now used for the approximately 21 km long Ulmtal Cycle Path. The covered rest area is modeled after the original waiting hall of the Ulm Station, where no tickets were sold but which provided travelers with protection from wind and weather. Today, the waiting shelter serves the same purpose for cyclists and hikers. In good weather, the nearby picnic area is a brilliant rest stop with beautiful views.

properties.name: Backhaus Elnhausen
properties.description:
Under the stewardship of the local heritage and cultural association, the bakehouse has proven itself as the center of village life at the very spot where a bakehouse was already built in 1891.

Today, it is mainly fired up and used for baking during village festivals. In the past, the order in which villagers baked their goods before each baking session was determined by lot: the person who was allowed to load the oven first had to pay particular attention to ensure that the breads and cakes did not become too dark in the oven, which was very hot at the start. The last person in line had to expect a correspondingly longer baking time.

properties.name: Sack pipe with Kaiser Wilhelm tower
properties.description:
At 674 metres, the Sackpfeife, Biedenkopf's local mountain, is the highest elevation in the Marburg-Biedenkopf district and one of the most beautiful vantage points. 

From the platform of the observation tower, you have a marvellous panoramic view over the mountain ranges of the slate mountains, the Marburg highlands and - on a clear day - even as far as the Taunus. Next to the tower is a hiking hut run by the Oberhessischer Gebirgs- und Wanderverein. The Sackpfeife is a wonderful place to hike and then take a break at one of the barbecue areas, relax and prepare a cosy meal.

properties.name: Jewish Community Marburg | New Synagogue
properties.description:
Since the beginning of 2003, the Jewish community of Marburg has had a new home in Liebigstraße in Marburg's southern neighbourhood.

Today, the synagogue and cultural centre of the Jewish community provide enough space for community life and for the diverse cultural offerings of the community.

After all, Judaism is not just a religion, but one of the oldest cultures in the world.

And the new community centre is also intended as a place of encounter and togetherness to help communicate more about it.

Barrier-free access to the building is also possible with the help of a lift at the rear of the building.

properties.name: Vogelschutzgebiet NATURA 2000 | Martinsweiher
properties.description:
The area is designated as a landscape conservation area and, with its diverse habitats in an otherwise intensively utilised cultural landscape, serves as a refuge for native resident and migratory bird species. Situated on a major trans-European bird migration route, the ponds act as resting places for migratory birds, which can rest and feed here. In recent years, around 420 bird species have been recorded here by an active ornithological scene.

Would you like to explore the bird sanctuary by bike? Then head to the themed cycle route [Höfe-Radeln](https://www.marburg-tourismus.de/radfahren#bm=oac%3Asummer&cat=Radtour&filter=r-fullyTranslatedLangus-,r-onlyOpened-,sb-sortedBy-0&ipd=59167879&ov=cycling)!

properties.name: Backhaus Rodenroth
properties.description:
The origins of today's Hessian bakehouses date back to the middle of the 16th century: Count Johann VI of Nassau-Dillenburg decreed in the "Wood and Forest Ordinance" of 18 January 1562: "In every village, several common baking ovens are to be decreed".

On the one hand, communal baking was intended to save wood, as resources were slowly becoming scarce in the region due to the immense consumption of wood, for example for iron smelting.

On the other hand, the fire risk for the farms, which were mostly built of wood, clay and straw, with their dwellings and stables, was reduced by a separate location of the now isolated bakehouses.

As a result of this ordinance, numerous village community bakehouses were built.

Due to the exchange of information - trade, marriage and itinerant trades - that went beyond the borders of the lordship, this advantageous model soon became popular throughout Hesse.

In the mid-19th century, communal bakehouse culture experienced a renaissance, starting in the then Prussian provinces in what are now Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse.

In 1846/1847, crop failures caused great hardship throughout Europe, including in the Kingdom of Prussia, which included the small town of Weyerbusch in the Westerwald.

When the government issued flour, mayor Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen - who is also considered the founding father of the cooperative system - initiated a "bread association".

The allotted flour was processed in a specially built bakehouse.

The bread baked here could be distributed to the needy population at a favourable price.

Neighbouring villages throughout the Westerwald, the Lahn-Dill mountains, the Burgwald and the Schwalm soon took up the idea of the "baking house and baking house association".

Today there are many bakehouses whose foundation stones were laid in the same era.

The art of baking good bread in a bakehouse has always required a great deal of experience and has been a community activity.

It began with the selection and cutting of suitable wood, the nightly heating of the oven and the determination of the baking sequence.

This was decided in advance by the baking community, often by lot.

The bread dough itself was usually made individually in advance according to a home recipe and carried to the bakehouse.

Not only the choice of flour, but also the temperature at which the loaves of bread were put into the oven with the pusher was decisive for good success.

The time during which the bread remained in the oven was used for communicative exchange among the "Backesbäcker/innen" and was therefore important for village cohesion.

This traditional village bakehouse system was an integral part of the local supply almost from the middle of the 19th century until the 20th century.

Due to technical developments, many households have had their own electric ovens since the mid-1950s, so that communal baking in bakehouses has become less and less important.

In the 1960s in particular, many bakehouses were demolished.

To this day, however, there are still numerous bakehouses and bakehouse associations, often with a long, unbroken tradition that continues into the present day, which bake in the time-honoured manner and cultivate the village community.

At present, communal baking is experiencing a rebirth in Hesse.

properties.name: Garbenheim – ein Wetzlarer Stadtteil
properties.description:
Der nahe an der Kernstadt gelegene Stadtteil Garbenheim wurde im Jahr 776 schon urkundlich erwähnt. Die mehr als tausenjährige Geschichte kann heute im Heimatmuseum angeschaut werden.  

Das Bauernhaus aus dem 19. Jahrhundert, das die Ausstellung beherbergt, befindet sich im alten Dorfkern, umgeben von einigen Fachwerkhäusern. Der Vorgängerbau samt Scheunen und Stallungen fiel dem großen Dorfbrand zum Opfer.  

Das Heimatmuseum gibt viel Wissenswertes über die Ur- und Frühgeschichte der Region, über die Arbeit der Landbevölkerung sowie der heimischen Handwerker und Bergleute samt ihrer Trachten und Gerätschaften preis.  

Vorbei an der evangelischen Kirche ist der Goetheplatz. Dieser Platz verweist mit seinem Denkmal auf den literaturgeschichtlichen Zufall, der Garbenheim in den Kreis der Schauplätze der Weltliteratur aufrücken ließ. Denn die ländliche Idylle Garbenheims fand auch bei Goethe Anerkennung, der hier gerne ausgedehnte Spaziergänge machte und den Ort unter dem literarischen Namen Wahlheim in sein Werk „Die Leiden des jungen Werthers“ mit aufnahm.  

Heute erinnert auf dem Goetheplatz eine lebensgroße Goethe-Bronze-Figur an den Dichter, die neben dem Heimatmuseum auch einen Teil des Wetzlarer Goethewegs darstellt.

properties.name: Naunheim – ein Wetzlarer Stadtteil
properties.description:
Naunheim is conveniently located with good bus connections, yet remains quiet on the right bank of the Lahn, and with its 275 hectares of forest it is Wetzlar’s most wooded district.

In the Naunheim area, excavations in recent years have uncovered remains of a Germanic settlement from Roman times. The Frankish settlement of Naunheim was first mentioned in 784 as “Niuuenheim.”

Characterizing the “Hiwwel,” as the people of Naunheim call the village center, are the church and the former school building, which now houses the district office. There is also the House of Local History, where changing exhibitions on local historical topics are presented.

Another building that can tell you a little about Naunheim’s history is the old ferryman’s cottage at the large Naunheim Lahn weir, which was built to house the ferryman. Until the construction of the iron footbridge at the beginning of the 20th century, the ferry was the only crossing over the Lahn.

Naunheim, which for centuries was shaped by small-scale farming, developed in the 20th century into a typical residential community with many leisure opportunities: in addition to cycling on the Lahn Cycle Route or boating on the Lahn, you can also climb the 261-meter Simberg and let your gaze wander over the picturesque Lahn Valley. Or simply enjoy the local recreation area on the Lahn Island.

 Katzenfurt Bakehouse 

 In 1836 a community bakehouse was built in the "Unterdorf" of Katzenfurt. Next to the bakehouse stood the "community cattle scales".  These cattle scales no longer exist today.  In 1996 the bakehouse was renovated by the "Backhausmähchern" (bakehouse mowers) in order to make it still usable for the population. Even today, some Katzenfurters bake breads, cakes, but also newfangled things like pizza etc. here.  In 2019, as part of a film project to document old village traditions, the Katzenfurt Local History Society organised a baking house festival at which cakes and bread from the baking house were offered.  The oven and interior are currently being renovated in order to keep the bakehouse usable in the future.

properties.name: Medieval synagogue
properties.description:
What a find! Unexpectedly, old walls were discovered during construction work in 1993. The medieval synagogue, first mentioned in 1317, had been buried for 550 years. Today you can see it above the market square under a glass cube: The remaining ruins of the ‘youngest’ of three buildings with basic dimensions of around 7 x 10 metres. Parts of the entrance area and the beginnings of a ribbed vault can still be clearly recognised. A preserved vault keystone shows a six-pointed star composed of flowers, the ‘Star of David’, as decoration. It is known from written sources that this building, known as the ‘Jewish school’, was demolished in 1452.

Would you like to experience the medieval synagogue in its original state in the 14th century before its destruction? With pleasure! Then head to Markt 23, grab a pair of 3D glasses and experience the building that no longer exists.

Guided tours on the topic of Jews in Marburg with a visit to the synagogue can be booked [here](https://www.marburg-tourismus.de/thekulfuehrung/de/tour/detail/RPT/00853839-54b5-4994-922e-0e44832629c2/juden_in_marburg).

Text: Naturpark Lahn-Dill-Bergland

Bakehouse Wissenbach 

Built in 1768 - as the third school building with a bakehouse on Altebach. The beautiful multi-storey half-timbered building survived two major fires in 1773 and 1879, which caused immense damage to the village. The "Backes" fulfilled various functions between 1879 and 1950. A schoolroom was used on the upper floor, and the teacher in charge also lived in a room. One floor below was the kindergarten.  The local prison was also located in the building and offered the inmates, mostly tramps, a warm place to stay, as the oven was located under the room. Even carpenters on their journey always found a warm place.   During the Second World War - in 1939 - one room was used to let undisciplined soldiers in prison - reflect on their misdemeanours. When the building could no longer be used as a school, it housed families seeking accommodation after fleeing. A community office was also set up in the "Ahl Schul". The rural women became active when the historic building was to be demolished. Supported by the local associations, they succeeded in preserving the centre of the village and it was completely renovated in 1979. The countrywomen took over the sponsorship. One of the two ovens was renovated in 1980.  The Backes was now used by the villagers to bake bread and cakes. Slate boards were used for the baking rules, which still hang in the bakehouse today. In 2014, a work group of today's countrywomen formed, cleared out the building and renovated a room - which is used by them for some activities. On the upper floor, the Eschenburg Regional Museum occupies a few rooms to store part of its collection and thus provide every museum visitor with a lively display about collections of local history.  The bread and cake baking tradition is continued by the countrywomen.

properties.name: Erzverladeanlage Ahausen
properties.description:
From 1830 onwards, iron ore was mined in the nearby **Allerheiligenstollen** by the Nieverner mining and smelting association. However, after reaching the groundwater level in 1885, production had to be halted.

The longest operating period began in 1928 when the Allerheiligen mine, now owned by the Buderus company, was reopened. The Ottostollen was renovated and a second exit was created to ensure the drainage of water. Thus, ore could be extracted until 1960 before production became unprofitable due to strong foreign competition.

From 1934 onward, small diesel locomotives transported the ore through the Ottostollen directly over the Ahäuser Bridge to the loading facility at Weilburg station. In 1936, a crushing and sorting facility was built to crush, process, and load the red iron ore. After the Ahäuser Bridge was destroyed in World War II, the ore was transported to Weilburg station by cableway. From 1955, transportation of the processed ore was carried out by truck for cost reasons, which diminished the significance of the loading facility.

Today, the loading facility has been restored by the **Heimatverein Ahausen e.V.** and documents the industrial past of the region.

properties.name: Tausendjährige Gerichts-Eiche
properties.description: The age of the English oak cannot be precisely determined. In popular belief, however, it was referred to as a 1000-year-old oak around 100 years ago. The oak is estimated to be 700 - 800 years old. The trunk is hollow and has several large openings, which are closed with cast-iron grilles. The oak was last renovated in the 1990s. The last measurement was taken in 2014 and it has a chest height circumference of a proud 8.10 metres. It is said to have been used as a court oak in the Middle Ages.

properties.name: Franz Erhard Walther - Fünf Raumformen im Barockviertel
properties.description:
Franz Erhard Walther (* 22. Juli 1939 in Fulda) ist ein deutscher Künstler (Bildhauer, Konzept-, Installations- und Prozesskünstler). Seit seiner Emeritierung als Professor an der Hochschule für bildende Künste in Hamburg lebt und arbeitet er wieder in Fulda. Seit einigen Jahren erfährt Walthers Werk eine zunehmende internationale Anerkennung. Er gilt mit seiner partizipativen Kunst als eine der Schlüsselfiguren der Gegenwartskunst.  

2017 wurde Franz Erhard Walther bei der Biennale di Venezia mit dem Goldenen Löwen als bester Künstler ausgezeichnet.  

Für seine Heimatstadt Fulda hat Franz Erhard Walther verschiedene Kunstwerke geschaffen, die im Stadtraum frei zugänglich sind:  

**5 Raumformen für Fulda**  
In den Jahren 1970/71 und 1993/94 entstanden die Raumformen für Fulda. An fünf Standorten wurden Stahlplatten mit Inschrift verlegt und nach sechs Richtungen ausgerichtet. Die Ortswahl wurde wesentlich durch die Gegebenheiten der Umgebung und den Blickachsen bestimmt, die durch die Leserichtung der auf den Platten eingravierten Worten definiert ist. Standorte der Raumformen im Barockviertel:

1. Vor dem Stadtschloss Fulda  
2. Domplatz (Rasenfläche)  
3. An der Michaelskirche (Rasenfläche)  
4. vor dem Paulustor (Rasenfläche)  
5. Frauenberg  

Tipp: Von allen Raumformen aus genießt du unerwartete Blicke auf die Barockstadt Fulda.  

**König-Konrad-Denkmal**  
Anlässlich der 1275-Jahr-Feier der Gründung des Klosters und damit der Stadt Fulda im Jahr 2019, bat Oberbürgermeister Dr. Heiko Wingenfeld den Künstler Franz Erhard Walther das Denkmal für König Konrad I. zu schaffen. Dieser regierte von 911 und 918 und wurde auf seinen Wunsch hin in der damaligen Stiftskirche begraben. Das auf dem Domplatz stehende Denkmal wurde im Dezember 2019 enthüllt. Der mächtige Sandsteinblock steht im gebührenden Abstand zum Dom und weist eine glänzend erscheinende Oberfläche auf. Zunächst wirkt er wie ein riesiges aufgestelltes Buch oder eine moderne Infotafel. Tritt man näher, erkennt man 911 vergoldete Plättchen, welche die Oberfläche des Objekts gliedern. Unten am Ende der Tafeln steht der Schriftzug Koenig Konrad 1 b7 911.  

**Bistumsarchiv**  
Einen Blick auf die zeitgenössische Architektur setzt das Gebäude des Bistumsarchiv, das etwas versteckt zwischen Michaelskirche, Generalvikariat und Dompfarrzentrum liegt. Eine Besonderheit ist die Inschrift "Die Ganzheit des Fragments", die von Franz Erhard Walther 2007 für dieses Gebäude geschaffen wurde.  

**Das sagt Franz Erhard Walther über seine Raumformen**  
abDie Maße der Platten sind auf den menschlichen Körper bezogen und haben daher eine Proportion. Proportion enthält auch die verwendete Antiquaschrift. Stahl wurde gewählt, da historisch mit Bedeutung beladene Materialien vermieden werden sollten.  

Die Werkform e28093 Fünf Raumformen für Fulda e28093 zog ich allen anderen Lösungen aus mehreren Gründen vor: Zuallererst deswegen, weil mir diese Form am unmittelbarsten meiner Forderung: WERK in der Handlung zu entwickeln am nächsten kam und tradierte Erwartungen enttäuschen würde.  

Darüber hinaus sah ich diese Arbeit als authentische Werkidee der Zeit, und sie enthielt wesentliche Merkmale meiner Gesamtarbeit: großräumige, auf den realen Raum bezogene Dimension, Realzeit, Werk in der Vorstellung, der Körper als Skulptur, offene Werkdefinition.bb

properties.name: Johannesberg Priory gardens
properties.description:
Barocke Kirche mit Schlossanlage und idyllischem Garten: Die Propstei Johannesberg ist ein geschichtsträchtiger Ort, dessen Anfänge bereits in der Karolingerzeit um 800 n. Chr. liegen. Johannesberg, ein südwestlich gelegener Stadtteil Fuldas, verwandelte sich vom einstigen Pilgerzentrum nach dem Dreißigjährigen Krieg zur Propstei und nach der Säkularisation im Jahr 1802 zur Staatsdomäne.  

Wer heute den Park der Propstei Johannesberg besucht, erlebt die historischen Bezüge der Bau- und Gartenkunst damaliger Zeiten hautnah. Symbolhafte Skulpturen, Sonnenuhren, Brunnen, ein Obelisk und Vasen zieren den Garten. Die Anlage gliedert sich in eine obere große Terrasse und nach Osten zur Fulda-Aue abfallend in weitere kleinere Terrassen und Böschungen. Hier und da schaffen Blickpunkte, sogenannte „points de vues“, Verbindungen zum Schloss Fasanerie in Eichenzell.  

Der Park der Propstei Johannesberg ist öffentlich zugänglich. Packe am besten eine Picknickdecke ein und mach es Dir auf einer der Terrassen gemütlich. Für Geschichtsinteressierte bietet sich außerdem der kostenfreie Audiowalk über die izi-TRAVEL-App an. 13 Stationen warten hier auf Dich. Plane etwa 75 Minuten für diesen Rundgang ein.

properties.name: Johannesberg Priory
properties.description:
Johannesberg Priory is located in southwest Fulda. Baroque renovations led to the creation of a palace-like complex in the 18th century. The buildings and gardens have been subject to extensive renovation and restoration works since 1984. Nowadays, Johannesberg Priory houses institutions that offer training and consultancy in the field of heritage conservation and the restoration of old buildings. A visit to the historical rooms in the red building, the gardens, the church, the workshops and the Johannesberg artisanry collection is included as part of the guided tours.

**Johannesberg artisanry collection**

The Johannesberg artisanry collection comprises multiple exhibition spaces presenting tools, workshops, restoration techniques and objects created by guilds. The artisanry collection is also home to one of the largest collections of model historical timber-framed houses from different regions in Germany. The objects were expertly crafted by hand over many years by model-builder Dieter Ehret from Hemsbach in Odenwald. Of the more than 50 models in the collection, around half can be seen in the permanent collection. The largest exhibit in the collection is a model of a building from Poland rather than Germany. It is a timber-framed peace church in Świdnica, which is believed to be the largest timber-framed church in Europe. The model measures 2.5 metres by 3.6 metres and is 1.5 metres tall. Open by request – bookings via contact below.

properties.name: Historical folding rule
properties.description:
Das Dorf Speckswinkel, an der ehemaligen wichtigen Handelsstraße die Langen Hessen gelegen, hat eine große historische Zoll-Tradition vorzuweisen. An die alte Zollstelle, den Zollerhof und die lange Zollgeschichte des Ortes wird heute durch das Bürgerhaus mit der historischen Bezeichnung „Zollhof“ und einer neuen aufwendigen Totalrekonstruktion eines hessischen Zollstocks aus dem Jahr 1751 in der Dorfmitte erinnert.  
Zollstöcke waren ein Symbol für das Zollregal, d.h. Gebietshoheit des Landesfürsten dem die Erhebung des Zolls zustand. Die Zollstöcke wurden an Handelsstraßen und möglichen Umgehungsstraßen an strategischen Stellen bis etwa Mitte des 18. Jahrhunderts errichtet, um u.a. auch bei Streitigkeiten die Rechte des Zollherrn zu dokumentieren. Im Bereich des Dorfes Speckswinkel gab es zwei solche Zollstöcke (hinter der Krücke und an der Bellnhauser Straße im Staatswald). Das Ignorieren durch Fuhr- und Kaufleute sowie Reisende hatte drastische Strafen zur Folge, wie die Entrichtung des dreifachen Zolls und er Beschlagnahme von Beförderungsmittel und Waren.  
Sie waren aus Sandstein gefertigt, der als sogenannter Marburger Bundsandstein aus den zahlreichen Steinbrüchen im Höhenzug der Lahnberge sowie aus dem Marburger Land kamen. Im Dach befand sich eine Richtungsmarkierung zur nächsten Zollstelle. In der Stele ist über dem fürstlichen Wappen deutlich die Bezeichnung „Landzoll“ zu erkennen, d. h. ein Passierzoll auf Transportmittel, Tiere und Waren, der erhoben wurde.  
Das fürstliche Wappen des Landgrafen von Hessen-Kassel konnte aus Bronzeguss oder wie in Speckswinkel aus einem eingearbeiteten Flachrelief bestehen.  
Original Zollstöcke als Kleindenkmäler gibt es in Deutschland nur sehr wenige, in Hessen keine.

properties.name: "Heinzelmannshöhlen" Caves on Baedecker's Rock Path
properties.description:
The wildly romantic rocky path high above Bad Ems along the rocks of the Bäderlei with ever new, grandiose views of the river landscape was already part of the standard tourist programme for spa guests in the 19th century.

On the way are the fascinating Heinzelmann Caves.

These are karstic tubes, a strange freak of nature around which countless legends entwine.

They were formed by lime erosion.

They fascinated the naturalist Senckenberg and Goethe's friend Lavater as early as the 18th century.

properties.name: Mariengrotto Momberg
properties.description:
The building visually resembles the grotto at the famous French Marian pilgrimage site of Lourdes at the foot of the Pyrenees.

A larger-than-life statue of the Mother of God is enthroned in a six-metre-high rock as the central figure.

properties.name: Old "Tavern at the river lahn"
properties.description:
In its almost 350-year history, the half-timbered house has offered many skippers and carters a safe place to stop for the night.

During the Thirty Years' War, the Wirtshaus an der Lahn catered for troops.

In the winter of 1814, General Blücher spent the night in the Wirtshaus an der Lahn.

An oak table from this period can still be found in the inn.

Goethe, who visited the inn more than half a dozen times between 1774 and 1815, carved his name on the tabletop of the oak table:

"Water alone makes you dumb - as the fish in the stream show.

Wine alone makes you stupid - see the gentlemen at the table.

Since I don't want to be either - I drink water with wine."

The saying was still legible on the tabletop, which was protected by a glass plate, until 1935.

Goethe had previously been sitting at the table drinking wine spritzers, which is why he was ridiculed by the gentlemen sitting at the neighbouring table.

properties.name: The convent garden of St Mary’s Abbey
properties.description:
The convent garden of the Benedictine St Mary’s Abbey is located in the heart of the town centre and forms part of the enclosure of the abbey. It is enclosed and separated from the town by the cloister wall, which has stood for almost 400 years. The view over the nuns’ kitchen garden from the small terrace in the abbey shop is highly recommended.  
The garden paths are gravelled. There are three flights of stairs (not steep) to climb to reach the abbey shop.  
Unfortunately, there is no parking available.

The abbey shop is closed on all public holidays, including on religious holidays  
(6th January, 21st March, 6th May, 22nd June, 15th August, 1st and 11th November).  
All opening hours subject to change. Opening hours may differ on local public holidays.

properties.name: The Carnival Museum
properties.description:
*Hatte Bonifatius, der „Apostel der Deutschen“, Humor?  
*Wie haben Fuldas Fürstbischöfe in der Barockzeit gefeiert?  
*Heißt es eigentlich Fastnacht, Fasching oder Karneval?  
*Und warum schmücken sich heute die Karnevalisten mit Orden und Narrenkappe?  

**Diese und viele weitere Fragen beantwortet ein Besuch im Fuldaer Fastnachtsmuseum.**

Erlebe hier die regionaltypische Fastnachtskultur Fuldas, wo sich bereits 1508 Belege für närrisches Treiben finden und erfahre, warum die Stadt zur osthessischen Karnevalshochburg wurde, in der sich Einflüsse des rheinischen Karnevals und der schwäbisch-alemannischen Fastnacht zeigen.

Das Museum bietet interessante Einblicke in die Struktur der fuldischen „Foaset“, die heute von über 4000 Aktiven begeistert gefeiert wird. Zwölf Randstaaten-Vereine pflegen gemeinsam mit der Fuldaer Karneval-Gesellschaft, die den Prinzen als närrisches Oberhaupt stellt, das Brauchtum des größten Heimatfestes in der Region. Die Straßenfastnacht wird mit ihren Höhepunkten, Akteuren und ihrer Organisation durch zahlreiche historische Fotos, Kostüme und abwechslungsreichen digitalen und analogen Exponaten erlebbar.

Das Motto des 2018 gegründeten Fördervereins Fastnachtsmuseum Fulda e.V. lautet: „Neues schaffen, Altes erhalten oder in Erinnerung rufen.“ Die Mitglieder des Vereins haben es sich zur Aufgabe gemacht, Gegenstände der Fuldaer Fastnacht zu sammeln, zu erhalten, zu inventarisieren und in einer Dauerausstellung zu präsentieren. Seit Anfang April 2022 widmet nun das Vonderau Museum Fulda den Eigenheiten und Besonderheiten des osthessischen Fastnacht-Brauchtums ein eigenes kleines Museum im Stadtschloss Fulda.

properties.name: Schloss Fasanerie Gardens
properties.description:
The idyllic grounds of the Schloss Fasanerie stately home span some 100 hectares and combine areas of wild nature with carefully designed gardens and small, idyllic areas of planting.

Natural meadows, well-kept flowerbeds and artistically designed lakes meet non-formal groups of trees and avenues through the woodland. A largely untouched forest meets a meandering beck.

The different areas of the grounds are criss-crossed by numerous paths and surrounded by a tall wall. They all come together to form a homogeneous whole centred around botanical rarities, carefully planned views and architectural highlights.

The park is open daily until dusk.

Local bus route:
7 (Engelhelms), bus stop: Engelhelms-Ortsmitte, then a 1.3km walk

properties.name: Der Spätlesereiter
properties.description:
The Residence’s courtyard is home to an almost life-size bronze sculpture, which was erected in 2021. The so-called “Spätlesereiter” - or “Late Vintage” horseman - is a tribute to a legend dating back to the 18th century.  

** Fulda – a town of wine?**  
Fulda is certainly home to good beer – there's no doubting that. But many people don't know that Fulda also has and had a notable culture for growing wine. Vineyards were planted at Frauenberg monastery shortly after it was founded. Over time, several vineyards were donated to the monastery in Fulda as a symbol of recognition for Boniface.  
This connection between Fulda and good wine lives on to this day – especially when the traditional wine festival is celebrated each year in the museum courtyard.  

**The legend of the late vintage horseman**  
In the 18th century, Prince-Bishop Heinrich VIII von Bibra owned several vineyards in the Rheingau. In 1775, a courier from Johannisberg Castle in the Rheingau was commissioned to obtain permission to harvest the grapes from Fulda. Unfortunately, he returned two weeks late because he was delayed. This had devastating consequences: the grapes on the vines in the Rheingau were already beginning to rot. Nevertheless, the decision was made to press the grapes anyway. To everyone’s surprise, this resulted in an excellent wine as the noble rot had encouraged the concentration of extractives and flavours. The popular Spätlese or late vintage was born.  
It is still not known why the horseman was delayed. Over the years he has been accused of drunkenness, laziness, being captured by robbers and even having a love affair. Whatever the reason, his delay led to the creation of something new and delicious.  

**The monument**  
The bronze sculpture created by Berlin sculptor Valerie Otte was erected in 2021 to mark the completion of the extensive renovation of the courtyard of the Residence in Fulda. There has been a sculpture – a historical counterpart – at Johannisberg Castle in the Rheingau since the 1960s. Both monuments serve to remember the legend of the horseman and the discovery of the Spätlese or late harvest wine.

properties.name: Mittelalterliches Gehöft
properties.description:

Unter fachkundigem Rat entstanden ein Wohnhaus und ein Stallgebäude aus geschälten Eichenbalken, die mit Geflecht und Lehm ausgekleidet wurden.

Das Hauptgebäude wurde anschließend mit Bündeln aus Miscanthus gedeckt, das Stallgebäude verkleidete man mit Reet.

properties.name: Sculpture park
properties.description:
Mit dem Jubiläumfest zur 1100 Jahrfeier ging ein lang gehegter Wünsch in Erfüllung, eine Parkanlage in der Ortslage von Breidenbach zu schaffen. Die Gemeinde wies in 2010 eine Teilfläche des Friedhofes als Grünanlage aus und nur zwei Jahre später began die Planung zur Gestaltung der gesamten Skulpturenparks, der am 10. Mai 2014 feierlich eingeweiht wurde.

Prägend für die Parkanlage ist ein über die gesamte Grünfläche gezogenes Bachbett, das den breiten Bach (Die Perf) symbolisieren soll, der durch den ehemaligen Breidenbacher Grund fließt, und an dessen Bachrand zur Erinnerung an den ehemaligen Friedhof Grabsteine aufgebaut wurden. Die Skulpturen der Ausbildungswerkstatt Christmann und Pfeiffer, die Figuren Geburt, Leben und Tod, diese Sägekunstwerke wurden von Jochen Adam aus den Randfichten des Friedhofs erstellt und die Anlage zur Erinnerung an die 1100 Jahrfeier mit einem Monument mit den Jahreszahlen und einem Bronzebuch mit Texten der Ersterwähnung von Breidenbach und Daten zu Breidenbach im Jubiläumsjahr.

properties.name: Wildweiberhäuschen Langenaubach
properties.description:
Das Wildweiberhäuschen ist eins der ältesten Naturschutzgebiete Hessens (seit 1927) und fällt besonders durch dessen namensgebenden Kalkfelsen auf, der 30 Meter aus dem Aubachtal ragt. 

In der Vergangenheit konnten in seinen eiszeitlichen Lößen-Schichten bereits zahlreiche Knochenreste gefunden werden, die auf eine historische Tierwelt mit Höhlenbären, Rentieren sowie Moor- und Alpenschneehühnern hinweisen. 

Untersuchungen deuteten ebenfalls auf die kulturhistorische Bedeutung des Felsen hin: Es existieren Belege von der menschlichen Besiedlungsgeschichte von der Altsteinzeit bis ins Mittelalter. 

Heute ist der Kulturort ein Wuchsort von teilweise seltene Moose, Flechten und Farne. 

In dem alten Stollen unter dem Kalkfelsen leben zudem streng geschützte Fledermausarten. 

Jedoch auch der Rest des Naturschutzgebietes, entlang des Bachtales, ist Lebensraum für ein gedeihendes Tier- und Pflanzenreich. 

Botanische Raritäten, wie der Blaue Eisenhut und die Trollblume, sowie verschiedene Arten von Schmetterlingen sind vom Naturfreund zu entdecken. 

Text: Stadt Haiger

properties.name: Reithaus und Marstall Dillenburg
properties.description:
Nach der Zerstörung des Dillenburger Schlosses 1760 im Siebenjährigen Krieg benötigten die ehemaligen Bewohner dringend eine neue Unterkunft. Mit Steinen der alten Festungsanlage (für Erdgeschoss und Fassade) baute man deshalb ab 1769 die barocken Häuser der heutigen Wilhelmstraße für die oranien-nassauischen Regierungsbeamten und deren Familien. Auch der Marstall, der zuvor im alten Schloss untergebracht war, entstand 1771 in dieser Straße neu. Er gehört mit dem Reithaus (1789/90) zum Kernstück der heutigen Gestütsanlage.

Das Hessische Landgestüt, das 1869 wiedergegründet wurde, geht in seinem Ursprung auf den in Dillenburg geborenen und in der Stadtkirche getauften Prinzen Moritz von Oranien zurück. Die Gesamtanlage auf beiden Seiten der Wilhelmstraße umfasst 10 ha.

**Tagungen, Konzerte, Ausstellungen und Messen im Reithaus (bis 650 Personen)**

Das Reithaus an der Wilhelmstraße wird von der heimischen Presse als der schönste Saal Dillenburgs beschrieben. Für größere Tagungen, Workshops, Firmenjubiläen oder auch Konzerte bietet es ca. 650 Gästen ein stilvolles Ambiente.  
Das barocke Gebäude aus dem Jahr 1769, welches auch heute noch täglich als Reitbahn genutzt wird, ist mit drei prächtigen Kronleuchtern ausgestattet und besitzt einen Innenraum von ca. 540 m². Für Ihre Veranstaltung decken wir den Reitsand mit einem Teppich ab. Im Nordflügel befindet sich eine barrierefreie Toilettenanlage.

Gerne beraten wir Sie persönlich und unterstützen Sie bei der Auswahl von Cateringanbietern, den Übernachtungsmöglichkeiten oder erstellen für Sie individuelle Tagungspauschalen. Weitere Informationen finden Sie [hier](https://llh.hessen.de/bildung/landgestuet-dillenburg/heiraten-feiern-tagen-eventlocation-landgestuet-dillenburg/).

Text: Oranienstadt Dillenburg und A. Rogocz

properties.name: Bakehouse Seilhofen
properties.description:
Die Entstehung der heutigen, hessischen Backhäuser hat einen ihrer initialen Ursprünge in der Mitte des 16. Jahrhunderts:  Graf Johann VI zu Nassau-Dillenburg verfügte in der „Holz- und Waldordnung“ vom 18. Januar 1562: „In jedem Dorf sollen etliche gemeinen Backöfen verordnet werden“.

Einerseits sollte durch das gemeinschaftliche Backen Holz eingespart werden, da die Ressourcen aufgrund des immensen Holzverbrauches, zum Beispiel für die Eisenverhüttung, in der Region langsam knapp wurden.

Anderseits wurde die Brandgefahr für die zumeist aus Holz, Lehm und Stroh errichteten Höfe mit ihren Wohnhäusern und Stallungen durch eine separate Lage der nun isoliert stehenden Backhäuser gesenkt.

Infolge dieser Verordnung entstanden zahlreiche Dorfgemeinschafts-Backhäuser.

Durch den, über die landesherrschaftlichen Grenzen hinausgehenden Informationsaustausch – Handel, Heirat und Wander-Handwerk – machte dieses vorteilhafte Modell schnell hessenweit Schule.

Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts erfuhr die gemeinschaftliche Backhauskultur eine Renaissance, ausgehend von den damals preußischen Provinzen im heutigen Rheinland-Pfalz und Hessen.

In den Jahren 1846/1847, sorgten Missernten in ganz Europa für große Not, so auch im Königreich Preußen, zu dem der kleine Ort Weyerbusch, im Westerwald, zählte.

Als die Regierung Mehl ausgeben ließ, initiierte Bürgermeister Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen - der auch als Gründungsvater des Genossenschaftswesens gilt - einen „Brodverein“.

Das zugeteilte Mehl wurde in einem eigens erbauten Backhaus verarbeitet.

Das hier gemeinschaftlich gebackene Brot konnte, zu einem günstigen Preis, an die Not leidende Bevölkerung verteilt werden.

Sehr schnell griffen die Idee des „Backhaus samt Backhausverein“ benachbarte Orte im ganzen Westerwald, im Lahn-Dill-Bergland und dem Burgwald bis zur Schwalm auf.

So finden sich heute viele Backhäuser, deren Grundsteinlegung in derselben Epoche erfolgte. 

Die Kunst des guten Brotbackens im Backhaus erforderte schon immer ein hohes Maß an Erfahrung und war gemeinschaftsprägend.

Es begann schon bei der Auswahl und des Schlagens des geeigneten Holzes, dem nächtlichen Anheizen des Ofens und der Festlegung der Backreihenfolge.

Diese wurde von der Backhausgemeinschaft im Vorfeld festgelegt, oft entschied das Los.

Der Brotteig selbst wurde in der Regel nach hauseigenem Rezept individuell im Vorfeld hergestellt und zum Backhaus getragen.

Entscheidend für das gute Gelingen war nicht nur die Auswahl des Mehles, sondern insbesondere auch die Temperatur, bei der die Brotlaibe mit dem Schieber in den Ofen geschoben wurden.

Die Zeit, in der das Brot im Ofen verweilte, wurde zum kommunikativen Austausch der „Backesbäcker/innen“ untereinander genutzt und war daher für den dörflichen Zusammenhalt von wichtiger Bedeutung.

Dieses traditionelle, dörfliche Backhauswesen war fast von der Mitte des 19. bis in jene des 20. Jahrhunderts fester Bestandteil der örtlichen Versorgung.

Durch die technische Entwicklung besaßen seit Mitte der 1950iger Jahre viele Haushalte einen eigenen elektrischen Backofen, sodass das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Backhäusern mehr und mehr an Bedeutung verlor.

Insbesondere in den 60iger Jahren wurden viel Backhäuser abgerissen.

Bis heute jedoch bestehen noch immer zahlreiche Backhäuser und Backhausvereine mit einer oftmals langen, ungebrochenen Tradition bis in die Gegenwart hinein, die in altbewährter Weise backen und die Dorfgemeinschaft pflegen.

Gegenwärtig erlebt das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Hessen eine Wiedergeburt.

properties.name: Stein-Starkes Erlebnis Spiel-Steine
properties.description:
At the geosite “Stone-Strong Experience” on the premises of Herhof Naturstein und Garten GmbH in Niederbiel, geology comes to life. Particularly fascinating are the **eleven play stones**, which invite visitors to explore the properties of different rocks with all their senses.

At the **“Resonant Stones”** station, you can experience how hard stones sound bright and soft ones dull. The **“scratch test”** reveals the differing hardness of the materials. Children can discover fossils in the slate, dig “lucky stones” out of the sandpit, and test their knowledge in the stone quiz. The play stones make nature tangible and turn the geosite into a place full of fun and discovery for young and old alike.

The site thus offers an exciting mix of learning and play – ideal for anyone who wants not only to see stones, but to **feel, hear, and experience** them.

The **five time stones** in the Solms city area show the traces of ore mining and its processing as a link between the Solms districts and provide information about history, especially mining and industrial culture.

properties.name: Forstkapelle Stadtallendorf-Neustadt
properties.description:
Located in the middle of the Herrenwald forest, the Forest Chapel "Mariabild" stands in quiet seclusion.
For centuries, people from Upper Hesse have been drawn to this old pilgrimage site. The place where the church of the abandoned village of "Forst" once stood developed into a site of Marian devotion, and pilgrims kept erecting wooden Marian shrines there until the middle of the 19th century. In 1895, these were replaced by a chapel built of stone. The chapel is framed in red sandstone, and with its red columns it is a feast for the eyes amid the green forest. At the center of the chapel is the Pietà with the Mother of God, holding her son, taken down from the cross, on her lap.

properties.name: Luther sculpture
properties.description:
The church square was the parish cemetery until 1853.

A Luther oak was planted in its centre in 1883 to mark the four hundredth anniversary of Luther's birth.

For a long time, the oak dominated the townscape of Dornholzhausen.

Unfortunately, it fell ill and had to be felled in 2004.

Part of the trunk was left standing and Arne Wilhelm from Bettendorf used chainsaws to create a sculpture with motifs from Luther's life.  
Luther's coat of arms, the Luther rose, and the three parish coats of arms can be seen on the front of the Luther oak.

properties.name: Fronhäuser Ried
properties.description:
Over the course of time, the Lahn has dug deeper and deeper into the landscape. Due to the regular flooding in the Lahn valley, there were already plans to ‘regulate’ the Lahn 200 years ago. The first construction measures between Bellnhausen and Sichertshausen had already taken place in 1809-1810, but the most important work was not carried out until 1926-1928, when two Lahn bends were cut between Roth and Bellnhausen. The old arms are still clearly recognisable, as are the old Lahn loops in the floodplain area. As part of a compensatory measure, the so-called ‘Fronhäuser Ried’ was created as an important site for migratory and breeding birds in this area. For several years now, you have been able to watch storks successfully raising their young directly from the Lahn cycle path.

Would you like to explore the Fronhäuser Ried by bike? Then head for the [Lange-Hessen-Radweg](https://www.marburg-tourismus.de/radfahren#area=*&bm=oac%3Asummer&cat=Radfahren-main,Radtour,Mountainbike,Fernradweg,E-Bike&filter=r-fullyTranslatedLangus-,r-onlyOpened-,sb-sortedBy-0&ipd=59256702&ov=cycling&q=lange&zc=10,8.80966,50.83543)!

properties.name: Manor Odenhausen
properties.description:
Bei dem vierstöckigen Gebäude handelt es sich vermutlich um das höchste freistehende und bewohnte Fachwerkhaus Hessens. Das Anwesen hat eine wechselvolle Geschichte hinter sich: ursprünglich als Wehrburg erbaut, dann den dramatischen Ereignissen des 30-jährigen Krieges ausgeliefert: Brände, Kriegswirren, marodierende Horden, jahrelanges Sterben der Bewohner durch die Pest, endlich Frieden.

Das Herrenhaus in seiner jetzigen Form wurde errichtet und die Herren Nordeck zur Rabenau benutzten die Hofanlage als Wirtschaftshof. Nach dem Aussterben der Linie wechselten mehrmals die Eigentümer. Heute ist es in privater Hand der Familie Maecker.

Das großzügig angelegte Hofgut beinhaltet heute unter anderem das liebevoll gestaltete Hofgut Theater Rabenau, welches sich in einem umgebauten Stall befindet und Platz für 50 Zuschauer gibt.

Das Gebäude kann nur von außen besichtigt werden. Das Hofgut Theater öffnet für Veranstaltungen, Hochzeiten, Firmenfeiern etc. seine Pforten. Schauen Sie doch einmal in unserem Veranstaltungskalender vorbei.

properties.name: Viewing platform on the "Druckele"
properties.description:
Der Lehberg bei Gaildorf lockt mit dem „Druckele“ und einer modernen Aussichtsplattform.

Eingebettet in den Premiumwanderweg „FeenSpuren“ bietet die Plattform Wanderern faszinierende Ausblicke über das Kochertal bis zur Hohenloher Ebene.

**Lehberg und "Druckele"**

Westlich von Gaildorf erstreckt sich mit dem **Lehberg** ein markanter Ausläufer der **Limpurger Berge**.

Gemeinsam mit dem benachbarten Kirgel bildet er einen bewaldeten Höhenrücken, der als Naherholungsgebiet der Region dient.

Der höchste Punkt dieses Kamms wird im lokalen Sprachgebrauch als „**Druckele**“ bezeichnet.

Genau an dieser exponierten Stelle befindet sich ein besonderer Anziehungspunkt für Naturbegeisterte: eine architektonisch markante Aussichtsplattform aus Holz.

**Beste Aussicht**

Die Anlage wurde im Zuge der touristischen Aufwertung der Region errichtet und fügt sich harmonisch in die Waldlandschaft ein.

Von der Plattform aus öffnet sich ein weiter **Panorama-Blick** in nördliche Richtung.

Der Blick schweift über das tief eingeschnittene **Kochertal**, die „**Westheimer Pforte**“ und reicht an klaren Tagen über die **Hohenloher Ebene** bis hin zum **Einkorn** bei Schwäbisch Hall.

**Premium-Wandern**

Erschlossen wird das Druckele über den zertifizierten **Premiumwanderweg** „FeenSpuren – Kirgel Ausblicke“.

Der rund 6,4 Kilometer lange Rundweg führt über naturnahe Pfade direkt an der Plattform vorbei.

In der Nähe befinden sich der **Kernerturm** sowie der **Grill- und Spielplatz am Kirgel**, was den Lehberg zu einem vielseitigen Ausflugsziel im Limpurger Land macht.

properties.name: Miniature Worlds Stuttgart
properties.description:
Miniaturwelten Stuttgart features the largest city model in Europe. Every detail of the city of Stuttgart was built by a single person. It’s an experience for Stuttgart residents, model enthusiasts, and especially children, who have a lot of fun here.

Over a period of just 29 years, Wolfgang Frey created a dream world in his spare time that leaves most visitors in awe. From 1978 to 1992 in Bad Cannstatt in a 25 m² room, and then during the second construction phase from 1992 to 2007, expanding to approximately 600 m², Wolfgang Frey first planned everything in great detail and then, during the second construction phase, built Europe’s largest city model in just 15 years. He had no overall plan and worked on the layout part-time—actually, almost every day. Train operations were very important to him, but even more important was his attention to detail in the houses, phone booths, and replicas of streetcars and track-maintenance vehicles. Learning about the layout’s history is very important here. Over many years, he purchased N-gauge models of vehicles that had actually run in Stuttgart at one time or still run there today. As a railroad employee, for whatever reason, he felt the urge to recreate his Stuttgart railroad world. He was probably unaware that, in doing so, he had built a monument to Stuttgart!

properties.name: Gertelbach Falls
properties.description:
At the edge of Bühlertal, head towards the Black Forest High Road. The main waterfall drops around 70 m. Gertelbach circular trail with refreshments available at the Kohlbergwiese forest restaurant.

Waterfalls in the wild and romantic gorge of the Gertelbach stream at the upper end of the village in the direction of Sand/Schwarzwaldhochstraße. The trail winds its way uphill along narrow paths, bridges, and stairs, past impressive water cascades and mighty rock formations. The crowning glory of the tour through the waterfalls is a wonderful panoramic view from the Wiedenfelsen rock high above Bühlertal.

At the starting point, there is a free hiking car park and the "Gertelbachstraße" stop on line 263 Bühl-Bühlertal-Forbach. Return from Wiedenfelsen via the "Gertelbach-Rundweg" or by bus, line 263, towards Bühlertal-Bühl.

properties.name: Sandsee
properties.description:
Sandsee is a small, idyllic lake located in the northern Black Forest between Sand and Herrenwies.

The lake's water was dammed in the 18th century and used for rafting. In 1933, the Sandsee was converted into a lido and used as a swimming lake until the mid-1970s. The lake owes its name to the red sandstone soil that is very common in this region.

properties.name: Oberbruch bathing lake
properties.description:
The bathing lake in Bühl-Oberbruch with its 50,000 square meters offers welcome refreshment on hot summer days.

Note: from May 2025 only accessible to guests of the campsite!!!

While parents relax on the shady shore of the bathing and boating lake or on the island, the children get their money's worth on the 42-metre-long water slide or at the refreshing shore fountains.

The sports and leisure facilities include table tennis, a beach volleyball court, two bocce courts, a soccer pitch and a children's playground. You can camp or camp out right by the lake, and mobile homes are also available as accommodation.  
[www.campingplatz-adam.de](http://www.campingplatz-adam.de)

properties.name: Eisental water treading basin
properties.description:
Im Gewann „Betschgraben“ wurde im Zuge der Rebflurbereinigungen eine Kneipp-Anlage mit Kinderspielplatz errichtet. 2008 nahm der Heimat- und Verkehrsverein eine grundlegende Sanierung vor. 2009 wurde die Anlage um einen kleinen Barfußpfad ergänzt. Die Anlage ist ein beliebtes Ziel der Naherholung an der Ortsrandlage.

Hier befindet sich auch ein Kräutergarten und ganz in der Nähe eine alte Weintrotte.

properties.name: Neumühl Lake
properties.description: Der Neumühlsee ist ein Stausee mit einer Größe von 50.000 qm, wovon 25.000 qm zum Baden geeignet sind. Der Badebereich ist durch Bojen markiert. Es steht eine Liegewiese sowie eine ausreichende Anzahl von Parkplätzen zur Verfügung. Am See befindet sich ein Campingplatz, Umkleidekabinen und WC’s sind vorhanden.Anfahrt: Von Waldenburg fahren Sie über die L1046 Richtung Obersteinbach, Abzweigung K2362 Richtung Sailach, Abzweigung K2363 zum Neumühlsee.

properties.name: Loßburg - Zauberland am Kinzigsee
properties.description:
Nature adventure trail Zauberland am Kinzigsee

Welcome to Zauberland am Kinzigsee

Nature is at home here and shows itself in the most beautiful colors and facets. Whether you want to cool off on hot summer days, enjoy the colorful variety of leaves in autumn, immerse yourself in the tranquility of the

winter or to celebrate the reawakening of nature in spring.



Whether on your own, with the help of the geocaching discovery tours, or on one of the nature trails, all generations will find their personal favorite place in Zauberland.  
Parking is available at the outdoor pool and below the Waldfestplatz on Schömberger Straße.  
Admission is free!

properties.name: Hardtsee Leisure Center
properties.description:
The Hardtsee leisure center offers swimming fun, camping, restaurants and playgrounds. Ideal for families, water sports enthusiasts and youth groups - nature, relaxation and fun combined!

The Ubstadt-Weiher leisure center is located around the beautiful Hardtsee lake and has long enjoyed great popularity in the region and beyond. The Hardtsee offers refreshing bathing fun with excellent water quality
water quality, non-swimmer, swimmer and water sports areas and a spacious and well-tended sunbathing lawn.

The leisure center's facilities include the bathing lake, the "Hardtseeliebe" restaurant, the Weiherer Bucht, a campsite, a variety of fun and games and a youth campsite.  

The Hardtsee campsite offers 50 bookable short-term and seasonal camping pitches, as well as modern, barrier-free sanitary buildings with separate showers and washrooms and a special children's sanitary area. There are also direct shopping facilities and a restaurant. The 310 permanently rented year-round camping pitches are a popular meeting place where the residents of the four sub-communities - Ubstadt, Weiher, Stettfeld and Zeutern - like to come together.

properties.name: Schönbucht Tower
properties.description:
The viewing experience in the Schönbuch Nature Park!

Due to the current situation, please observe the known distance rules and the instructions on the tower regarding the ascents and descents.

It looks far beyond Schönbuch and Gäu to the Black Forest and the Swabian Alb. A viewing tower on the Stellberg in Herrenberg, visible as far as the highway and beyond. An outstanding attraction for the Schönbuch Nature Park with tremendous appeal. As part of a wide-ranging ideas competition, a grandiose design for a tower was created that fits perfectly into the Schönbuch cultural landscape.

With a construction made of local coniferous wood and tensioned steel cables, the tower integrates perfectly into its natural surroundings in the nature park. Modern and light, it is an attraction just to look at.

Two counter-rotating staircases spiral upwards to a height of 30 meters. From three platforms, you can enjoy a fantastic view of the surrounding area.



You can find more information at:

[https://www.schoenbuch-heckengaeu.de/schoenbuchturm](https://www.schoenbuch-heckengaeu.de/schoenbuchturm)

properties.name: Arkau Municipal Outdoor Pool
properties.description:
The 50 x 15 m pool is divided into a swimming pool and a fun pool (non-swimmers). The fun pool has a wide slide, a water spout, as well as floor bubbles and massage jets.

There is also a 120 m² paddling pool for children.  In addition, there is a mud pit, a climbing frame, and a nest swing for the little ones. The large sunbathing lawn, which is equipped with child-friendly play equipment, offers plenty of opportunities for fun and relaxation with table tennis tables, a beach volleyball court, and a kiosk.

properties.name: Church of God
properties.description:
The church is located one kilometer outside the town in the direction of Münster.

The Herrgottskirche dates back to the discovery of a consecrated host in 1389.

It features a masterpiece by Tilman Riemenschneider as well as two side altars.

properties.name: Privates Bauernmuseum
properties.description: Private collection of all kinds of rarities from times gone by. Exhibition spread over three floors: agricultural equipment, tractors, sewing machines, pictures and books from earlier times, old shoemaker's workshop, children's playground. Opening hours: Guided tours on request

properties.name: Bühler Stein
properties.description: Rock formation and viewpoint. Formerly the left-hand stronghold of the Bühl-Stollhofen line built by Margrave Ludwig Wilhelm von Baden and successfully defended in 1703.

properties.name: Baroque church of St. Maria
properties.description:
The 51 m high onion dome is the landmark of the baroque church of St. Maria, visible from afar.

A church had already been built on this site in the 13th century, which was demolished in 1763 and replaced by the current church in 1764 - 1768. The rococo building is one of the most important buildings of this era in Baden. Not far from the church is a lime tree planted in 1737. Together with the former rectory from 1758 and the Nepomuk Chapel to the south of the parish church, a former mortuary chapel built in 1503 and rebuilt in 1745/46, the center of Kappelwindeck boasts a remarkable ensemble of buildings.

properties.name: Carl Netter Observation Tower
properties.description:
Zwischen Bühl-Altschweier und Bühl-Eisental liegt der 10 m hohe Aussichtsturm, von dem sich eine herrliche Aussicht über Rheinebene, Reben und zu den Schwarzwaldbergen bietet.

Der Turm aus Metall wurde 1902 zu Ehren von Großherzog Friedrich errichtet. Stifter des Turmes waren die Brüder Adolph und Carl Leopold Netter, die um die Jahrhundertwende mit ihrem Stahlunternehmen die Weltmärkte erobert hatten und die Stadt Bühl mit Stiftungen und Schenkungen unterstützten. Der Turm ist jederzeit zugänglich.

properties.name: Black Forest pool
properties.description:
The Schwarzwaldbad Bühl is a combined indoor and outdoor pool with 3 indoor and 6 outdoor pools with a water surface area of over 2000 square meters.

The indoor pool includes a swimmers' pool, a non-swimmers' pool and a toddlers' pool. A service station with hot and cold drinks and various snacks is available in the warming hall with a separate relaxation room.  
In addition to the swimmers' and non-swimmers' pool, the outdoor pool offers a children's pool with two water slides and a diving facility. The spacious outdoor area offers a wonderful view of the Black Forest. The outdoor pool also has a playground with two large wooden boats, a beach volleyball court and a children's paddling pool with a sun awning for the little ones.

properties.name: City Museum
properties.description:
The town museum has been housed in a former bakery since 2010. The 17th century building is one of the oldest residential buildings to have survived in Bühl.  

The collection guides visitors through the eventful history of the town from the first traces of settlement to the 20th century. The first floor is dedicated to economic history: market and trade, guilds, crafts and manufactories, industry and companies. The exhibition on the top floor provides an insight into the lithographic workshop of Johannes Lohmüller (1830-1918), the last portrait lithographer in Baden. Here you can see the Lohmüller family's original photo studio, where visitors can have their picture taken in the style of the Wilhelminian era. The basement is dedicated to religious history: Catholic, Protestant and Jewish religion as well as the history of Jewish citizens from the 16th century to the deportation in 1940.  
Guided tours and educational museum activities are offered by the City History Institute.

properties.name: Mehliskopf Tower
properties.description:
Der Mehliskopf-Turm ist der älteste steinerne Aussichtsturm im Nordschwarzwald und liegt auf 1.010 m ü. NN.

Der Mehliskopf ist ein Berg im nördlichen Schwarzwald. Er liegt oberhalb der Schwarzwaldhochstrasse, zwischen Sand und Hundseck. Der Turm ist nicht sehr hoch und liegt am Westrand des Gipfelplateaus. Der Mehliskopfturm wurde 1880 vom Schwarzwaldverein erbaut und seitdem mehrfach renoviert. Er besteht aus einer steinernen Basis mit hölzerner, überdachter Aussichtsplattform und bietet eine schöne Aussicht in das Rheintal und über die Gipfel des Nordschwarzwaldes. Der Aussichtsturm ist frei zugänglich.

properties.name: Parish church of St. Peter & Paul
properties.description:
The Catholic parish church of St. Peter and Paul, built in 1872-1877 by architect Karl Dernfeld, offers space for around 650 worshippers.

The church is 60 m long, 24 m wide and has a 63 m high openwork tower. The parishioners donated altars in the neo-Gothic style, of which only the sculptures remain today. In addition to the building deed and Baden coins, a bottle of Affentaler red wine 1870 and a bottle of white wine 1865 were placed in the foundation stone.

properties.name: Aussichtspavillon Eisental
properties.description: From here, there are fantastic views over Eisental and the Rhine Valley as far as the Vosges mountains. The viewing pavilion is just one information point on the 4.1 km Red Wine Trail in Bühl-Eisental. This can be hiked in around 1.5 hours, either alone or accompanied by a wine guide. The circular trail starts and ends in the Eisental district of Bühl and is very well signposted.

properties.name: Imperial City Museum in the Old Hospital
properties.description:
The Imperial City Museum in Bad Wimpfen brings the city's development after the fall of the Staufer dynasty to life on three floors. The Old Hospital in Bad Wimpfen The Old Hospital was founded before 1230 by the Knights Hospitaller and later taken over by the Order of the Holy Spirit. It developed into one of the largest hospitals in southern Germany. In the 15th century, it was divided into a spiritual and a civil hospital. The convent house, built in 1775, served as the monastery and hospital wing of the Order of the Holy Spirit. This classicist building impresses with its decorative order coat of arms in the Langgasse.

Today's hospital complex comprises the medieval stone building, the attached north and east wings, and an extension on Hauptstraße. Particularly noteworthy is the Alemannic half-timbered structure, which is one of the oldest in the city. Imperial City Museum Today, the Old Hospital houses the Imperial City Museum with an exhibition on the imperial history of Bad Wimpfen.  

The exhibition focuses on: - The territory of the imperial city with a large model of the city - The city's relationship with the emperor and the empire - City law - Defense - Jurisdiction - Crafts and trade - Life in the imperial city - The Jewish community in Wimpfen - The history of the salt works - The history of the hospital system - The history of the Battle of Wimpfen
- Technology and forms of half-timbered construction Another highlight awaits visitors on the top floor: the Helfrich Collection with **over 400 historical cameras** – from the first pinhole camera to modern digital cameras. In addition to the museum, the municipal gallery and the culture and tourist information office are also located in the Old Hospital. The museum is sponsored by the Alt Wimpfen e.V. association.

Visitor information Opening hours: Daily from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Guided tours: Individual guided tours can be booked during opening hours through the Culture and Tourist Information Office.

properties.name: Schloss Langenburg
properties.description: Known as a **jewel of Renaissance architecture**, the castle is still the **residence of the princely family of Hohenlohe-Langenburg** today.  The **baroque garden with its orangery** offers a **unique view of the Jagst Valley**. Weddings, family celebrations, and corporate events become unforgettable experiences in this setting. A highlight for garden lovers are the **Princely Garden Days**, which take place every year on the first weekend in September. The garden is only accessible during events.

properties.name: Volkskundemuseum
properties.description:
You can visit two museums in the Ostrach administrative building: the Folklore Museum and the Local History Museum. The Folklore Museum, located on the first two floors of the former Salem administrative building, houses a wide variety of exhibits from rural life. The focus is on "19th century folklore." In addition, special exhibitions are regularly held.

After a large number of small exhibits on folk culture, which convey the craftsmanship and artistic sensibility of their producers, a "Leidringer" bedroom, a spinning room, and a kitchen-living room are on display. Other highlights of the collection include rustic cabinets and chairs, musical instruments, and religious folk art.

The museum is open every first Sunday of the month (except August).

properties.name: Kniebis forest swimming pool
properties.description:
The forest swimming pool is just the thing for anyone who enjoys swimming outdoors and spending time in the fresh air—whether young or old.

For those who enjoy being out in the fresh air and want to get some exercise, the forest swimming pool, idyllically situated on the Kniebis, is the perfect spot. Whether you want to swim laps or just soak up the sun—even the little ones can have fun in the wading pool. Sports enthusiasts can play volleyball or table tennis. The kiosk offers light snacks and drinks.

An overview of events taking place at the forest swimming pool can be found at: [Events at the Kniebis Forest Swimming Pool](https://www.waldschwimmbad-kniebis.de/Veranstaltungen)

properties.name: Ottenhöfen - Basgarde Hof
properties.description:
Experience farm with Baden/Bavarian beer garden

The rustic experience farm with Baden/Bavarian beer garden.

Our beer garden has about 80 outdoor seats, barn with 50 seats, 13 different types of beer, various wines, a wide range of drinks, hearty menu, quiet location with beautiful views to the Vosges, parking at the farm.

Corporate club celebrations, children's and adult birthdays, groups of up to 50 people

properties.name: Deer barn
properties.description:
Discover the fascinating world of the Sommer family of artists at the Hirschwirtscheuer Museum. Explore the permanent exhibition and the changing special exhibitions on modern art from the Würth Collection. Right in the heart of Künzelsau's old town, you will find an art museum in a historic residential building with a barn: the Hirschwirtscheuer.

**Sommer family of artists** The museum offers you a unique insight into the life and work of the remarkable Sommer dynasty of artists, who have shaped the regional art scene for five generations. You can discover the baroque works of this family of artists in castles and churches throughout the region. The dynasty is known for its diverse artistic talents – from **painting and sculpture** to graphic design and photography. Their works reflect not only the artistic development of recent decades, but also the deep personal and cultural influences that have shaped their art.

**Exhibitions** The museum houses an extensive collection of works by the Sommer family. **Changing special exhibitions** also offer you new perspectives on contemporary and modern art from the Würth Collection. Immerse yourself in the inspiring world of the **Sommer family of artists**!

properties.name: Leyk's Lotus Garden
properties.description: **Asian Water Garden.** The 3,000 square meter water garden on the southern edge of Rothenburg enchants visitors with its lush variety of exotic plants. Secluded seating areas surrounded by greenery, in the tea house, or on the viewing terrace allow visitors to quickly forget the outside world. **Offers:** Guided tours of the ceramics factory and garden by appointment. Cafe and gift shop on site. **Seasonal admission:** Year-round season ticket €2. **Opening hours**: April to December, Monday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. (from October until 5 p.m.).

properties.name: Taubertal on the Eich
properties.description:
**Landscape park.** With its double bridge, Kobolzeller church, and numerous mills along the Tauber River, the Tauber Valley at Eich is the epitome of an English garden and was also internationally recognized as such around 1900.

**Other attractions:** Guided tour "Romantic Rothenburg – In the footsteps of the artists" only available in German and as a group tour with prior registration. Bronnenmühle "Helmes" beer garden, "Rothenburger Eich" vineyard, Europe's highest concentration of mills.

properties.name: Greenery and gardens in front of historic walls, Dinkelsbühl
properties.description: **City park.** The walled old town, preserved from the Middle Ages, can be completely surrounded by greenery. The walled old town, preserved from the Middle Ages, can be completely surrounded by greenery. From Rothenburg Pond, where swans glide majestically across the water, to the ramparts and moats and the Old Promenade to the herb gardens in front of the Nördlinger Gate. The Bäuerlinsturm tower on the banks of the Wörnitz is the town's landmark, past the Wörnitz lido and through the Bleiche with its orchards. A tour that opens your heart and eyes. ** Offers:** Green tours, fruit tree auction, concerts in the city park, church services in the countryside, Lake Festival at the Landestheater Dinkelsbühl, circular trail around the city walls: 30 Years' War.

properties.name: Sophianeum in the Old Court Pharmacy
properties.description:
**"Flora" guided tour.** Guided tours in the wildly romantic garden with views of the beautiful Jagst Valley. Meditation with plants in nature. "White Rose" guided tour "In the footsteps of Sophie Scholl and her friend Lisa Remppis." **Offers:** Nature-oriented garden tour or search for traces of Sophie Scholl.

**Admission:** €5, oil seminar €10, tasting separate, min. 5 - max. 20 people.

properties.name: Hohenlohe Castle Schillingsfürst/Garden Delight
properties.description:
**Cardinal's Garden.** The beautiful and atmospheric Cardinal's Garden, located very close to the Hohenlohe Castle, is considered a green oasis of relaxation. It was named after Gustav Adolf Prince of Hohenlohe Schillingsfürst (1823–1896), Curia Cardinal and Papal Chamberlain. He was the son of Franz Joseph zu Hohenlohe Schillingsfürst and Princess Konstanze, née Princess zu Hohenlohe-Langenburg; two of his brothers were Chlodwig zu Hohenlohe (1819–1901) and Victor, Duke of Ratibor (1818–1893).

For three years now, the "Gartenlust" has been taking place in this historic park. In a dreamlike location with old trees and a beautiful view, the park offers a spacious area for over 90 exhibitors with high-quality items. There is also a children's playground in the park, inviting visitors to linger.

There is the Franz Liszt monument, which was erected during the piano virtuoso's lifetime (1811-1886), and the "mausoleum," the burial place of the Princes of Hohenlohe. The park is open to the public free of charge, except during events.

**Attractions:** Castle, falcon museum, foreign legion museum, Liszt museum. Nearby: Doerfler museum. Well house museum with ox treadmill, princely hunting falconry.

**Gartenlust event** **Opening hours:** Outside of the "Gartenlust" and "Medieval Market" events, the Cardinal's Garden is open to the public all year round.

properties.name: Burggarten Rothenburg o.d.T.
properties.description:
**Park on the site of a former castle complex.**

A Staufer castle built here in 1142 on an exposed mountain spur high above the Tauber River was destroyed in the mid-14th century. Today, it is a Baroque and English garden with the best view of the city and the Tauber Valley. When you reach the castle garden through the castle gate, you can enjoy beautiful views of the Tauber Valley from the viewing platforms on the left and right. To the north, visitors can see the district of Detwang, whose church houses a wooden altar by Tilman Riemenschneider. Rothenburg was first mentioned in a document here in 960. A short hiking trail leads from the castle garden to Detwang, which should take about 20 minutes – you will also pass the Unter den Linden beer garden, located directly on the Tauber. The Topplerschlösschen castle also peeks out from behind the trees in the north. To the south, the castle garden offers views across the An der Eich vineyard to the Tauber Valley with the Kobolzeller church and the double bridge, as well as the hospital district on the opposite side with the striking dormers of the youth hostel (formerly a horse mill).

**Other offers**: Night watchman tour open to the public every evening during the high season at 8:00 p.m. (English) and 9:30 p.m. (German) €8 or €9 per person, Staufer stele and information board Stauferburg, Rothenburg Tower Trail.

Einer der schönsten Tierparks Deutschlands

TIERE SEHEN UND ERLEBEN

Im Wildpark Bad Mergentheim, einem der artenreichsten Wildparks in Europa, erwarten Sie mehr als 50 Tierarten auf insgesamt 35 Hektar Fläche. Hier gibt es kaum Maschendraht, Käfige oder Gitter; fast alle Gehege sind mit kaum wahrnehmbaren Begrenzungen als naturnah gestaltete Freisichtanlagen erbaut. Natürlichkeit und artgerechte Tierhaltung stehen dabei im Vordergrund. Für die Gehege und Einrichtungen werden größtenteils natürliche Materialien verwendet, und es wird bei allen Maßnahmen auf ökologische Verträglichkeit geachtet.

Ganz nach dem Motto „Tiere sehen und erleben“ kommen Sie in den Genuss, Wildtiere artgerecht beobachten zu können. Für Ihre entspannte Pause haben Sie die Wahl zwischen mehreren herrlichen Biergärten am Rundweg, umgeben von purer Natur.

Ihre Kinder werden die Abenteuerspielplätze und den Spielbauernhof mit Streichelzoo lieben. Ein Tag im Wildtierpark Bad Mergentheim – Seelenbalsam für Groß und Klein!

properties.name: Teutonic Order Castle Museum
properties.description:
From 1527 to 1809, Mergentheim Castle was the residence of the Grand Masters and German Masters of the Teutonic Order. In 1996, the Teutonic Order Museum was reopened here, covering an area of around 3,000 square meters. Artworks, models, objects, and texts vividly illustrate the history of the Teutonic Order from its beginnings in 1190 to the present day, as well as its activities in the Holy Land, Prussia, and the Holy Roman Empire.

The princely rooms of the castle give an impression of the former glory of the Teutonic Order. The Berwart staircase and columned hall from the Renaissance, the Rococo Götterzimmer (Hall of the Gods) and Neue Fürstenwohnung (New Prince's Apartment), and the classicist Kapitelsaal (Chapter Hall) and main staircase bear witness to the castle's eventful architectural history. The jewel of the residence is the castle church, to whose construction important artists such as Balthasar Neumann and François de Cuvilliès contributed. The history of Bad Mergentheim is shown from its time as a Frankish settlement to its development as a spa town. In addition, there is an exhibition consisting of medieval sculpture and panel painting, exotica, faience, alabaster and marble reliefs from the Renaissance and Baroque periods, precious small pieces of furniture, handicrafts and curiosities from Baron Carl Joseph von Adelsheim, as well as a collection of 40 doll's kitchens, doll's rooms and doll's houses, and toy shops (19th/20th century) in the castle. The Mörike Cabinet is located in the city history section. Among other things, it is dedicated to the seven-year stay of the Swabian poet.

properties.name: Catholic parish of Eppingen
properties.description:
There are currently around 7,000 Catholic Christians living in the parish of Eppingen. The parish covers eight towns with seven churches: Eppingen, Mühlbach, Gemmingen, Richen, Adelshofen, Ittlingen, and Rohrbach.

The parish church of Our Lady towers above the old town of Eppingen (Kirchgasse 10), which is rich in half-timbered buildings. In addition to the **parish church**, the church hill is also home to other central church buildings: The **parish office** is located in **St. Josefhaus** (Kirchgasse 8). This building also houses the offices of the pastoral staff and meeting rooms. The house next door (Kirchgasse 6), the **former Speyer rectory**, houses the **Museum of Religious Folk Beliefs** and the Catholic public library. The museum also includes a show cemetery behind the parish church.

To the left of the church is the **parsonage** (Kirchgasse 14). The building, which dates from 1810, was originally a Protestant schoolhouse. Right next to it is the **St. Catherine's Chapel** (Kirchgasse 16). The former chapel, which served as a schoolroom after the Reformation, is now a small community center.

properties.description:

Die Gemeinden Kraichtal-Unteröwisheim und Bad Schönborn runden den schönen Radius des Kirchenbezirks ab.

Die acht Kirchengemeinden des Bezirkes Bruchsal bestehen aus rund 1.300 Mitgliedern.

Christen beteten Anfang des 19. Jahrhunderts um ein verstärktes Wirken des Heiligen Geistes. Weissagungen traten auf. So wurden bis 1835 zwölf Apostel gerufen. Die Katholisch-apostolische Kirche entstand und breitete sich schnell aus.

Geburtsstunde

Nach Meinungsverschiedenheiten sprach die Katholisch-apostolische Kirche 1863 die Exkommunikation der Gemeinde Hamburg aus. Die Gemeinde blieb jedoch zusammen und erhielt in ihrem früheren Priester Carl Preuß einen Apostel. Dies war die Geburtsstunde der Neuapostolischen Kirche.

Entwicklung

Ausgehend von Hamburg entstanden zahlreiche neue Gemeinden. Heute zählt die Neuapostolische Kirche weltweit 60.000 Gemeinden mit nahezu neun Millionen Christen.

properties.name: Themenjahr Stadt.Landschaft.Natur
properties.description:
Rothenburg ob der Tauber liegt eingebettet zwischen zwei charakteristischen Landschaften: der Frankenhöhe im Norden und dem Taubertal im Süden. Diese geologische und kulturelle Grenzlage prägt das Stadtbild bis heute. Rothenburg ob der Tauber markiert den Übergang zwischen der sanft gewellten Frankenhöhe und Hohenloher Ebene – hier entspringen zahlreiche Bäche, die sich tief in die Landschaft eingeschnitten haben.

Die Tauber hat über Jahrtausende ein eindrucksvolles Tal geformt, das heute zu den reizvollsten Flusslandschaften Süddeutschlands zählt.

Dieses Themenjahr öffnet Türen, die sonst verschlossen bleiben und führt dich an der Seite von Naturparkrangern, Winzern, Förstern, Märchenerzählern und Vereinen hinaus in die Natur, hinein in die Geschichte und mitten hinein in das Rothenburg-Gefühl.

Rothenburg ob der Tauber ist weit mehr als eine mittelalterliche Stadt mit weltberühmter Silhouette – sie ist eine Stadtlandschaft, ein gewachsenes Gesamtkunstwerk aus Kultur, Geschichte und Natur.
