properties.name: Höhenfreibad Streichen
properties.description:
Kleines, familiäres Freibad mit benachbarter Minigolfanlage  

Eine Geschichte von Einfallsreichtum und Gemeinschaft

Das Höhenfreibad Streichen blickt auf eine faszinierende Geschichte zurück. In den 1950er-Jahren, als die umliegenden Möbelfabriken häufig von Bränden heimgesucht wurden, sollte ein großer Feuerlöschteich Abhilfe schaffen. Doch der damalige Bürgermeister Walter Hetzel und seine Gemeinderäte hatten eine andere Vision. Heimlich versetzten sie in der Nacht vor Baubeginn die Markierungspflöcke, um den Teich deutlich zu vergrößern. Aus dem geplanten Löschteich wurde so 1957 ein Freibad. Die schrägen Beckenwände sind bis heute ein Zeugnis dieser Zeit – sie wurden so konzipiert, dass das Wasser auch im Winter im Becken bleiben konnte, ohne dass Eis die Wände beschädigte.

Vom „Grottenteich“ zum modernen Freibad

Anfangs war das Schwimmbad, das sein Wasser aus einem Bach bezog, noch als „Grottenteich“ bekannt, in dem sich Frösche und Molche wohlfühlten. Doch mit dem Bau einer modernen Umwälzanlage, dem Anschluss an das Wassernetz und der Auskleidung des Beckens mit einer Folie verwandelte es sich in ein sauberes und einladendes Bad.

Heute ist das Höhenfreibad Streichen ein Ort der Erholung und der Gemeinschaft. Seit 1994 betreibt die **DLRG Streichen** das Freibad in Eigenregie und sorgt für die Beckenaufsicht, den Verkauf von Eintrittskarten und die Bewirtung. Die Entscheidung, die Verantwortung zu übernehmen, hat sich als Glücksfall erwiesen. Die DLRG hat das Bad kontinuierlich weiterentwickelt und die Attraktivität durch eine **18-Loch-Minigolfanlage** erhöht. Das Freibad ist ein beliebter Treffpunkt für Anwohnende und Besuchende, die eine entspannte Atmosphäre schätzen.

Bitte beachten Sie, dass das Freibad bei kühlem oder schlechtem Wetter (unter 20 °C) vorübergehend geschlossen sein kann. Informationen zur Öffnung erhalten Sie telefonisch unter 0 74 33 / 9 04 68 45.

Jedes Zimmer ist einem Planeten zugeordnet und dementsprechend sind Möbel und Farben angepasst. Ihren Tag beginnen Sie mit einem leckeren Planeten-Frühstück, im Planetengarten können unterschiedliche Hölzer wachsen sehen, genächtigt wird in einem komfortablen Planetenzimmer.  
Unser Haus ist offiziell durch den ADFC als Bett+Bike Unterkunft ausgezeichnet.

**Zimmer:**  
53 Zimmer mit 186 Betten  
8 behindertengerechte Zimmer  
alle Zimmer Nichtraucherzimmer mit Dusche/WC, TV, Fön, Safe

properties.name: 600 Jahre altes Rathaus
properties.description: Das Nördlinger Rathaus ist nicht nur über 600 Jahre alt, sondern auch das älteste Steinhaus der Stadt aus dem 13. Jahrhundert. Seit dem Jahr 1382 wird es ununterbrochen als Rathaus der Stadt genutzt. Die Besonderheit ist die nachträglich im Jahr 1618 von Wolfgang Walberger erbaute Freitreppe aus Suevit-Haustein - ein kunsthistorisch bedeutsames Bauwerk.

properties.name: Fahrrad Wiedemann
properties.description:
Hier werden fachkompetente Beratung, guter Service und faire Preise noch großgeschrieben!

Meisterbetrieb für Fahrradreperaturen, Ersatzteile und Zubehör für Fahrräder, Neuradverkauf.

properties.name: Flugplatz Aumühle
properties.description:
Auf dem Sportflugplatz besteht am Wochenende die Möglichkeit als Ultraleicht- und Motorflieger aktiv zu werden. Segelflugschlepp mit einem Ultraleichtflugzeug ist auf Anfrage möglich und darüber hinaus werden auch Hubschrauberflüge angeboten. Hallenplätze zu Übernachtungszwecken sind evtl. auf Anfrage verfügbar.

In der Fliegergaststätte auf dem Platz werden kalte Getränke, sowie Kaffee und Kuchen angeboten.

properties.name: Waldklassenzimmer in Wörnitz
properties.description:
Das Waldklassenzimmer mit seinem schönen Eichenwald liegt ca. 1 km westlich von Wörnitz, nahe der Autobahnausfahrt Wörnitz (A 7). Der Eingang befindet sich unmittelbar am Wanderparkplatz am Fuße des Heinerbergs. Das Waldklassenzimmer der Gemeinde Wörnitz wurde 2002 eingeweiht, sowie in der Folge an den Wanderweg Wörnitz-auber und den Europäischen Wasserscheideweg angebunden.

Mit großer finanzieller und fachlicher Unterstützung des Naturparks Frankenhöhe wurde das Waldklassenzimmer 2018 erneuert, inhaltlich aktualisiert und mit der Erstellung des neuen Eingangsportals sehr einladend gestaltet.

Als außerschulischer Lernort bietet das Waldklassenzimmer für geschlossene Gruppen, wie Schulklassen oder Kindergärten, optimale Voraussetzungen für Erlebnisse und Wissensvermittlung in freier Natur. So können sich auch Naturfreunde auf anschauliche Weise mit dem Thema Wald und Natur auseinandersetzen.

Lassen Sie sich von den 10 Informationselementen zu Lage, Geschichte und Besonderheiten, die örtliche Fauna und Flora, sowie Forstwirtschaft und Geologie zum Nachdenken anregen. Entlang des Baumpfads am Spechttelefon oder in der Bodengrube wird zur aktiven Auseinandersetzung mit einem der wichtigsten Lebensräume unserer Heimat eingeladen.

In der Mitte des Waldklassenzimmers bieten alte Eichenstämme einen stimmungsvollen Sitz – u. Versammlungsplatz für Besuchergruppen. Als Rastmöglichkeit und Wetterschutz dient ein kleines Holzhaus direkt am Wanderparkplatz „Heinerberg".

properties.name: Geisterführung mit Henker
properties.description:
für mutige Kinder ab 8 Jahre geeignet.

Dauer: ca. 60 Minuten, Teilnehmerzahl: bis 50 Personen.

properties.name: Walburga's journey through time
properties.description: In Rothenburg ob der Tauber, the craftswoman's widow Walburga is confronted with the challenges posed by the death of her last husband. She has to remarry quickly, otherwise she will have to leave her home. Who was she, how and where did she live, what did her everyday life look like and what customs, rules and punishments were there? All these questions are answered by "Walburga's Time Travel", which takes you back to around 1500 and takes you on an entertaining journey through the alleyways of Rothenburg to "her home", the "Old Rothenburg Craftsman's House" from 1270. Easter to October and December: Thursday, Friday, Saturday at 7 pm. Also as a group tour, meeting point: Town Hall entrance, duration: 60 minutes, languages: German and English. Information and contact: Christine Glindemann, Tel. 09861/938668

properties.name: English Trail
properties.description: Eine der steilsten Weinberglagen Europas. Mit kleinem Klettersteig und Aussichtsplattform.

properties.name: Tourist Information Dinkelsbühl
properties.description: Die Tourist Information im Alten Rathaus bietet zahlreiche Prospekte über die Sehenswürdigkeiten, Ausflüge sowie Wander- und Radtouren.

properties.name: Stadtpark rund um die Altstadt
properties.description: Ein Rundgang, der zu wirklich jeder Jahreszeit Herz und Augen öffnet: Es bieten sich immer wieder romantische Blicke, wie z. B. über den Rothenburger Weiher auf den Faulturm mit Parkwächterhäuschen, man begegnet dem Mauergeist, kommt durch eine alte Lindenallee, folgt der Turmparade bis zu den Krautbeeten am Nördlinger Tor. Weiter geht es an der Wörnitz entlang mit imposantem Blick auf die Altstadt, vorbei am Strandbad, einem der letzten Flußbäder Bayerns und durch die Bleiche mit Ihren Streuobstbeständen.

properties.name: St. Stephen's Monastery
properties.description:
Das ehemalige Stephanskloster ist eine Ruine auf dem Heiligenberg.

St. Stephan, neben St. Michael das zweite Kloster auf dem Heiligenberg, wurde um das Jahr 1090 von dem Benediktiner Arnold erbaut. Dieser war kurz zuvor in den Benediktiner-Orden eingetreten. Er errichtete sich eine Klause und eine Kapelle auf dem vorderen Gipfel des Aberinsberges.

Zundebold, Propst im nahe gelegenen Michaelskloster, fand Gefallen an der Zelle Arnolds und ließ vier Jahre später, mit Erlaubnis des Klosters Lorsch, an die Kirche Gebäude anfügen. Von hier aus konnte man jede Bewegung im Neckartal schon von weitem beobachten, denn die Kuppe war kahl. Durch Bau und Heizung war ein großer Teil des Waldes abgeholzt worden. Gleichzeitig wurde die alte Zisterne (das Heidenloch) wieder instand gesetzt. St. Stephan bekam einen eigenen Bezirk zugewiesen und war damit wirtschaftlich unabhängig.

properties.name: Philosopher's garden
properties.description:
A sun-drenched natural balcony with an abundance of exotic plants.

Here you can relax on one of the benches or on the beautiful lawns and get some fresh air while enjoying the view.

Due to the mild climate along the Philosophenweg, many plants from subtropical areas (e.g. almond trees, lemon trees and gingko trees) thrive here and have become native to this area.

properties.description: The Carl Bosch Museum in Heidelberg offers its visitors over 300m² of insights into the life and discoveries of Nobel Prize winner Carl Bosch.

properties.name: Philosopher's path
properties.description:
On the natural balcony of the Philosophenweg, every spectator sits in the front row and can take in nature and the view of the city at the same time.

Unprotected, the exotic plants thrive on this climatic island, which is one of the warmest places in Germany: Japanese woolly mistletoe and American cypress, Spanish broom and Portuguese cherry, lemon and pomegranate, bamboo, palm trees, pine trees. Everything blooms weeks earlier than in the valley. Scholars once walked here in stiff frock coats and relaxed their thoughts on a walk: the Heidelberg Philosophers' Path on the sunny slope of the Heiligenberg has led many to new insights, and in any case to unique views of Heidelberg. From this place in the sun, whose mild climate and vegetation are reminiscent of Tuscany, the "Heidelberg triad" of old town, river and mountains can be enjoyed at leisure.

properties.name: Tiefburg Handschuhsheim
properties.description:
Ruins of a moated castle in the Heidelberg district of Handschuhsheim.

The Tiefburg, also known as Handschuhsheim Castle, is a moated castle ruin from the Middle Ages located in the Heidelberg district of Handschuhsheim.

It was once surrounded by a moat that was fed by the Mühlbach stream. The walled tributary is still visible at the north-east corner of the complex today.

In the past, the castle was the ancestral seat of the Lords of Handschuhsheim; in 1624, the castle passed to the Lords of Helmstatt. The Thirty Years' War up to the Palatinate War of Succession, as well as several fires, led to the castle being destroyed and uninhabitable in 1674.

Between 1911 and 1913, the owner Raban Graf von Helmstatt renovated the deep castle and made the residential building usable again. After being rented out to various citizens, the castle became a youth hostel in 1921. In 1950, the city of Heidelberg acquired the castle and handed the property over to the Handschuhsheim district association.

properties.name: Heiliggeistkirche
properties.description:
At the beginning of the 13th century, a small Romanesque basilica Zum Heiligen Geist stood on the site of today's Heiliggeistkirche, which presumably fell victim to a fire at the beginning of the 14th century.

An early Gothic church was built in its place, in which the opening mass for the founding of Heidelberg University took place on October 18, 1386.

Under Ruprecht III, the choir of the church was demolished and replaced by a larger one.

The hall choir was completed in 1410, the nave with the substructure of the tower in 1441.

Louis III laid the foundations for the later famous Palatinate Library, the BIBLIOTECA PALATINA, by having the first books placed in the galleries of the Heiliggeistkirche.

During the reign of Louis V (1508-1544), the tower was further built and completed.

In the course of the Reformation, the church changed several times between Lutheran and Reformed-Calvinist denominations.

In 1563, the Heidelberg Catechism was created as a reformed confession.

With the Thirty Years' War and the conquest of Heidelberg by Catholic troops, the city and the church became Catholic for many years and Pope Gregory XV had the BIBLIOTECA PALATINA brought to Rome as spoils of war in 1623.

The church was severely damaged during the Palatinate-Orléans War of Succession in 1693.

Almost all of the tomb slabs of the Electors Palatine were destroyed; the one of Elector Ruprecht II has been preserved.

Of the once 5000 books and 3524 manuscripts, only 885 were returned to Heidelberg in 1816, all others remained in the Vatican.

In the following two centuries, both Catholics and Protestants laid claim to the church, so that Catholic mass was celebrated in the choir and Protestant services in the nave, separated by a dividing wall.

It was not until 1936 that an agreement was reached with the Catholic Church; the church became the property of the Protestant Church in Baden.

On the Feast of St. John in 1936, the Protestant Heiliggeist parish celebrated services in a church without a dividing wall for the first time again.

properties.name: Jesuitenkirche
properties.description:
The Jesuit Church (correct name: Pfarrkirche Heiliger Geist und St. Ignatius) is the largest and most important church in Heidelberg alongside the Heiliggeistkirche and forms the architectural focal point of the former Jesuit quarter in the old town in the immediate vicinity of Universitätsplatz. Today, it is the main church of the Roman Catholic Holy Spirit parish in Heidelberg.

In 1685, the Electoral Palatinate fell to Elector Philipp Wilhelm (1685-90) of the Catholic Palatinate-Neuburg line; he returned the Catholic Church to the Palatinate and called the Jesuits to Heidelberg. After the destruction of Heidelberg by the French in 1693, Elector Johann Wilhelm (1690-1716) wanted to turn Heidelberg into a center of Catholic activity with the help of the Jesuits. The large college building was erected between 1703 and 1711 and construction of the church began immediately afterwards. The Elector provided building land, stones from the Thick Tower of Heidelberg Castle, timber from the manorial forests, sand from the moat and free transportation. The architect Johann Adam Breunig (around 1660-1727) drew up the plan. The first phase of construction work lasted until 1723.  
Elector Johann Wilhelm died in 1716; his brother and successor Karl Philipp fought with the Reformed Church Council over the 80th question of the Heidelberg Catechism and the nave of the Heiliggeistkirche, as a result of which the Elector moved his residence and government to Mannheim in 1720. It was not until 1749 that building work could be resumed thanks to the generosity of Elector Karl Theodor (1742-1799). The nave was already covered the following year and the façade and vaulting were completed in 1751; however, the work dragged on until the late fall of 1759. The Mannheim court architect Franz Wilhelm Rabaliatti (1716-1782), who was also building the Seminarium Carolinum for the Heidelberg Jesuits, was in charge of the construction. After the dissolution of the Jesuit order in 1773, their tasks and institutions were taken over by the Lazarists from 1782 to 1793. In the following years, the church served as a military hospital; since 01.11.1809, it has been the parish church of the Catholic parish of Heilig Geist.  
The baroque interior is no longer preserved today. The altarpiece by the Kaulbach pupil Andreas Müller has been preserved. Elector Frederick the Victorious is buried in a crypt in the north-east corner of the church. To the east of the church portals is the entrance to the former Jesuit College. Originally, the Jesuit facilities included a grammar school (now the Philosophical Seminary) and the Seminarium Carolinum, which is now used by the university administration.

properties.name: Botanischer Garten Heidelberg
properties.description:
Heidelberg Botanical Garden  
Place of recreation with a "green school"

Founded in 1593, the Botanical Garden of Heidelberg University is one of the oldest botanical gardens: important scientific work by Heidelberg botanists is inextricably linked to it and its research and conservation collections are of great importance. There is also a herbarium with unique specimens. The Heidelberg Botanic Garden is a place of scientific research and academic teaching, protects endangered plant species, offers public education programs and is an important institution for the horticultural trade and its training. Last but not least, it is also a place of tranquillity and recreation. The Heidelberg Botanic Garden's Green School offers a wide range of public programs: guided tours and courses, such as "By candlelight through the tropics", or "Making your own natural cosmetics" and even children's birthday parties are on offer. There are also private guided tours on topics such as "Living fossils" or "Carnivorous plants". Offers for school classes and kindergartens impart botanical knowledge with the aim of developing enjoyment in dealing with this living world, to feel appreciation for these natural foundations of life and to motivate a willingness to treat nature with care.

properties.name: Electoral Palatinate Museum Heidelberg
properties.description:
Das Kurpfälzische Museum gehört zu den großen Kultureinrichtungen der Stadt Heidelberg.

Es versammelt einzigartige Bestände zur Historie der Kurpfalz, die viele Jahrhunderte lang zu den bedeutendsten deutschen Territorien gehörte und Weltpolitik machte, zuletzt in den Auseinandersetzungen des Dreißigjährigen Krieges und in den kriegerischen Konflikten mit Ludwig XIV. im Pfälzischen Erbfolgekrieg. Eine Fülle von Objekten vermitteln Geschichte und Lebensgeschichten. Die kostbare Sammlung Frankenthaler Porzellans und das Tafelsilber der letzten Kurfürstin Elisabeth Augusta verweisen auf den Glanz und Repräsentationswillen des Hofes, aber auch auf ein ungestörtes Wirtschaftswachstum im 18. Jh., das erst durch die Napoleonischen Kriege wieder unterbrochen wurde. Den geschichtlichen Wandel zeigt das Altersporträt der Kurfürstin, die sich als Bürgerin in dezent dunkler Kleidung präsentiert. Gemälde durchziehen wie ein roter Faden das gesamte Museum. In der Kurpfalz-Abteilung werden in Art einer Porträtgalerie die herausragenden Protagonisten der Regionalgeschichte vorgestellt, darunter der „Winterkönig“ Friedrich V. mit seiner Gemahlin Elizabeth Stuart, „Liselotte von der Pfalz“ und der Hofnarr Perkeo. Viele Jahrtausende zurück datieren die Bestände der Archäologischen Abteilung, die auf 2 Etagen präsentiert wird. Von der Altsteinzeit (homo heidelbergensis) bis in die Tage der kurpfälzischen Residenz wird die wechselvolle Geschichte Heidelbergs dokumentiert. Damit werden 600 000 Jahre Menschheitsgeschichte weit über die hiesige Region hinaus lebendig. Den weitaus größten Raum nimmt die Römerzeit ein. Versteckte Kostbarkeiten finden sich in der Graphischen Sammlung, die zu den umfangreichsten Südwestdeutschlands gehört. Mit etwa 7.000 Aquarellen und 13.000 Druckgraphiken umfasst die Sammlung Exponate vom ausgehenden Mittelalter bis ins 21. Jh.. Arbeiten regionaler Künstler sind in ihr ebenso vertreten wie herausragende Einzelblätter, zu denen Marc Chagalls „Der blaue Bär“ gehört. Sammlungsschwerpunkte liegen in den Themenbereichen Romantik, Kurpfalz, Porträts, historische Darstellungen und Flugblätter. Sie können nach vorheriger Anfrage im Vorlageraum des Kabinetts eingesehen werden.

Seit Herbst 2020 ist das Kurpfälzische Museum um eine Attraktion reicher: mit der "HD Discovery Station" reist es sich bequem und auf höchstem digitalen Niveau in die Zeit der Kelten und Römer! Mithilfe eines Spielcontrollers können die Besucher auf eine virtuelle Zeitreise gehen. Wie mit einem Gleitschirm fliegen sie über die keltische Höhensiedlung Heiligenberg oder spazieren durch die römischen Siedlungen am Neckarufer. Erfasst wurde eine Fläche von 100 Quadratkilometern, 130 000 Objekte sind bereits integriert. Das Projekt ist ausbaufähig: neueste wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse werden von den Spezialisten der Archäologischen Abteilung des KMH unmittelbar integriert, weitere Zeitebenen sind in Vorbereitung.

properties.name: BODY WORLDS Heidelberg
properties.description:
# BODY WORLDS Museum in Heidelberg - On the trail of happiness

Great love, a carefree life, true friendship ... Everyone strives for happiness. But where does happiness live? Why can't we get enough of it? And why can't we keep happiness forever? The KÖRPERWELTEN Museum in the Altes Hallenbad explores these and other questions about happiness.

It is not only dedicated to the anatomy of humans, their organ functions and questions about health, but also the anatomy of happiness.

Gunther von Hagens and Angelina Whalley are presenting their exhibition on the human body, which was specially designed for Heidelberg, on an area of around 1000 m² in the former men's pool of the old indoor swimming pool. It is a reminder of what is our most precious asset: our own body. The aim of the exhibition is to show visitors the complexity of the human body in a lifelike way and thus sensitize them to their own body in all situations and phases of life.

The exhibition is based on Gunther von Hagens' invention of plastination. The scientist invented the preservation process back in 1977 at the University of Heidelberg and has been perfecting it ever since. His plastinates impress with their extremely precise, scientifically sound preparation as well as their creative, aesthetic and often unusual form of presentation.

More than 45 million people around the world have already been inspired and fascinated by the KÖRPERWELTEN exhibitions, 10 million of them in Germany alone. Never before has an exhibition moved the public so much and changed their view of their own physicality so lastingly as Gunther von Hagens' BODY WORLDS.

properties.name: Universitätsmuseum und Aula der Alten Universität
properties.description: The opening hours can be found on the homepage at [http://www.uni-heidelberg.de/einrichtungen/museen/](http://www.uni-heidelberg.de/einrichtungen/museen/).

properties.name: Heidelberg Zoo
properties.description:
Der Zoo Heidelberg mit wunderschönem Baumbestand ist ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel für die ganze Familie.

Auf Safari durch den Zoo: Über 160 verschiedene Tierarten aus aller Welt laden im Zoo Heidelberg zu einer spannenden Entdeckungsreise ein. Die Roten Pandas verbringen den Tag gerne hoch oben im Geäst und die Sumatra-Tiger lieben es, durch den dichten Bambuswald in ihrem Gehege zu streifen. Kaum zu übersehen sind die leuchtend orange-roten Kubaflamingos auf ihrem See oder die Asiatischen Elefanten, die sich im Sommer gerne im Badebecken abkühlen.

Ebenso wie das Berberlöwenpaar Chalid und Binta, erfreuen sich die Mähnenrobben bei den Besuchern besonderer Beliebtheit. Zweimal täglich, außer freitags, findet an der Robbenanlage eine kommentierte Fütterung mit Training statt. Zoobesucher erhalten dort viele Infos zu den Mähnenrobben und zur Arbeit der Tierpfleger. Vielfältige Aktionstage und Veranstaltungen im Zoo Heidelberg sorgen das ganze Jahr über für Abwechslung. Bei Familien mit Kindern sind das große Spielschiff „Arche“, die Klettertürme und die beiden Wasserspielplätze beliebte Zwischenstationen beim Zoobesuch.

Mit seinem didaktischen Konzept setzt der Zoo Heidelberg auf erlebnisreiche Bildung: Bei Rundgängen mit der Zooschule Heidelberg lernen Kinder sowie Erwachsene Spannendes über die Tiere im Zoo Heidelberg. Im Technik- und Ausstellungsbereich des Explo Heidelberg können wissenschaftliche Phänomene erkundet werden. Der Eintritt für die Explo-Ausstellung ist im Zooeintritt bereits enthalten.

properties.name: Deutsches Verpackungs Museum
properties.description:
The German Packaging Museum is conveniently located in Heidelberg's Old Town. Here you can see a unique collection of interesting and sometimes astonishing goods packaging in a lovingly restored "emergency church".

Located in the heart of Heidelberg's old town, the - first and only - German Packaging Museum is housed in the rooms of a former emergency church. Lovingly renovated and equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure, the building is a real gem that is worth a visit from an architectural point of view alone.

In its rooms, the museum shows the packaging of goods as a reflection of the cultural development of our society. The diverse functions of packaging are presented as well as its historical development: packaging as the result of a creative and artistic achievement. Different exhibition areas present packaging as the result of constant change: artistic and technical innovations have influenced the design of packaging at all times.

The history of industrial goods packaging is also a history of our everyday lives in the 19th and 20th centuries. A number of packaging designs can be traced back to important artists of their time, are real "works of art" and are not just collector's items, but have long been a recognized part of art and design history.

Technical innovation has always had a new face over the past hundred years. The German Packaging Museum therefore also shows those "milestones" that impressively illustrate the varieties of human imagination and creativity through unusual or inventive packaging solutions, and reviews the past with brands that are still popular today.

properties.name: Prinzhorn Collection
properties.description:
The Prinzhorn Collection is a museum for art by people with exceptional mental experiences. Its well-known historical collection comprises around 6,000 works created by inmates of psychiatric institutions between 1840 and 1945.  

This globally unique collection was largely compiled by the art historian and psychiatrist Hans Prinzhorn (1886-1933) during his time as an assistant doctor at the Psychiatric Clinic of Heidelberg University. The best-known artists/authors in the historical collection include Else Blankenhorn, Franz Karl Bühler, Karl Genzel, Paul Goesch, Emma Hauck, August Klett, August Natterer, Agnes Richter, Joseph Schneller, Barbara Suckfüll and Adolf Wölfli.

**The history of the collection**

In 1919-21, Hans Prinzhorn wrote letters to psychiatric clinics in German-speaking countries with the then clinic director Karl Wilmanns, requesting artistic patient works for the establishment of a museum for psychopathological art.

In 1922, Prinzhorn published his richly illustrated study "Bildnerei der Geisteskranken" based on the collection, which appealed to many art lovers and artists of his time and became the surrealists' pictorial bible. Reprinted several times and translated into various languages, the book remains a classic.

In 1938, clinic director Carl Schneider donated works from the collection to the traveling exhibition "Degenerate Art". In the exhibition, they are misused as pathological comparative material for modern art.

Forgotten after the war, the collection was rediscovered by Harald Szeemann in 1963. He shows a selection at the Kunsthalle Bern. National and international exhibitions followed, making the collection famous once again.

In 2001, the collection finally receives its own museum building, a converted old neurology lecture hall on the grounds of the old university hospital in Heidelberg.

**The collection today**

Since 1980, the collection has been growing again through art by psychiatric patients. This newer collection now comprises around 20,000 works. These include works by Friedrich Boss, Gudrun Biersky, Vanda Vieira-Schmidt, Sonja Gerstner, Alfred Stief and Dietrich Orth. In order to be able to regularly present new acquisitions and a permanent exhibition alongside the temporary exhibitions in the future, an extension is planned.

**The Prinzhorn Collection Museum - Exhibitions and Research**

The museum presents three to four themed exhibitions each year. The aim of the museum is to help destigmatize mental illness. By contextualizing and interpreting artistic works that are shaped by exceptional mental experiences and their social consequences, it contributes to the inclusion of affected people. As part of Heidelberg University Hospital, the museum sees itself not only as a museum and exhibition venue, but also as a scientific institution that researches the fate of the artists represented here, their works and overarching issues. For this reason, scientists, artists and other interested parties can view the museum's archive and depot holdings by appointment. The museum's academic staff will be happy to provide information and assistance.

properties.name: Old Town Heidelberg
properties.description:
With its romantic alleyways, quaint traditional restaurants, and historic buildings, the Old Town is considered the heart and historic center of Heidelberg.

It is world-famous for its unique triad of city, mountains, and river. Around 10,000 Heidelberg residents live in the old town and, like visitors, appreciate the short distances, the multitude of [cultural and leisure facilities](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/culture), the attractive [shopping opportunities](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/entdecken/shopping "shopping opportunities") and the extensive [range of restaurants and hotels](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/planen/uebernachten "range of restaurants and hotels"). In addition, the old town is the founding seat of Germany's oldest university, the "Ruperto Carola." Students from near and far attend Heidelberg University, giving the old town its lively, youthful, and international flair.

The old town covers around 1,380 hectares, of which only 9.8 percent is built up. The district is characterized by the forest area of the Königstuhl, which at 564 meters is one of the highest mountains in the Odenwald.

**Highlights:** [Castle](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/schloss-heidelberg)

[Mountain railway](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/heidelberger-bergbahnen) [Market square](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/marktplatz) [University library](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/universitaetsbibliothek)

[Main street](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/hauptstrasse) [Old bridge](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/alte-bruecke) [Grain market](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/kornmarkt)

properties.name: Dinkelsbühl
properties.description: NOT A FREE MUSEUM - DINKELSBÜHL IS A LIVING PRESENCE Towers and gates surround one of the best-preserved medieval towns in Germany. Not only the people of Dinkelsbühl think so: Focus magazine voted the old town the most beautiful in the country. An insider tip and time travel destination, according to the editors. Ponds, meadows and parks form a green frame and surround the medieval core like a precious jewel. Protected by the defensive wall, magnificent patrician houses such as the "Hezelhof" and the "Deutsches Haus" are reminiscent of Dinkelsbühl's heyday in the 15th and 16th centuries. To this day, the Gothic St. George's Minster in the heart of the town and the spacious Heiliggeistspital hospital are stone witnesses to civic pride and strength of faith. SUMMER HIGHLIGHTS In July, the colors of summer dominate: at the open-air games in the garden at the Wehrgang or at the Kinderzeche. The historical festival is based on a legend according to which the children of Dinkelsbühl saved their hometown from the Swedes during the Thirty Years' War. SEE AND UNDERSTAND You can trace the town's history at the House of History - of War and Peace, where the past is brought back to life in exciting productions. If you miss the Kinderzeche in July, you should plan a visit to the Zeughaus der Kinderzeche. The mighty half-timbered building houses the festival's extensive collection of weapons, costumes and equipment. The museum counterpoint is provided by the 3rd Dimension Museum in the town mill, which presents optical illusions and holography, among other things. OVERNIGHT AND ENJOYMENT The diverse gastronomy with its beer gardens in summer invites you to linger. The modern hotel industry offers something for everyone, from 5-star hotels to guesthouses or vacation apartments. "LISTEN TO YOUR PEOPLE AND LET THEM TELL YOU..." Relaxation is also the motto of the evening tour with the Dinkelsbühl night watchman. In summer, he starts daily at 9 pm in front of St. George's Minster and takes his guests on a journey into the past. FOREST MEANS ENJOYING In the second half of the year, the Open Monument Day in September and the Fish Harvest Week at the beginning of November invite you to go on epicurean forays. On Open Monument Day, towers and buildings that otherwise remain hidden from the public open their doors. During the Fish Harvest Week, the focus is on tried-and-tested and new variations of carp, pike and co. A culinary highlight that no fish lover should miss. The MOST BEAUTIFUL TIME OF YEAR For many people, this is Advent and Christmas. The city presents itself festively shining within its old walls. In December, the Dinkelsbühl Christmas market attracts visitors with all the pre-Christmas delights their palate desires: mulled wine, bratwurst and fragrant gingerbread, plus typical Christmas and gift items such as toys, spices and Christmas tree decorations. Under the motto "Ihr Kinderlein kommet", Dinkelsbühl commemorates Christoph von Schmid, the town's famous son. He wrote the lyrics to the world-famous Christmas carol. With all this heritage, Dinkelsbühl creates a connection with the present day with casual ease: anyone who visits here is right in the middle of the most beautiful Franconian attitude to life. The old town of Dinkelsbühl is one of the "particularly landscape-defining monuments" in Bavaria. The Bavarian State Office for the Preservation of Monuments only classifies a few very special places. In Romantic Franconia, the old towns of Rothenburg ob der Tauber and Bad Windheim, Schillingsfürst Castle and the Hesselberg have a particularly large number of these monuments. Sights Wine market and German House with Renaissance façade, St. Georg Minster, hospital complex, "Malerwinkel" at the Rothenburg pond with park keeper's house and fermentation tower. More information

properties.name: Breig´s Motorrad- und Spielzeugmuseum
properties.description:
Walter Breig’s museum in Zell am Harmersbach is a true feast for the eyes of any motorcycle fan. Mobility, combined with sportiness, creativity, idealism, and passion—that’s what his motorcycle and toy museum has stood for since its opening on May 1, 2015.

Spanning over 900 square meters, the museum presents a unique comprehensive exhibition of many milestones in motorcycle history in a light-filled hall. This permanent exhibition features over 80 historically significant original vehicles from the past nine decades. From Adler, BMW, and Kreidler to NSU and Zündapp, visitors can experience the spirit of the times in motorized two-wheelers up close, making every motorcyclist’s and collector’s heart beat faster.


Walter Breig, a passionate collector of time-honored two-wheeled machines for 60 years, tinkerer, and gifted restorer, is the initiator and driving force behind this impressive exhibition of roadworthy motorcycles and “firehorses” gleaming with chrome and paint—all masterfully and lovingly restored by Walter Breig himself.


And—take note!—the museum opens up a second exciting dimension with its magnificent collection of tin toys: over 2,000 exhibits are displayed in more than 80 man-sized display cases, offering an overview of the cultural history of toys: Toy cars, motorcycles, carriages, and, of course, the good old train—a true delight for children and adults alike.


Why and how does such a large private collection come to be? Ask Mr. Breig yourself during your visit; he’ll be happy to answer your questions and will gladly show you his “favorite exhibits.”

Step into a world full of wonder and imagination, let yourself be transported back in time, and join us on a journey through the ages.


There’s no art without a patron: Erwin Junker, owner of the Maschinen Fabrik in Nordrach and proprietor of the museum hall, is a dedicated supporter and benefactor working behind the scenes, providing Walter Breig with advice and assistance in all matters—a driving force behind the new museum.

properties.name: Viewing platform on the "Druckele"
properties.description:
The Lehberg near Gaildorf attracts visitors with the “Druckele” and a modern observation deck. Nestled along the “FeenSpuren” premium hiking trail, the deck offers hikers fascinating views across the Kocher Valley all the way to the Hohenlohe Plain.

Lehberg and “Druckele”

To the west of Gaildorf lies the Lehberg, a striking spur of the Limpurger Mountains. Together with the neighboring Kirgel, it forms a forested ridge that serves as a local recreation area for the region. The highest point of this ridge is known locally as “Druckele.” It is precisely at this exposed spot that a special attraction for nature lovers is located: an architecturally striking wooden viewing platform.

Best View

The structure was built as part of efforts to enhance the region’s appeal to tourists and blends harmoniously into the forest landscape. From the platform, a sweeping panoramic view opens up to the north. The view sweeps across the deeply incised Kochertal valley and the “Westheimer Pforte,” and on clear days extends across the Hohenlohe Plain all the way to the Einkorn near Schwäbisch Hall.

Premium Hiking

The Druckele is accessible via the certified premium hiking trail “FeenSpuren – Kirgel Ausblicke.” The approximately 6.4-kilometer loop trail follows nature trails that pass directly by the platform. Nearby are the Kernerturm tower and the barbecue area and playground at Kirgel, making the Lehberg a versatile destination in the Limpurger Land region.

properties.name: AliSa adventure trail Wolfslochrunde
properties.description:
Start at the hiking parking lot. This can be found by car when driving on the B292 from Helmstadt to Waibstadt, shortly after Helmstadt on the right-hand side.

There are two concrete field paths leading off from here, please take the one on the right. Then it goes past fields, along the Auerbach and after approx. 300 m you cross a bridge.


Continue along the concreted field path until you finally reach the edge of the Forlewald forest.

This is the first highlight of the route. The small pond is a water conservation area, but there is still plenty to discover here (please follow the signs around the pond).

Pass the pond on the left. You are now on a beautiful forest path with lots to discover.  
At first you will pass the Wolfslochhütte hut on a slight uphill section, then continue through the forest. After a short stretch, you reach the Wolfslocheiche oak tree.

On reaching the mountain, turn right onto the forest path and then right again after a short distance at the crossroads.

Now it's always slightly downhill.

Here you will discover some ant hills - some are even fenced in.

Continue towards the Alfred-Winterbauer beech tree.

Following the path further downhill, you reach the Wolfsloch beech. In spring 2020, the beech was still in full sap, but unfortunately it has since died off.

Finally, you come back to the pond.  
From here, the same concreted field path leads back to the hiking parking lot.

properties.name: Vegetation and Geology Nature Trail
properties.description:
Both trails lead through scenic but steep terrain in places. The geological trail is currently being revised. ## Geological nature trail

The geological nature trail **begins at the Junghans company parking lot** on Geißhaldenstraße and leads up to the [**Hohenschramberg castle ruins**](http://www.schwarzwald-tourismus.info/Media/Attraktionen/Burgruine-Hohenschramberg), past the **Lauterbach waterfall**. Along the way, you will cross the impressive main faults of Schramberg twice. Numerous **information boards** help to decipher the traces of the Black Forest's geological history, which dates back over 300 million years. We invite you to discover the natural heritage of the Schlossberg on this **approx. 1.5-hour hike** (elevation difference approx. 200 m). ## The vegetation trail **Geology and flora** are closely related. It therefore makes sense to combine the vegetation trail and the geological trail in one hike. The vegetation trail **begins at the end of the geological trail** at Hohenschramberg Castle and leads back to Schramberg via the shorter descent from the castle ruins (walking time approx. 45 minutes). Along the trail, you can marvel at the **extraordinary diversity of the protected flora and fauna**. With the help of information boards, you can trace the dramatic changes that the flora has undergone over the last millennium.

properties.name: Schillergarten
properties.description:
From a cemetery to a green oasis amid the hustle and bustle of traffic: Gaildorf’s Schillergarten holds a fascinating history.

Today’s Schillergarten combines church history with the legacy of a world-renowned poet. Where a small green space now defies the street noise, the town’s first cemetery stood from 1710 to 1906. At the time of its establishment, the site was still located a short distance outside the gates of the town center itself, to allow room for the town’s growth. A massive stone cemetery wall completely enclosed the consecrated grounds, clearly demarcating the resting place of the dead.

The history of burials in Gaildorf, however, goes back even further. Originally, the town’s deceased were buried in what is now the district of Münster. For a long time, the parish church responsible for Gaildorf was located in Münster. It was not until 1433 that Gaildorf itself became an independent parish. Nevertheless, the citizens did not abandon their burial site in Münster, so burials continued to take place there. It was not until 1710 that the cemetery was moved to Gaildorf.

After the new cemetery opened in December 1906, the old site was decommissioned. The cemetery owes its current name to the famous Schiller family of poets. Karl von Schiller, Friedrich Schiller’s eldest son, worked as a district forester at the nearby Reichenberg Castle in the 1820s. He fell in love with Louise Friederike Locher, the daughter of Gaildorf’s chief medical officer. On February 12, 1825, the couple married in Gaildorf. On the 100th anniversary of the poet’s death in 1905, a Schiller monument was erected on what was then the cemetery grounds.

To this day, fragments of the old cemetery wall, scattered gravestones, and a stone statue of Christ dating back some 140 years serve as reminders of the site’s sacred past.

There is plenty of space here to play and let off steam.

properties.name: Brentano House (13)
properties.description: Kommt man aus dem früher eher bescheidenen Wohnquartier der Frauengasse heraus, steht man direkt neben dem schönsten Profanbau der Stadt, dem Brentanohaus. Die Handelskompanie Brentano-Monticelli & Co., die hauptsächlich mit dem in Günzburg und in der Umgebung gewebten Leinenstoff handelte, ließ sich dieses stattliche Wohn- und Geschäftshaus um 1750 errichten. An der Durchfahrt (heute Hauseingang) kann man die Größe damaliger Fuhrwerke erahnen. Der Merkurkopf (Gott der Händler) ist eine Zutat des 20. properties.description:
Der Spielplatz befindet sich am Straßenrand neben einem Bibergraben. Die Gegend ist verkehrsarm. Auf dem zaunlosen Gelände gibt es viele alte Baume, welche viel Schatten spenden.

Am Straßenrand kann geparkt werden.

properties.name: Alpine Bowling at Landgasthof Hotel Linde
properties.description:
At the Landgasthof Linde, an Alpine bowling experience awaits you on a total of four modern bowling lanes. Here you can roll a few relaxed frames in a sociable atmosphere or compete in exciting matches. Sports fans also get their money's worth, as current sporting events are broadcast on Sky.

The Bowling Bar is not only a place for leisure fun, but also ideal for company celebrations, private parties, or children's birthdays.  
Advance reservation by phone at +49 8221-367 400 is required.

properties.name: Hospital of the United Charitable Foundations of Nördlingen
properties.description:
Fachabteilungen: Chirurgie, Innere Medizin, Kardiologie, Anästhesie, Palliativmedizin  
Belegabteilungen: Gynäkologie, Geburtshilfe, Hals, Nasen, Ohren, Urologie, Augenheilkunde, Ambulante Operationen, Liposuktion

properties.name: Brauereimuseum Autenried
properties.description: Nowhere else does the brewing industry boast such a long tradition. The privately owned “Schlossbrauerei Autenried,” located in the heart of the Günzburg district, is committed to nurturing and preserving the rich history of brewing. To this end, a small, charming brewery museum has been established beneath the historic roof trusses of the brewery inn, in the former “Niederes Schloss.” Through lovingly restored historical exhibits, visitors can gain a vivid understanding of how beer was brewed in Swabia from hops, malt, and water not too long ago.

properties.name: Kahbachweg Playground
properties.description:
Am Ortsrand von Schnelldorf ist der Spielplatz aufzufinden. Er befindet sich in einer Sackgasse, wodurch die Gefahr von Durchgangsverkehr nicht vorhanden ist.

Zudem ist er nicht umzäunt. Parken kann man neben dem Spielplatz und am Rande des Kabachweges.

properties.name: Museum Illertissen - Geschichten und Geschichte im Schloss (Museum Illertissen - Stories and history in the castle)
properties.description: Das ehemalige Heimatmuseum hat einen neuen Namen und ein neues Gesicht als zeitgemäße Präsentation Illertissens und seiner Bewohner:Unter dem Motto „Geschichten und Geschichte“ lernen die Besucher auf ihrer unterhaltsamen Zeitreise durch die Jahrhunderte neben der Vielfalt der Stadt u. a. die ehemaligen Schlossherren, einen gewitzten Posthalter und selbstbestimmte Damen kennen. Und auch gegenwärtige Einwohner Illertissens kommen zu Wort.

properties.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
No matter how or from where you approach the city, the mighty city wall magically draws you in and promises a different world behind the gates.  
Curious, you enter and soon discover that your feelings and premonitions were not wrong.  
The painters and writers of the Romantic period who were drawn to Rothenburg felt the same way much earlier. "I thought I had suddenly been transported to the Middle Ages", wrote Ludwig Richter in his memoirs around 150 years ago, and one involuntarily searches the streets for the motifs that could have inspired Karl Spitzweg's famous paintings.

The old town of Rothenburg ob der Tauber is one of the "particularly landscape-defining monuments" in Bavaria. The Bavarian State Office for the Preservation of Monuments only classifies a few very special places. In Romantic Franconia, the old towns of Bad Windheim and Dinkelsbühl, Schillingsfürst Castle and the Hesselberg have a particularly large number of these monuments.

[More information](http://www.romantisches-franken.de/Staedte)

properties.name: Wünsch Lake
properties.description:
Nestled among large old trees lies a small, dreamy lake, divided in two by a bridge. In the northern part, swimmers get their money’s worth. The broad bathing cove creates a holiday feeling. South of the bridge, the diving area beckons. In this area there are three springs that provide slightly cooler and wonderfully clear water.

**Facilities:** large sunbathing lawn, picnic benches and tables, restaurant with beer garden

properties.name: District model garden of the Neu-Ulm district
properties.description:
The 9,000-square-metre district model garden of the Neu-Ulm district offers visitors inspiration and tips on garden design. Magnificent flowers, fragrant roses, medicinal herbs, juicy fruit and fresh vegetables are on display.

For many amateur gardeners, it has become a cherished tradition to visit our district-owned horticultural education centre several times a year.

Guided group tours are available on request by prior arrangement.

As a new highlight, an environmental pavilion was built as a "Green Classroom" as part of a LEADER project for environmental education for school classes, youth groups and adult education regardless of the weather. Adjacent to the orchard variety conservation garden, it complements the district model garden's broad educational programme for promoting garden culture and orchard meadow ecology in the Neu-Ulm district.

The "Conservation Garden for the Diversity of Pome Fruit in the Neu-Ulm District" was newly created in 2020 as an extension of the district model garden as part of a LEADER project to preserve endangered regional varieties of apples and pears. The orchard meadow with 50 standard fruit trees serves to preserve and safeguard the cultural heritage of the region.

Representatives of the local horticultural associations are available to answer visitors' questions from early May to early October on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays in the afternoons.

**[You can watch a short film about the district model garden at this link.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NV_3aFffVDo&feature=youtu.be)**

[**Directions by public transport**](http://www.ding.eu/ding/XSLT_TRIP_REQUEST2?language=de&place_destination=Wei%C3%9Fenhorn&name_destination=Kreismustergarten&type_destination=poi&sessionID=0)

properties.name: Sängermuseum (Singer Museum)
properties.description: Die Geschichte des vereinsmäßig organisierten Chorgesangs, von den ersten Männergesangsvereinen im 19. Jh. bis zur heutigen Massenbewegung, steht im Zentrum des Sängermuseums. Das einzige Chormuseum Deutschlands präsentiert zahlreiche Vereinsgegenstände, Noten, schriftliche Dokumente, Klangbeispiele, Fotografien und Filme.

properties.name: Landkäserei Herzog
properties.description:
Die Heimat der Landkäserei Herzog liegt im bayerisch schwäbischen Voralpenland, am Fuße des Klosters Roggenburg. Seit 1995 stellen Firmeninhaber Walter Herzog und seine Frau Gerlinde hier ihre vielfältigen Käsespezialitäten her.

Die Milch dafür liefern 25 Landwirte aus der Region, denn Regionalität gehört in der Landkäserei Herzog ebenso zur Firmenphilosophie wie die traditionelle Herstellung ihrer Produkte.

Das breit angelegte Sortiment umfasst verschiedene Sorten von Frisch-, Schnitt- und Hartkäsen aus Kuh- und Ziegenmilch und wird national über den Groß- und Fachhandel vertrieben.

**In dem Käseladen in Weißenhorn wartet die komplette Produktvielflat der Landkäserei Herzog.**

Hier können die Produkte erworben werden

- [Onlineshop](https://landkaeserei-herzog.de/shop/)
- [Märkte & Handel](https://landkaeserei-herzog.de/maerkte-und-handel/)

Die Landkäserei Herzog ist auch auf zahlreichen Wochenmärkten vertreten, z.B. Neu-Ulm, diverse Märkte in Ulm, Weißenhorn, Pfaffenhofen, Illertissen und viele mehr. 

[**Anfahrt mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln**](http://www.ding.eu/ding/XSLT_TRIP_REQUEST2?language=de&place_destination=Roggenburg&name_destination=Stoffenrieder%20Stra%C3%9Fe%201&type_destination=address&sessionID=0)

properties.name: Engelhardmühle
properties.description:
The Engelhardmühle Attenhofen has been family-owned since 1413, making it the oldest family-run business in the entire region.


In the [**mill shop**](https://www.engelhardmuehle.de/muehlenladen/)

you can shop. There you will find a wide range of flours and grain products. The mill processes exclusively regional grain from Swabia and the neighboring districts.


In addition, the mill shop offers a large selection of baking ingredients, mueslis, pasta, oils, honey, and much more...


[**Directions by public transport**](http://www.ding.eu/ding/XSLT_TRIP_REQUEST2?language=de&place_destination=Wei%C3%9Fenhorn&name_destination=Engelhardm%C3%BChle%201&type_destination=address&sessionID=0)

properties.name: Roggenburg Monastery
properties.description:
Bereits seit mehr als 900 Jahren leben und wirken die Prämonstratenser in und um Roggenburg. Diese beeindruckende Tradition schaffte den Sprung ins 21. Jahrhundert , denn nach der Restaurierung der Gebäudeanlage und der barock angelegten Außenanlagen erstrahlt das Kloster in neuem Glanz.

Die Klosterkirche, das Klostermuseum sowie der Klostergarten sind zu jeder Jahreszeit ein beindruckend schönes Erlebnis.  

- [Klostermuseum](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/klostermuseum-roggenburg)  
- [Klostergasthof](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/gastro/klostergasthof-roggenburg) mit Hotel
- [Klosterladen](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/klosterladen)
- [Bildungszentrum für Familie, Umwelt und Kultur](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/bildungszentrum-fuer-familie-umwelt-und-kultur)  
- [Kirchen- und Klosterführung](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/fuehrung-roggenburg-kloster-und-kirche)
- [Klostergarten](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/klostergarten-roggenburg) mit Efeu-Labyrinth und Kräutergarten  
- [Lauschtour "Rund ums Kloster Roggenburg"](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/tour/rund-ums-kloster-roggenburg)
- [Wanderwege rund um Roggenburg](https://www.roggenburg.de/tourismus-and-kultur/ausflugsziel/wanderwege)  
- [Walderlebniszentrum](https://www.landkreis.neu-ulm-tourismus.de/poi/walderlebniszentrum-roggenburg)  

[Direkt zur virtuellen Klosterführung](https://fuehrung.kloster-roggenburg.de/)

properties.name: Schäfertanz-Kabinett (Shepherd dance cabinet)
properties.description: The Rothenburg brotherhood of shepherds has met annually since 1472 for the Shepherds' Day with a church service and feast. The young shepherds danced with the citizens' daughters. The exhibition in the gatehouse of St Wolfgang's Church (15th century) documents shepherding in the Rothenburg area and the custom of this joyful dance, which was revived at a carnival event in 1911

properties.name: Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum
properties.description: Over 1000 years of legal history on an exhibition area of around 3000 m²: the Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum (Medieval Crime Museum) houses an important collection of legal history. In addition to instruments of torture and devices for the execution of corporal, life and honour punishments, the museum also exhibits valuable paintings, prints, engravings, seals and law books. The most prominent exhibits are the so-called Iron Maiden of Nuremberg, which Bram Stoker also adapted into literature, and replicas of the imperial insignia.

properties.name: Toppler-Schlösschen (Toppler Castle)
properties.description: The picturesque Toppler-Schlösschen (Toppler-Schlösschen) is somehow reminiscent of an oversized birdhouse: the small moated castle, built in 1388/89 for the then mayor Heinrich Toppler, is part defence tower, part residential building. The fully preserved building is furnished with furniture from the 16th to the 19th century.

properties.name: Burggarten Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
The beautifully landscaped Castle Garden, with its geometric garden layout from the 17th/18th century and 8 sandstone figures representing the four seasons and the four elements, is well worth a visit. From here you have a wonderful view over the southern part of the town, of the Double Bridge and Kobolzell Church toward the Tauber Valley, as well as of Toppler Castle, built in 1388.

The site is the location of the Imperial Castle of the Hohenstaufen, which was destroyed by an earthquake in 1356.

properties.name: St. John's Church Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
Ab 1600 wurde das Dachgeschoss der Johanniskirche zum größten städtischen Getreidespeicher ausgebaut.

Hinter der Johanniskirche finden Sie einen der schönsten Ausblicke. In der Straße An der Eich führt der Blick von einer Kanzel aus über den Weinberg Richtung Taubertal und Burggarten.

properties.name: Alt-Rothenburger Handwerkerhaus (Old Rothenburg craftsman house)
properties.description: Nie wirklich modernisiert und deshalb wie aus dem Mittelalter herbeigezaubert steht das Häuschen mitten in der Rothenburger Altstadt. Das Baudenkmal aus dem Jahre 1270 beherbergte über sieben Jahrhunderte verschiedenste Handwerker. Die Ausstellung führt Wohn- und Arbeitsmilieu vergangener Zeiten eindrücklich vor Augen.

properties.name: RothenburgMuseum
properties.description: Here you can learn all about the eventful history of the former imperial city of Rothenburg, highlight: monastery kitchen from the 13th century

properties.name: Bayerisches Schulmuseum (Bavarian School Museum)
properties.description: How and what did the first humans learn? Have there always been exercise books? What did lessons look like 100 years ago? The Bayerisches Schulmuseum (Bavarian School Museum) presents the history of learning and teaching from the Stone Age to the present in a vivid and entertaining way. For example, in the "Schreibstube", which is dedicated to the development of writing. Here you can write on Egyptian papyrus, scratch on wax tablets and try out letterpress printing with lead type. In the historical classroom from 1920, today's school classes can experience the strict discipline of past generations of pupils. Another section provides insights into the Jewish school system in Bavaria from the early 19th century to the present day.

properties.name: Vogel - Beobachtungsturm am Mooswaldsee
properties.description:
Observe the full diversity of feathered life with the permanently installed telescope on the birdwatching tower at Mooswaldsee. Information boards help you identify the birds. And there is often also an ornithologist on site. From the observation tower, the view extends beyond the lake to nature-friendly managed meadow areas, the Leipheimer Moos and the wild Mooswald - in other words, around 500 hectares of natural landscape. Here you can experience the impressive spectacle when, in the evening, hundreds of greylag geese fly in on rushing wings over the observation tower to Mooswaldsee to spend the night. The little ringed plover can also be observed at close range while raising its young. On the open forest area north of the tower, a nesting platform specially for ospreys was installed in 2015 - perhaps you will be lucky enough to spot one of these elegant birds of prey.

You can reach the birdwatching tower at Mooswaldsee near Günzburg by turning west off Heidenheimer Strasse between Günzburg and Niederstotzingen at the Mooswald lakes. After about 1 km, park your vehicle. After passing a barrier, you will reach the tower after about 1.5 km.

properties.name: Lauschtour "Through the Leipheim Moor"
properties.description:
...interessant, humorvoll und überraschend.

**HINWEIS: Aus Sicherheitsgründen ist der Bohlenweg momentan nicht begehbar. Die Lauschtour kann mit einer kleinen Streckenänderung jedoch durchgeführt werden.**

Schwarzer Torf und tiefe Tümpel: Erkunden Sie hier eine der mystischsten Landschaften in Bayerisch-Schwaben. Hier hören Sie den Pulsschlag eines wiederbewässerten Moors! Der Biologe erklärt faszinierende Naturphänomene. Außerdem gibt’s Interviews mit ehemaligen Torfstechern und wir schauen bei einer Straußenfarm vorbei. Das pickt!

**Infos zur Strecke**

Streckenlänge: 4,2 km

Schwierigkeit: leicht

Gehzeit: ca. 2 Stunden - ab Lauschpunkt 4 befinden Sie sich im Naturschutzgebiet. Bitte verlassen Sie die Wege nicht und nehmen Sie Rücksicht auf Tiere und Pflanzen.


**Mit App oder iPod auf Tour:**

Smartphone-Besitzer nutzen einfach unsere kostenlose Lauschtour-App.

Alles, was Sie brauchen, sind Smartphone-Kopfhörer oder die Lautsprecher-Funktion und etwas Zeit und Muse zum Wandern oder Radeln. Und schon eröffnet sich Ihnen ganz großes Kino für die Ohren mit reizvollen, unkonventionell gestalteten Audio-Beiträgen.

Und so funktioniert`s:

**1. App laden**

Kostenlos im App Store und im Google Play Store unter „Bayerisch-Schwaben-Lauschtour“. iPods gibt es auch zum Ausleihen. (mehr hierzu im Internet)

**2. App starten**

**3. Loslauschen**

Starten Sie Ihre Tour zu Fuß (oder ggfls. per Fahrrad). Von Lauschpunkt zu Lauschpunkt erwarten Sie spannende Audio- Erlebnisse – fantasievoll vertont und journalistisch recherchiert.

**Tipp:** Laden Sie die App bereits vor Ihrem Start zur Lauschtour und speichern sie diese offline ab – so sind Sie unabhängig von der Verbindungsleistung.

Danke, dass Sie die Einzigartigkeit der Natur bewahren und stets auf den Wegen bleiben, keinen Müll hinterlassen und auf Lärm verzichten.

properties.name: Lauschtour "Keltenpfad Ichenhausen"
properties.description:
**Current notice: Lauschpunkt 6 marked on the maps is currently not accessible. The audio tour ends at the Celtic farmstead (Lauschpunkt 5), where you can now get even more detailed information.**

The most famous Celts are called Asterix and Obelix — because the term Celts comes from the Latin CELTAE or GALLI. Although the little Gaulish village was not located in the family and children’s region, you can also follow in the footsteps of the Celts in the Günzburg district.

At 6 listening points — starting from the parking lot at the cemetery in Ichenhausen — the lives of the Celts and druids are presented acoustically.

Set off on an exciting search for clues, past burial mounds, sacred trees, and a nearly vanished fortification in the forest. The highlight of the tour: the lovingly reconstructed Celtic farmstead.


You can enjoy the listening experience in the open air in two ways:

Via the app, which is available free of charge in the App Store and Google Play Store under “Bayerisch-Schwaben-Lauschtour,” or via iPod, which can be borrowed from the Bavarian School Museum.


**Route length**: 3 km from the first to the last listening point

**Difficulty:** easy

**Walking time:** approx. 35 minutes (one way)


**iPod rental station**: Bavarian School Museum Ichenhausen, Schlossplatz 3-5, 89335 Ichenhausen, Tel. 08223/6189

properties.name: Backhaus Rittershausen
properties.description:
The origins of today's Hessian bakehouses date back to the middle of the 16th century: Count Johann VI of Nassau-Dillenburg decreed in the "Wood and Forest Ordinance" of 18 January 1562: "In every village, several common baking ovens are to be decreed".

On the one hand, communal baking was intended to save wood, as resources were slowly becoming scarce in the region due to the immense consumption of wood, for example for iron smelting.

On the other hand, the fire risk for the farms, which were mostly built of wood, clay and straw, with their dwellings and stables, was reduced by a separate location of the now isolated bakehouses.

As a result of this ordinance, numerous village community bakehouses were built.

Due to the exchange of information - trade, marriage and itinerant trades - that went beyond the borders of the lordship, this advantageous model soon became popular throughout Hesse.

In the mid-19th century, communal bakehouse culture experienced a renaissance, starting in the then Prussian provinces in what are now Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse.

In 1846/1847, crop failures caused great hardship throughout Europe, including in the Kingdom of Prussia, which included the small town of Weyerbusch in the Westerwald.

When the government issued flour, mayor Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen - who is also considered the founding father of the cooperative system - initiated a "bread association".

The allotted flour was processed in a specially built bakehouse.

The bread baked here could be distributed to the needy population at a favourable price.

Neighbouring villages throughout the Westerwald, the Lahn-Dill mountains, the Burgwald and the Schwalm soon took up the idea of the "baking house and baking house association".

Today there are many bakehouses whose foundation stones were laid in the same era.

The art of baking good bread in a bakehouse has always required a great deal of experience and has been a community activity.

It began with the selection and cutting of suitable wood, the nightly heating of the oven and the determination of the baking sequence.

This was decided in advance by the baking community, often by lot.

The bread dough itself was usually made individually in advance according to a home recipe and carried to the bakehouse.

Not only the choice of flour, but also the temperature at which the loaves of bread were put into the oven with the pusher was decisive for good success.

The time during which the bread remained in the oven was used for communicative exchange among the "Backesbäcker/innen" and was therefore important for village cohesion.

This traditional village bakehouse system was an integral part of the local supply almost from the middle of the 19th century until the 20th century.

Due to technical developments, many households have had their own electric ovens since the mid-1950s, so that communal baking in bakehouses has become less and less important.

In the 1960s in particular, many bakehouses were demolished.

To this day, however, there are still numerous bakehouses and bakehouse associations, often with a long, unbroken tradition that continues into the present day, which bake in the time-honoured manner and cultivate the village community.

At present, communal baking is experiencing a rebirth in Hesse.

properties.name: Backhaus Offdilln
properties.description:
Die Entstehung der heutigen, hessischen Backhäuser hat einen ihrer initialen Ursprünge in der Mitte des 16. Jahrhunderts:  Graf Johann VI zu Nassau-Dillenburg verfügte in der „Holz- und Waldordnung“ vom 18. Januar 1562: „In jedem Dorf sollen etliche gemeinen Backöfen verordnet werden“. Einerseits sollte durch das gemeinschaftliche Backen Holz eingespart werden, da die Ressourcen aufgrund des immensen Holzverbrauches, zum Beispiel für die Eisenverhüttung, in der Region langsam knapp wurden. Anderseits wurde die Brandgefahr für die zumeist aus Holz, Lehm und Stroh errichteten Höfe mit ihren Wohnhäusern und Stallungen durch eine separate Lage der nun isoliert stehenden Backhäuser gesenkt. Infolge dieser Verordnung entstanden zahlreiche Dorfgemeinschafts-Backhäuser. Durch den, über die landesherrschaftlichen Grenzen hinausgehenden Informationsaustausch – Handel, Heirat und Wander-Handwerk – machte dieses vorteilhafte Modell schnell hessenweit Schule.

Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts erfuhr die gemeinschaftliche Backhauskultur eine Renaissance, ausgehend von den damals preußischen Provinzen im heutigen Rheinland-Pfalz und Hessen. In den Jahren 1846/1847, sorgten Missernten in ganz Europa für große Not, so auch im Königreich Preußen, zu dem der kleine Ort Weyerbusch, im Westerwald, zählte. Als die Regierung Mehl ausgeben ließ, initiierte Bürgermeister Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen - der auch als Gründungsvater des Genossenschaftswesens gilt - einen „Brodverein“. Das zugeteilte Mehl wurde in einem eigens erbauten Backhaus verarbeitet. Das hier gemeinschaftlich gebackene Brot konnte, zu einem günstigen Preis, an die Not leidende Bevölkerung verteilt werden. Sehr schnell griffen die Idee des „Backhaus samt Backhausverein“ benachbarte Orte im ganzen Westerwald, im Lahn-Dill-Bergland und dem Burgwald bis zur Schwalm auf. So finden sich heute viele Backhäuser, deren Grundsteinlegung in derselben Epoche erfolgte.

Die Kunst des guten Brotbackens im Backhaus erforderte schon immer ein hohes Maß an Erfahrung und war gemeinschaftsprägend. Es begann schon bei der Auswahl und des Schlagens des geeigneten Holzes, dem nächtlichen Anheizen des Ofens und der Festlegung der Backreihenfolge. Diese wurde von der Backhausgemeinschaft im Vorfeld festgelegt, oft entschied das Los. Der Brotteig selbst wurde in der Regel nach hauseigenem Rezept individuell im Vorfeld hergestellt und zum Backhaus getragen. Entscheidend für das gute Gelingen war nicht nur die Auswahl des Mehles, sondern insbesondere auch die Temperatur, bei der die Brotlaibe mit dem Schieber in den Ofen geschoben wurden. Die Zeit, in der das Brot im Ofen verweilte, wurde zum kommunikativen Austausch der „Backesbäcker/innen“ untereinander genutzt und war daher für den dörflichen Zusammenhalt von wichtiger Bedeutung. Dieses traditionelle, dörfliche Backhauswesen war fast von der Mitte des 19. bis in jene des 20. Jahrhunderts fester Bestandteil der örtlichen Versorgung. Durch die technische Entwicklung besaßen seit Mitte der 1950iger Jahre viele Haushalte einen eigenen elektrischen Backofen, sodass das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Backhäusern mehr und mehr an Bedeutung verlor. Insbesondere in den 60iger Jahren wurden viel Backhäuser abgerissen. Bis heute jedoch bestehen noch immer zahlreiche Backhäuser und Backhausvereine mit einer oftmals langen, ungebrochenen Tradition bis in die Gegenwart hinein, die in altbewährter Weise backen und die Dorfgemeinschaft pflegen. Gegenwärtig erlebt das gemeinschaftliche Backen in Hessen eine Wiedergeburt.

Text: Naturpark Lahn-Dill-Bergland

Das Backhaus Offdilln

in welchem Jahr das Offdillner Gemeindebackhaus erbaut wurde, ist vermutlich nicht überliefert worden. Jedenfalls ist bis jetzt noch kein schriftlicher Hinweis über dessen Errichtung bekannt geworden. Nach Meinung von Gebäude Experten des hessischen Denkmalschutzes dürfte dieses aber um 1800 erfolgt sein. Ob dieser Bau schon einen gemeindeeigenen Vorgänger hatte oder ob bis dahin die Dorfleute ihr Brot, wie seit Jahrhunderten gewohnt, in ihren kleinen gemauerten Lehmöfen gebacken haben, ist ebenfalls nicht bekannt. Diese Öfen standen im freien und wurden entweder von einzelnen Familien oder ganzen Gemeinschaften genutzt.

Jeden Samstag nach dem Mittagsläuten wurden die Backreihen durch den Gemeindediener an der Kirchentreppe verlost. Das geschah mittels Loshölzchen, wovon jedes mit einem sogenannten Haubergszeichen versehen war. Diese Haubergs- oder auch Hauszeichen sind uralte Male, die noch aus jener Zeit stammen, als Lesen und Schreiben für die einfachen Leute noch gänzlich unbekannt war. Bei der Verlosung wurden die einzelnen Hölzchen in aller Regel von einer der beteiligten Frauen aus ihrer Schürzentasche gezogen. Die Backreihen begannen am frühen Montagvormittag, wobei die erste Reihe stets für das erneute Anheizen des Backofens zu sorgen hatte. Dieser wurde zwar die ganze Woche über auf Temperatur gehalten, blieb aber über Sonntag unbeheizt und war demensprechend am Montag abgekühlt. Wegen der damit verbundenen Mehrarbeit und dem größeren Bedarf an Heizmaterial war diese erste Backreihe nicht gerade beliebt. Etwa zur Mitte der 1950er Jahre war Schluss mit dieser altbewährten Methode. Nur einige wenige Familien nutzten noch das Backhaus und diese machten die Backreihen unter sich aus. Da mittlerweile auch der Backofen schadhaft geworden war, die notwendigen Reparaturmaßnahmen aber unterblieben, wurde der Backbetrieb bald gänzlich eingestellt. Erst als vier Jahrzehnte später die Offdillner Dorfgemeinschaft das Backhaus wieder renoviert hatte, begann wieder eine zögerliche Backhausbenutzung. Der Offdillner Backes ist der Mittelpunkt im Dorf und wird von den Ortsvereinen und privaten Gesellschaften zum Feiern genutzt. Auch das Brotbacken ist wieder aktuell und wird derzeit von einigen Familien durchgeführt.

properties.name: Old guard Haiger
properties.description:
The guardhouse was located in front of the then still standing city wall and was built in 1810 in the Greek temple style. It served the town guard as a guardroom and detention cell. Carters passing through had to pay "road and lake tolls" there. During this period Haiger belonged to the Duchy of Berg ("French period") and was effectively under Napoleon's rule. After Haiger became part of Nassau again, the small guardhouse lost its function and was put up for auction as early as 1817. After 1827, the town wall was also gradually dismantled.

Next to the watchtower was one of the public fountains, which gave its name to the inn opposite. Not far from the Wacht in Hickenweg is the site of the so-called "Wilhelmshof".

Hickenweg (also called Hofhausweg) used to be the main road to Langenaubach, to the Hickengrund and to the Westerwald.

The Westerwald road was not built until 1823/24.

properties.name: Backhaus Roth
properties.description:
The origins of today's Hessian bakehouses date back to the middle of the 16th century: Count Johann VI of Nassau-Dillenburg decreed in the "Wood and Forest Ordinance" of 18 January 1562: "In every village, several common baking ovens are to be decreed". On the one hand, communal baking was intended to save wood, as resources were slowly becoming scarce in the region due to the immense consumption of wood, for example for iron smelting. On the other hand, the fire risk for the farms, which were mostly built of wood, clay and straw, with their dwellings and stables, was reduced by a separate location of the now isolated bakehouses. As a result of this ordinance, numerous village community bakehouses were built. Due to the exchange of information - trade, marriage and itinerant trades - that went beyond the borders of the lordship, this advantageous model soon became popular throughout Hesse.

In the mid-19th century, communal bakehouse culture experienced a renaissance, starting in the then Prussian provinces in what are now Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse. In 1846/1847, crop failures caused great hardship throughout Europe, including in the Kingdom of Prussia, which included the small town of Weyerbusch in the Westerwald. When the government issued flour, mayor Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen - who is also considered the founding father of the cooperative system - initiated a "bread association". The allotted flour was processed in a specially built bakehouse. The bread baked here could be distributed to the needy population at a favourable price. Neighbouring villages throughout the Westerwald, the Lahn-Dill mountains, the Burgwald and the Schwalm soon took up the idea of the "baking house and baking house association". Today there are many bakehouses whose foundation stones were laid in the same era.

The art of baking good bread in a bakehouse has always required a great deal of experience and has been a community activity. It began with the selection and cutting of suitable wood, the nightly heating of the oven and the determination of the baking sequence. This was decided in advance by the baking community, often by lot. The bread dough itself was usually made individually in advance according to a home recipe and carried to the bakehouse. Not only the choice of flour, but also the temperature at which the loaves of bread were put into the oven with the pusher was decisive for good success. The time during which the bread remained in the oven was used for communicative exchange among the "Backesbäcker/innen" and was therefore important for village cohesion. This traditional village bakehouse system was an integral part of the local supply almost from the middle of the 19th century until the 20th century. Due to technical developments, many households have had their own electric ovens since the mid-1950s, so that communal baking in bakehouses has become less and less important. In the 1960s in particular, many bakehouses were demolished. To this day, however, there are still numerous bakehouses and bakehouse associations, often with a long, unbroken tradition that continues into the present day, which bake in the time-honoured manner and cultivate the village community. At present, communal baking is experiencing a rebirth in Hesse.

Text: Naturpark Lahn-Dill-Bergland

Eschenburg Roth Bakehouse

 Built in 1730, originally a two-storey half-timbered house. The lower floor was the bakehouse. The upper floor consisted of 2 rooms, schoolroom and town hall room. In 1857/58 the bakehouse had to make way for a new building. It is a one-and-a-half-storey stone-built house, doors and windows are framed in sandstone. On the lower floor was the baking room with 2 ovens. Next to the baking room was the fire brigade's fire engine house. In the attic room the congregation met and at the same time it was the meeting room of the congregation council. A small adjoining room served as a prison cell, with a barred window. In 1934, one of the ovens was bricked up and the other renovated. In 1952 there was a fire in the roof truss, after which the roof truss was demolished, the bakehouse was raised and 4 families of emergency flats were built.   In 1922, a baking order / sequence was established, which family was allowed to bake on which day of the week and for how long. The dates were drawn by lot and attached to the board with house numbers. This board still exists today and is displayed in the bakehouse.   Until the end of the 1970s, the bakehouse was regularly used by Rother families, after that it was used more sporadically, for example for club celebrations.    In 2005, the firing chamber was renovated and a new fireclay floor was installed.    As of 2016, the chimney in the Rother Backes is smoking regularly again, a group of Rother people has made it their task to preserve this old tradition. A dough machine and a proofer were purchased, clubs, groups and families are baking again, in 2020 about 400 loaves. Regular baking appointments are held for the people of Rother, where bread is baked to order. The expenses for maintaining the bakery are financed exclusively by the bread donations, so that the community does not incur any additional expenses.

properties.name: Kersen natuurpad
properties.description:
Der Kirschlehrpfad führt Sie durch die größte Ansammlung von Süßkirschen in Deutschland. Die insgesamt ca. 365 Bäume bilden dabei ein buntes Sammelsurium aus verschiedensten alten Sorten, alle mehr oder weniger stark vom Aussterben bedroht. Die z.T. letzten Bäume ihrer Sorte dienen als Quelle für sogenannte "Reiser": Triebe für die Veredelung neuer Bäume dieser Sorte. Die Aufgabe Hagens ist es, diese „Mutterbäume“ zu hegen und zu pflegen.




Um dem Pflegeanspruch gerecht zu werden, hat sich die Gemeinde Verstärkung in Form von Schafen geholt. Die Beweidung dient der Freihaltung der Bäume und wirkt sich als extensive Landschaftspflegemaßnahme positiv auf die gesamte Fläche aus.



Genießen Sie den entspannenden Blick auf Kirschen und Tiere. Beachten Sie dabei aber bitte, dass die Zäune in der Regel unter Strom stehen. Auch die im Frühjahr im Lehrpfad stehenden Bienen brauchen ihren Freiraum. Der Bereich ist deutlich gekennzeichnet.

Sie möchten gerne Deutschlands größte Kirschsorten-Sammlung erleben? Sie planen mit einer Gruppe eine schöne und zugleich informative Aktivität an der frischen Luft? Dann sind Sie herzlich eingeladen zu einem Streifzug durch die Welt der Hagener Süßkirschen. Buchen Sie eine Führung durch den Kirsch-Lehrpfad!

properties.name: Boomkroonpad Bad Iburg
properties.description:
Einzigartige und inspirierende Erlebnisse über den Wipfeln in Bad Iburg: Intensives Walderleben bietet der Baumwipfelpfad Bad Iburg auf fast 600 Metern Lauflänge. Als Teil des UNESCO Global Geopark TERRA.vita geben Pfad und dazugehöriger Ausstellungspavillon Einblicke in die Erdgeschichte des Teutoburger Waldes. Der barrierefrei Einstiegsturm mit über 30 Metern Höhe bietet einen fantastischen Rundblick auf das Iburger Schloss und den Teutoburger Wald!

Der Baumwipfelpfad ist jetzt Teil eines bundesweit einzigartigen digitalen Erlebnis-Parks. Mit Hilfe einer eigens programmierten App wird er zum Leben erweckt: Virtuelle Begegnungen mit den Tieren des Waldes, Pflanzen, Pilzen und Insekten – inspirierendes Wald-Wissen. Einzigartig und extrem spannend, das ist „Augmented Reality“ (AR). Dazu virtuelle Geschicklichkeits-, Wissens- und Bewegungsspiele – gemeinschaftliches Erleben von Natur und Umwelt ist Trumpf! Zusätzlich halten über 30 analoge Erlebnis- und Lernstationen attraktiv verpacktes Wissen zu Flora, Fauna, Geologie und Geschichte bereit.
